article_content: MPs have backed Enfield Council’s bid to ban spitting on the streets and make it a criminal offense. Communities and Local Government Secretary Eric Pickles agreed with the council that the practice is 'deeply anti-social.' Enfield applied for provisional approval to introduce a by-law prohibiting public spitting 'without reasonable excuse,' and has now received the go-ahead. Councillor Chris Bond, the council’s cabinet member for environment, said: 'This is a victory for the people of Enfield, who overwhelmingly supported a ban on spitting in this borough. It’s an awful and disgusting habit, and I’m delighted we can now move forward with banning this filthy practice. I hope other local authorities will follow suit.' 'Our campaign to end this practice has resonated across the United Kingdom, with several other councils contacting us to say they are considering similar bans,' he added. A one-month public consultation period will precede Mr. Pickles’ final decision. If approved, the by-law will take effect one month later. Mr. Pickles stated: 'Spitting is a deeply anti-social and unpleasant practice. It is not socially acceptable on Britain’s streets. Given the cross-party support from both ruling and opposition groups, we are granting Enfield Council new powers to address this localized issue.' Enforcement will be handled by magistrates’ courts. While Doncaster Council previously received provisional approval for a similar ban, Enfield will be the first London borough to implement such a by-law.

Enfield søkte om midlertidig godkjenning til å innføre en forskrift som forbyr spytting i offentlige rom 'uten rimelig grunn,' og har nå fått grønt lys. Rådmann for miljø, Councillor Chris Bond, sa: 'Dette er en seier for folkene i Enfield, som overveiende støttet et forbud mot spytting i dette området. Selv om Doncaster Råd tidligere fikk midlertidig godkjenning til et lignende forbud, vil Enfield være det første London-borgeriet som innfører en slik forskrift.

article_content: Six men have been arrested in connection with the gang rape of a 29-year-old woman in northern India — an attack that bears disturbing similarities to the December 2012 rape and murder of a student in New Delhi. On January 11, the woman was traveling by coach to her in-laws’ home in Punjab when she was allegedly abducted. Five accomplices joined the bus driver and conductor, who had taken her by motorcycle to a secluded area near Amritsar. There, all six men took turns raping her throughout the night. She was abandoned near her in-laws’ village the following morning, where she recounted the assault to her sisters-in-law. Local police confirmed the rape after a medical examination, though the full extent of her injuries remains under investigation. 'Six men have been arrested on suspicion of raping the woman after forcibly taking her to an unknown location on the night of January 11,' said police officer Raj Jeet Singh. He added that a seventh suspect is still at large. According to reports, the suspects — who had been drinking — hijacked a school bus for a joyride. Despite passing multiple police checkpoints, the vehicle was never stopped. The attackers allegedly beat the woman’s male companion and raped her inside the moving bus, before dumping her on the roadside. Local politician Partap Singh Bajwa criticized police for failing to enforce nighttime safety checks on buses. 'It all happened due to laxity,' he told AFP. The case has reignited nationwide protests demanding stronger protections for women and accountability from law enforcement, echoing demonstrations that followed the December attack in Delhi.

Den 11. januar var kvinnen på vei med buss til svigerfamiliens hjem i Punjab da hun ble kidnappet. Fem medgjerningspersoner slo seg sammen med sjåføren og konduktøren, som tok henne med motorsykkel til et avsidesliggende sted nær Amritsar. Han la til at en syvende mistenkt fremdeles er på friluft. Ifølge rapporter hadde mistenkte — som hadde drukket — tatt en skolebuss for en tur. Tross flere politikontroller passerte kjøretøyet uten å bli stoppet. Angriperene skal ha slått kvinnens mannlige ledsager og voldtekten henne inne i bussen, før de kastet henne på veikanten. Lokal politiker Partap Singh Bajwa kritiserte politiet for ikke å ha ivaretatt nattlige sikkerhetssjekker på buser. 'Alt skjedde på grunn av slapphet,' sa han til AFP. Saken har gjenopplivet landomfattende demonstrasjoner som krever sterkere beskyttelse for kvinner og ansvarlighet fra lovfuldhetsmyndighetene, og minner om demonstrasjoner etter angrepet i desember i Delhi.

article_content: During a hiking trip in May 2013, Jordan Liles, a resident of San Diego, California, made an extraordinary discovery in Tennessee’s Great Smoky Mountains National Park: an abandoned town long forgotten by time. The town, once known as the Wonderland Club, was constructed more than a century ago and has remained largely undisturbed since its decline after a 1925 flood. Liles captured a series of hauntingly beautiful photographs and an extended video of the site, offering a rare glimpse into a piece of American history hidden deep within the forest. He described the location on his blog as 'a mile up an unnamed gravel road' in the Elkmont section of the park. Although once a private resort for the elite, the Elkmont Historic District is now officially recognized by the National Park Service — and since Liles shared his images, the site has attracted increased attention from hikers and photographers.

Byen, som tidligere het Wonderland Club, ble bygget for mer enn hundre år siden og har blitt stort sett uforstyrret siden sin nedgang etter en oversvømmelse i 1925. Liles tok en rekke utrolig vakre bilder og et lengre videoklipp av stedet, og gir et sjelden innblikk i en del av amerikansk historie skjult dypt inne i skogen. Han beskrev lokasjonen på sin blogg som 'en mil opp en uoppfylt grusvei' i Elkmont-området i parken. Selv om det engang var et privat resort for eliten, er Elkmont Historic District nå offisielt anerkjent av National Park Service — og siden Liles delte sine bilder har stedet trukket økt oppmerksomhet fra vandrere og fotografere.

article_content: Maryland authorities plan to prosecute a man for allegedly urinating on the grave of former Baltimore Ravens owner Art Modell. The man, identified only as a Cleveland Browns fan, faces charges of disorderly conduct in a cemetery. He posted a video of the incident on YouTube this month, showing him urinating on the gravestone while wearing his Browns jersey. Baltimore County State's Attorney Scott Shellenberger confirmed the man will not be publicly named until formal charges are filed and served. If convicted, he could face up to two years in jail and a $500 fine. Art Modell, who died in 2012 at age 87, served as an NFL owner for 43 years—leading the Cleveland Browns from 1961 until relocating the franchise to Baltimore in 1996, where it became the Ravens. He and his wife, Patricia, are buried at Druid Ridge Cemetery in Baltimore. David Modell, Art’s son, told ESPN the family appreciates the police’s efforts and the decision to pursue charges. 'We also agree with the state’s attorney’s office that everyone who has buried a loved one has the right to know their final resting place will not be defiled,' he said. The offensive video has drawn widespread condemnation beyond the football community. Commenters such as DeMario Tucker called the act 'ignorant,' while Scott Eisen labeled Cleveland a 'classless, ungrateful sports town.' Shawn Rollins countered, 'Way to keep it classy. Respect everyone.'

article_content: On February 20, 2014, 27-year-old camera assistant Sarah Jones lost her life in a preventable tragedy on the set of the biographical film 'Midnight Rider'. Filming on an active railroad bridge in southeast Georgia — without official permission — the crew was caught off guard when a CSX freight train approached. Despite being warned they had about a minute to evacuate, a heavy metal bed prop, used in a dream sequence depicting Gregg Allman, remained on the tracks. The train struck the bed, which then pinned Jones against the rails. She died instantly. Six others were injured. Footage from a camera mounted inside the locomotive, later released by ABC’s 20/20, shows crew members sprinting across the trestle as the train barrels toward them. Actors William Hurt and Wyatt Russell can be seen fleeing alongside others, while some cover their ears against the deafening whistle. The train’s engineer sounded the horn 26 seconds before impact, but the crew couldn’t clear the tracks in time. Investigators confirmed CSX had explicitly denied the production’s request to film on the bridge. A letter to location manager Charley Baxter read: 'Unfortunately, CSX is not able to support your request.' Yet filming continued. Director Randall Miller and producer Jody Savin were later charged with involuntary manslaughter and trespassing — crimes carrying up to 10 years in prison. Gregg Allman, whose life story the film was based on, had no direct role in production decisions. His legal team confirmed he only licensed his memoir, 'My Cross to Bear', and had no involvement in safety planning. The Jones family, after reviewing evidence, formally dropped their claims against him — as well as against executive producer Michael Lehman and distributor Open Road Films. Joyce Gilliard, a hairstylist who sustained arm injuries, recalled the chaos: 'They told us we had 60 seconds to get off the track... then everything happened too fast.' She and others now say the crew was treated as expendable in pursuit of a single cinematic moment. The incident exposed deep flaws in film industry safety norms — especially around unregulated locations and inadequate risk assessments. No train schedules are publicly available for freight lines, making it nearly impossible for crews to predict movement. Production on 'Midnight Rider' stopped immediately after the crash. Legal proceedings continue, with the Jones family seeking accountability from Miller, Savin, CSX, and Rayonier.

article_content: On Easter Sunday, a man in his 50s was spotted calmly walking down a residential street in Much Wenlock, Shropshire, holding a handgun and smoking a cigarette. Witnesses reported he appeared completely unfazed as he moved through the snowy neighborhood. He reportedly attempted to force entry into a home believed to be the former residence of a serving police officer. Armed officers arrived within seconds and, after he raised the weapon toward them, fired a warning shot — which missed. A police dog was deployed and tackled the man, allowing officers to safely arrest him. He was taken into custody at Malinsgate Police Station in Telford and later detained under the Mental Health Act. Eyewitness Jane Shepherd, a mother of three, captured video of the incident. Her eight-year-old son, William, had been playing outside with friends when police shouted for children to seek shelter. 'I didn’t believe him at first — I thought it was an April Fools’ joke,' she said. 'Then I looked out and saw him — just standing there, holding a gun like it was nothing.' Shepherd, who moved to the area for its peace and quiet, described the event as unprecedented: 'Nothing like this has ever happened here. Everyone is in shock.' West Mercia Police confirmed that a round was fired by an armed officer but no one was injured. The handgun is currently undergoing forensic analysis to determine if it was operational. The case has been referred to the Independent Police Complaints Commission for review.

Han skal ha forsøkt å tvinge seg inn i et hus som antas å være det tidligere hjemmet til en aktuell politimann. Våpnede politibetjenter ankom innen få sekunder og avfyrte et advarselsskudd — som bommet — etter at han hevet våpenet mot dem. En politihund ble satt løs og kastet seg over mannen, noe som tillot politiet å arrestere ham trygt. Han ble tatt til fange ved Malinsgate politistasjon i Telford og senere holdt under psykisk helseloven. Vitne Jane Shepherd, mor til tre barn, filmet hendelsen. Hennes åtteårige sønn, William, hadde vært ute og spilt med venner da politiet skrek til barna om å søke ly. 'Jeg trodde ikke ham først — jeg tenkte det var en 1. april-funn,' sa hun. 'Da jeg så ut, så jeg ham — bare stående der, med et gevær som om det ikke betydde noe.' Shepherd, som flyttet til området for dets fred og ro, beskrev hendelsen som uten eksempel: 'Ingenting slik har noen gang skjedd her. Alle er i sjokk.' West Mercia Politiet bekreftet at et skudd ble avfyrt av en våpenforsvarer, men ingen ble skadd. Håndvåpenet blir foreløpig undersøkt av eksperter for å avgjøre om det var funksjonelt. Saken er sendt videre til Uavhengige politiklagenes kommisjon (IPCC) for gjennomgang.

article_content: Matt Stonie, a 21-year-old trainee dietitian and competitive eater from California, recently completed a personal challenge: consuming four oversized Chipotle burritos in just under three minutes. The meal, totaling roughly 3,700 calories, was filmed and uploaded to YouTube, where it has surpassed one million views. Each burrito was stuffed with white rice, black beans, sour cream, and salsa — two with chicken, two with steak. He washed them down with a large Diet Coke, at a total cost of $34.23 before tax and tip. In the video, titled '4 Chipotle Burritos & A Diet Coke,' Stonie, known by his nickname 'Megatoad,' used his hands to quickly shovel each wrap into his mouth after removing the foil wrapping. He finished the final bite at 2 minutes and 59 seconds, visibly exhausted, wiping his forehead and mouth. Viewers reacted with astonishment: 'My stomach hurts from just watching,' and 'I can barely finish one burrito.' Though his consumption seems at odds with his nutrition studies, Stonie maintains a rigorous exercise and diet routine outside of competitive eating. Ranked second in the world by Major League Eating, he holds multiple records, including devouring a 5.5-pound birthday cake in under nine minutes and 10.5 pounds of frozen yogurt in six minutes. This burrito feat was not a formal competition but part of his ongoing series of viral stunts — most recently, consuming 12 Cinnabon rolls (over 11,000 calories) in under ten minutes. 'I feel like hell,' he admitted afterward. His message remains clear: don’t try this at home.

article_content: Diego Costa was involved in a physical clash with Swansea midfielder Gylfi Sigurdsson during Chelsea’s match, sparking debate among fans over whether he deserved a red card. Graham Poll, writing for Sportsmail, offers his assessment. Poll describes Costa as a superb centre-forward whose physical, old-fashioned style resembles a traditional English target man. He emphasizes that Costa is far from a 'soft foreigner' and contends that his earlier yellow card for diving at Burnley was unjust. During the incident, Costa forcefully pushed away Sigurdsson after being held in the penalty area. While referee Kevin Friend could have issued a caution for this action, Poll sees no justification for a red card. In fact, the lack of a booking may have balanced out the earlier controversial caution at Turf Moor. Video footage showed Costa appearing to shove Sigurdsson to the ground as both players contested a free-kick. Despite the intensity, Poll maintains the challenge was within acceptable physical limits. On a separate note, Costa netted a hat-trick in the match, taking his goal tally for Chelsea to seven in just four appearances.

article_content: At least 51 people were killed and 121 injured in a bombing at a mosque in Ghondi village, Khyber Agency, Pakistan, according to local official Muthar Zab. The attack occurred during Friday prayers, when approximately 300 worshippers were present. In a separate incident on the same day, two Pakistani security officers were killed and six others wounded when gunmen opened fire on their convoy in the Aka Khel region of Khyber. In response, security forces conducted a search operation, killing 10 militants and injuring five, while destroying three militant hideouts. Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) claimed responsibility for the mosque bombing, stating it was retaliation for local villagers who had killed two Taliban fighters and destroyed three of their hideouts earlier in the week. Khalid Kundi, a senior official in Khyber, confirmed the bomber used between 8 and 10 kilograms of explosives and detonated himself in the mosque courtyard. One survivor, Hikmat Ullah Afridi, recalled the blast was so powerful it knocked him unconscious. When he regained consciousness, he saw dead and injured people scattered around him. Khyber Agency, formerly one of Pakistan’s federally administered tribal areas, is now administratively part of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The region, bordering Afghanistan, has experienced persistent violence over the past decade. CNN’s Shaan Khan contributed to this report.

I et separat tilfelle samme dag ble to pakistanske sikkerhetsfolk drept og seks andre skadet da skyttere åpnet ild mot en konvoi i Aka Khel-regionen i Khyber. I respons utførte sikkerhetsstyrkene en søkeoperasjon der de drepte ti militanter og såret fem, mens de ødela tre militante skjulesteder. Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) tok ansvar for bommengden på moskéen og sa det var hævn for lokale bygder som hadde drept to Taliban-krigere og ødelagt tre av deres skjulesteder tidligere i uken. Khalid Kundi, en høyere funksjonær i Khyber, bekreftet at bombemannen brukte mellom 8 og 10 kilo eksplosivt materiale og detonerte seg selv i moskéns hof. En overlevende, Hikmat Ullah Afridi, husket at eksplosjonen var så kraftig at den slo ham bevisstløs. Når han kom til seg, så han døde og skadede mennesker overalt. Regionen, som ligger ved grensen til Afghanistan, har opplevd vedvarende vold i flere tiår. CNNs Shaan Khan bidro til denne rapporten.

article_content: On Thursday evening, Robert Wayne Harris, 40, was executed by lethal injection in Texas for the 2000 murders of five people at the Mi-T-Fine Car Wash in Irving. He had been fired from the job just a week earlier — a trigger, according to prosecutors, for a meticulously planned attack. Harris, who had previously served eight years for burglary and other offenses, returned to the car wash armed and opened fire on employees, killing the manager, assistant manager, cashier, and two others. He was arrested the following day. Though Harris confessed to all five killings — and even guided police to the remains of Sandra Scott, a woman he abducted and killed months before the car wash massacre — he was only formally tried for two of the murders: those of Agustin Villasenor and Rhoda Wheeler. His defense team argued he suffered from intellectual disabilities, making him ineligible for execution under Supreme Court precedent, and claimed Black jurors were systematically excluded from his trial. Both arguments were rejected by courts and prosecutors, who cited IQ testing and denied racial bias in jury selection. In his final moments, Harris spoke calmly to his brother and three friends watching through the glass: 'I'm going home. Don't worry about me. I'll be alright. God bless, and the Texas Rangers, Texas Rangers.' He was pronounced dead at 6:43 p.m., becoming the eighth person executed in Texas that year — the state with the highest execution rate in the U.S. His brother left the chamber before the procedure ended. Relatives of the victims watched from another room; two embraced after his death but declined to speak to the press. Court records revealed Harris had a long history of violent behavior in prison, including arson, threats against staff, drug dealing, and sexual misconduct. Yet his attorneys maintained he never received a fair hearing on whether his cognitive impairments warranted life imprisonment instead of death. As Texas prepares for another execution next week, the case continues to fuel debate over justice, mental health, and race in the American penal system.

Harris, som tidligere hadde sittet i åtte år for innbrudd og andre forbrytelser, returnerte til bilvasken med våpen og åpnet ild mot ansatte, drepte sjefen, assistenten, kassereren og to andre. Han ble arrestert dagen etter. Selv om Harris innrømmet alle fem mordene – og selv førte politiet til restene av Sandra Scott, en kvinne han hadde kidnappet og drept måneder før bilvask-massakren – ble han bare formelt dømt for to av mordene: de på Agustin Villasenor og Rhoda Wheeler. Forsvarerne argumenterte for at han lider av intellektuelle vansker, noe som gjør ham udektlig for dødsstraff ifølge Høyesterettens prinsipper, og hevdet at svarte potensielle jurer ble systematisk ekskludert fra rettssaken. Begge argumentene ble avvist av domstolene og tiltalende, som pekte på IQ-tester og nektet rasebasert diskriminering i juryutvelgelsen. Han ble erklært død kl. 18:43, og ble den åttende personen som ble henrettet i Texas dette året – staten med høyest antall henrettelser i USA. Bror hans forlot kammeret før prosedyren var fullført. Pårørende til ofrene så fra et annet rom; to omfavnet hverandre etter at han var død, men nektet å snakke med journalistene. Men advokatene hans hevdet at han aldri fikk en rettferdig høring på om hans kognitive vansker burde ha ført til livsvarig fengsel istedenfor dødsstraff. Mens Texas forbereder seg på en ny henrettelse neste uke, fortsetter saken å føre til debatt om rettferdighet, psykisk helse og rasisme i det amerikanske strafferetten-systemet.

article_content: A Colorado pastor has criticized Disney's Frozen, calling it a tool for indoctrinating children into homosexuality. Pastor Kevin Swanson made the remarks during a segment on his radio show on Wednesday, suggesting that the Devil may have influenced Disney’s corporate direction since the 1980s to turn American families away from traditional values. Swanson condemned Disney for ending its partnership with the Boy Scouts of America, citing the Scouts’ previous stance against gay leaders as a reason for the split. He claimed the move was part of a broader effort to undermine Christian families. 'Friends, this is evil — just evil,' Swanson said. 'I wonder if people realize that this cute little movie might lead their five-year-old to accept homosexuality—or even bestiality—as normal.' Though he offered no specific scenes or dialogue from Frozen to support his claims, Swanson labeled Disney as 'one of the most pro-homosexual organizations in the country' and speculated that Satan himself might be directing its policies. He referenced the 1984 attempt by corporate raider Saul Steinberg to take over Disney, implying that this moment marked a turning point in the company’s values. 'If I were the Devil,' he asked rhetorically, 'what would I do to really corrupt an entire social system and harm 5-, 6-, and 7-year-olds in Christian homes? I’d buy Disney in 1984.' Swanson also described Frozen’s storyline — centered on a misunderstood princess learning self-acceptance — as a metaphor for gay 'coming out,' despite no such intent being stated by the filmmakers.

article_content: Last Sunday, thousands of domestic workers flooded the streets of Hong Kong’s Wanchai district, demanding justice for Erwiana Sulistyaningsih — a 22-year-old Indonesian woman who survived eight months of horrific abuse while working as a housemaid. After being left unable to walk and suffering severe internal injuries, she was flown back to Indonesia and hospitalized in critical condition. Her story, shared with Al Jazeera from her hospital bed in Sragen, revealed a nightmare: forced to sleep on the floor, fed only one bowl of rice daily, and beaten relentlessly — often with the handle of her own mop — for minor mistakes or even no reason at all. Her wounds festered for months; when blood and pus leaked onto the carpet, her employer simply wrapped her in plastic bags instead of seeking medical help. Eventually, when Erwiana could no longer work, her employer bought her a cheap plane ticket home, gave her just HK$70, and threatened to kill her parents if she ever spoke out. Her ordeal is not isolated. Another Indonesian helper, known only as Bunga, came forward describing nearly identical abuse during her time working for the same family in 2010 — including being dragged to a balcony and threatened with being thrown off, forced to beg for her life, and warned that her family would be killed if she told anyone. Both women were locked indoors for months, forbidden from leaving the apartment, and subjected to constant psychological terror. The protest, organized by migrant workers and human rights advocates, drew an estimated 5,000 people — a dramatic surge from earlier demonstrations. Marchers carried Indonesian flags and signs reading 'Justice for Erwiana,' delivering a petition to Hong Kong’s police commissioner calling for urgent action. Officials had originally classified the case as 'miscellaneous,' but public outcry forced a criminal investigation. Investigators are now planning to travel to Indonesia to interview Erwiana directly. Human rights groups like Amnesty International have long condemned Hong Kong’s treatment of foreign domestic workers, highlighting how recruitment agencies exploit vulnerable women by seizing passports, charging exorbitant fees, and making false promises about pay and conditions. Despite nearly 300,000 domestic helpers living and working in the city — mostly from Indonesia and the Philippines — protections remain weak. Last year, a Hong Kong couple was sentenced to prison for torturing a maid with an iron and a bike chain, but such convictions remain rare. Erwiana’s doctors say she suffers from brain swelling due to repeated head trauma, cellulitis in her limbs, broken teeth, and a fractured nose. 'I thought Hong Kong was a luxurious place,' she said. 'But it became my prison.' Her courage has ignited a movement. Two more women have since stepped forward with similar stories. As Eni Lestari of the International Migrants Alliance put it: 'Without protests like this, there will be no justice.'
translated_content: Søndag siste trakk tusenvis av husarbeidere gatene i Wanchai i Hongkong for å kreve rettferdighet for Erwiana Sulistyaningsih — en 22 år gammel indonesisk kvinne som overlevde åtte måneder med skremmende mishandling mens hun arbeidet som husjomfru. Etter å ha blitt udekkelig og opplevd alvorlige indre skader, ble hun flyttet tilbake til Indonesia og innlagt i kritisk tilstand. Hun delte sin historie med Al Jazeera fra sykehusbettet sitt i Sragen, og avslørte et mareritt: tvunget til å sove på gulvet, spist bare én bolle ris hver dag, og slått uten opphør — ofte med håndtaket på egen tretts — for små feil eller ingen grunn overhodet. Vundene hennes utviklet seg til infeksjoner; da blod og pus lekket ut på teppet, viklet arbeidsgiveren henne i plastposer istedenfor å søke medisinsk hjelp. Til slutt, da Erwiana ikke lenger kunne jobbe, kjøpte arbeidsgiveren henne en billige flybillett hjem, ga henne akkurat HK$70 og truet med å drepe foreldrene hennes hvis hun noen gang talte om det. Hennes skjebne er ikke isolert. En annen indonesisk hjelper, kjent bare som Bunga, kom frem med nesten identiske misbruk under sin tid hos samme familie i 2010 — inkludert å bli dratt ut på balkongen og truet med å bli kastet av, tvunget til å be om livet sitt, og advart om at familien hennes ville bli drept hvis hun fortalte noen. Begge kvinnene var låst inne i måneder, forbudt å forlate leiligheten, og utsatt for konstant psykologisk terror. Demonstrasjonen, organisert av migranter og menneskerettighetsaktivister, trakk en anslått 5.000 personer — en dramatisk økning fra tidligere protester. Demonstranter bærer indonesiske flagg og plakater med ordene 'Rettferdighet for Erwiana', og leverte en petisjon til politichefen i Hongkong for å kreve hurtig handling. Myndighetene hadde opprinnelig klassifisert saken som 'diverse', men offentlig opprør tvang en straffesak. Etterforskere planlegger nå å reise til Indonesia for å snakke med Erwiana direkte. Menneskerettighetsorganisasjoner som Amnesty International har lenge fordømt behandlingen av utenlandske husarbeidere i Hongkong, og understreket hvordan rekrutteringsbyråer utnytter sårbare kvinner ved å konfiskere pass, kreve ekstreme gebyrer og gi falske løfter om lønn og arbeidsforhold. Tross nær 300.000 husarbeidere som bor og jobber i byen — hovedsakelig fra Indonesia og Filippinene — er beskyttelsen svak. Forrige år ble et hongkongsk par dømt til fengsel for å mishandle en husjomfru med et jern og en sykkelkjede, men slike dommer er sjeldne. Erwiana sine leger sier hun lider av hjerneødem på grunn av gjentatte hodetreff, cellulitt i lemmer, brudd i tenner og en brutt nese. 'Jeg trodde Hongkong var et luksuriøst sted,' sa hun. 'Men det ble min fangehytte.' Hennes mod har antent en bevegelse. To flere kvinner har siden kommet frem med lignende historier. Som Eni Lestari fra International Migrants Alliance sa: 'Uten slike protester vil det ikke bli noe rettferdighet.'

article_content: By Ray Massey. PUBLISHED: 08:29 EST, 12 February 2014. | UPDATED: 11:26 EST, 12 February 2014. If you're California dreaming and have a spare £153,000 to spare, the new Ferrari California T might be just the ticket to banish Britain's rain-soaked winter blues. Set to arrive in the UK from September, the 200mph Ferrari California T will make its global debut at next month's Geneva Motor Show. By then, hopefully, the deluge will have passed—allowing drivers to enjoy the sun with the roof down and wind in their hair. Elegance, sportiness, and technology define the Ferrari California T, unveiled at the Geneva Motor Show. Its new V8 engine delivers an intense sound and vivid acceleration across the rev range—the first time such performance has been achieved with a turbocharged engine. You may not even feel the need to play the Beach Boys, Eagles, or Mamas & Papas on the infotainment system. Ferrari suggests you’ll be too captivated by the roar of its finely tuned engine and exhaust. Powered by a mighty 3.8-litre twin-turbocharged V8 engine producing 560 horsepower—equivalent to nearly six Ford Fiestas—it accelerates from 0 to 62 mph in just 3.6 seconds. Ferrari claims the retractable hardtop transforms the car from a chic coupe into a sleek, sophisticated spider in just 14 seconds. Available in two launch colors: an intensely deep red called Rosso California, inspired by classic Ferraris of yesteryear, and an elegant Blu California. A Ferrari spokesperson said: 'The Ferrari California T epitomises elegance, sportiness, versatility, and exclusivity—characteristics that have defined every California model since the 1950s.' Engineers at Ferrari’s Maranello headquarters developed an entirely new engine that delivers exceptional performance, blistering acceleration, and what the company calls 'the most exhilarating soundtrack any turbo engine has ever produced.' Inside, driver and passengers are enveloped in luxurious Frau semi-aniline leather trim. With the engine mounted up front, the car promises ultra-sharp and instantaneous throttle response. Technologies refined in Ferrari’s F1 cars have been adapted to improve performance and efficiency in the California T. Despite adding 70 horsepower and a 49% increase in torque, fuel efficiency has improved by around 25%, reaching 27 mpg. CO2 emissions have dropped by 8% to 250 g/km. The retractable hardtop enables seamless transition from coupe to open-top sports car in 14 seconds. The California T features the latest evolution of the F1-Trac traction control system for maximum corner exit acceleration. Equally powerful brakes are essential—and the carbon-ceramic braking system brings the car to a stop from 62 mph in just 34 metres. The car’s sleek proportions were designed by the Ferrari Styling Centre in collaboration with Italian design house Pininfarina. A spokesperson noted: 'The shape of the California T’s flanks draws inspiration from the iconic pontoon fenders of the 250 Testa Rossa. The front wing line flows back toward the compact, muscular rear, creating aerodynamic sleekness and motion.' The interior offers flexible storage: even with the roof down, owners can maximize boot capacity thanks to an opening between the luggage compartment and rear seats. The steering wheel includes integrated controls. Centrally mounted between two air vents is a 'Turbo Performance Engineer' interface—a touch-sensitive display allowing drivers to scroll through real-time engine performance data. The California T replaces the previous model, which has been in production since October 2008.

article_content: A few years ago, Glyzelle Palomar was begging for food on the streets of northern Manila. This week, the 12-year-old girl stood on a stage in front of tens of thousands of people and asked Pope Francis why God allows children to suffer. 'There are many children neglected by their own parents,' Glyzelle said Sunday at a ceremony at a 400-year-old Catholic university in Manila. 'Many have become victims of terrible things—drugs, prostitution, abuse.' 'Why is God allowing this to happen, even though it's not the children's fault?' she asked, breaking down in tears. Another former street child, Jun Chura, 14, told the Pope about his struggle to survive without a home. 'I fed myself with whatever I could find in the trash. I didn’t know where to go—I slept on the sidewalk.' 'On the streets, I witnessed things I never wanted to see: my friends were taught to steal, even to kill—and they lost all respect for adults,' he said. Pope Francis responded by embracing both children. 'She is the only one who asked a question with no answer—and she couldn’t even speak it in words, only in tears,' the 78-year-old Pope told the crowd. Glyzelle and Jun are now cared for by the Tulay ng Kabataan Foundation, a nonprofit supporting Manila’s street children. According to Alexandra Chapeleau, the foundation’s communications manager, the girls had left home because their impoverished parents couldn’t support or educate them. They first visited a drop-in center before moving into a residential facility and beginning school. In November, their younger brother joined them. Glyzelle still maintains contact with her mother and visits her at Christmas, Chapeleau said. The residential center where Glyzelle lives houses about 40 other former street children. 'Most of them are survivors of the horrors that happen on the streets—including physical and sexual abuse,' Chapeleau noted. Yet Glyzelle’s tears were not rooted in her own trauma. 'She asked the question on behalf of all the children we care for—not because of something personal in her own story,' Chapeleau clarified. Later Sunday, Pope Francis celebrated Mass in a Manila park with millions present, despite heavy rain. 'We must see every child as a gift to be welcomed, cherished, and protected,' he said. 'We must care for our young—not allow them to be condemned to life on the streets.' The Pope had visited the foundation’s center on Friday and reportedly said he was 'very moved' by what he saw. According to the He Cares Foundation, there are an estimated 1.5 million street children in the Philippines, roughly 70,000 in Metro Manila. Jun described watching friends sniff glue and use other drugs. He learned to distrust adults offering help—it was often a trap to exploit children. He initially refused help from Tulay ng Kabataan but later realized, 'Not everyone has no heart.' Pope Francis departed the Philippines on Monday after concluding a historic Asia trip that included Sri Lanka. During his first papal visit to the predominantly Catholic Philippines in 20 years, he traveled to Tacloban—the city devastated by Super Typhoon Haiyan in 2013. Though forced to shorten his stay due to an approaching typhoon, he still celebrated Mass in Tacloban on Saturday for hundreds of thousands gathered in stormy weather, wearing a raincoat.
translated_content: For noen år siden ba Glyzelle Palomar om mat på gatene i nordlige Manila. Denne uken stod den 12-årige jenta på en scene foran titusenvis av mennesker og spurte pave Frans hvorfor Gud lar barn lider. 'Det er mange barn som blir neglisjert av sine egne foreldre,' sa Glyzelle søndag ved en seremoni på et 400 år gammelt katolsk universitet i Manila. 'Mange har blitt ofre for veldig onde ting—narkotika, prostitusjon, vold.' 'Hvorfor lar Gud dette skje, selv om det ikke er barnas skyld?' spurte hun og brøt sammen i tårer. En annen tidligere gatebarn, Jun Chura, 14, fortalte pave Frans om kampen sin for å overleve uten et hjem. 'Jeg matet meg med alt jeg kunne finne i søpla. Jeg visste ikke hvor jeg skulle gå—jeg sov på gata.' 'På gata så jeg ting jeg aldri ønsket å se: vennene mine ble lært å stjele, ja selv å drepe—og de mistet all respekt for voksne,' sa han. Pave Frans svarte ved å omfavne begge barna. 'Hun er den eneste som stilte et spørsmål som ikke har noe svar—og hun klarte ikke engang å uttrykke det med ord, bare med tårer,' sa den 78-årige paven til folkemengden. Glyzelle og Jun blir nå omsorgsfullt tatt vare på av Tulay ng Kabataan-stiftelsen, en frivillig organisasjon som støtter gatebarn i Manila. Ifølge Alexandra Chapeleau, kommunikasjonsleder i stiftelsen, hadde jentene forlatt hjemmet fordi deres fattige foreldre ikke kunne støtte eller gi dem utdanning. De besøkte først et drop-in-senter før de flyttet inn i en boligfacilitet og begynte på skolen. I november slo den yngre broren seg til dem i stiftelsen. Glyzelle har fortsatt kontakt med moren sin og besøker henne til jul, sa Chapeleau. Boligsentret der Glyzelle bor har omtrent 40 andre tidligere gatebarn. 'De fleste av dem er overlevende av skrekkene som skjer på gata—inkludert fysisk og seksuell vold,' sa Chapeleau. Men Glyzelles tårer var ikke forårsaket av egen traume. 'Hun stilte spørsmålet på vegne av alle barna vi omsorger—ikke på grunn av noe personlig i sin egen historie,' klargjorde Chapeleau. Senere søndag feiret pave Frans Messe i et Manila-park med millioner til stede, trots kraftig regn. 'Vi må se hvert barn som en gave som skal velkomnes, verdsettes og beskyttes,' sa han. 'Vi må ta vare på våre unge—ikke la dem bli dømt til et liv på gata.' Paven hadde besøkt stiftelsens sentrum fredag og skal ha sagt at han var 'veldig rørt' av hva han så. Ifølge He Cares Foundation er det anslått 1,5 millioner gatebarn i Filippinene, omtrent 70 000 i Metro Manila. Jun beskrev hvordan han så vennene sine snuse lim og bruke andre narkotika. Han lærte å mistro voksne som tilbød hjelp—det var ofte en felle for å utnytte barna. Han avviste opprinnelig hjelp fra Tulay ng Kabataan, men oppdaget senere: 'Ikke alle har ingen hjerte.' Pave Frans forlot Filippinene mandag etter en historisk Asia-reise som også inkluderte Sri Lanka. Under hans første pavebesøk til de dominerende katolske Filippinene på 20 år, reiste han til Tacloban—byen ødelagt av supertyfonen Haiyan i 2013. Selv om han måtte forkorte oppholdet på grunn av en ny tyfon, feiret han likevel Messe i Tacloban lørdag for hundretusener som samlet seg i stormveit vær, med en regnjakke på.

article_content: Seven adorable panda cubs, all born within a three-month span at the Chengdu Panda Base in Sichuan, China, have been unveiled together for the first time following medical evaluations. The cubs — born between July and September 2012 — now make up the largest group of artificially bred giant pandas in the world, bringing the center’s total population to 113. One cub, named Oreo, was born on the opening day of the London Olympics. Weighing just six ounces at birth, he has since grown to a stone (14 pounds) and is being prepared for eventual release into the wild — a rare and significant milestone in panda conservation. Other cubs are named Xiao Qiao, Si Yi, Yuan Run, Miao Miao, and twin siblings Cheng Shuang and Cheng Dui. Their births have sparked joy among conservationists and visitors alike, with the center reporting record-breaking reproductive success in 2012. Aimee Cheung, a participant in the global Pambassador competition from London, expressed personal connection to Oreo: 'He was born on the opening day of the London Olympics, and experts believe he has strong potential for rewilding.' Dr. Zhang Zhihe, director of the Chengdu Panda Base, stated, 'The remarkable number of cubs born this year is a testament to the effectiveness of our breeding program.' Three winners of the Pambassador competition will receive a five-month international conservation tour, working alongside experts in 11 countries committed to panda preservation.
translated_content: Syv veldig søte pandaunger, alle født innen et tidsrom på tre måneder ved Chengdu Panda-basen i Sichuan, Kina, har blitt vist frem sammen for første gang etter medisinske sjekker. Ungene — født mellom juli og september 2012 — utgjør nå den største gruppen av kunstig avlsette store pandaer i verden og øker basens totale populasjon til 113. En av ungene, kalt Oreo, ble født på åpningssdagen for Sommer-OL i London. Ved fødselen veide han bare seks unser, men har nå vokst til en sten (14 pund) og forberedes til frigivelse i viltet — en sjelden og betydelig milepæl i pandakonservasjon. De andre ungene heter Xiao Qiao, Si Yi, Yuan Run, Miao Miao og tvillingene Cheng Shuang og Cheng Dui. Deres fødsler har skapt glede blant konservatorer og besøkende, og basen rapporterer rekordhøye suksessrater i 2012. Aimee Cheung, en deltaker i det globale Pambassador-konkurransen fra London, uttrykte personlig tilknytning til Oreo: 'Han ble født på åpningssdagen for Sommer-OL i London, og eksperter tror han har stort potensiale for tilbakeføring til viltet.' Dr. Zhang Zhihe, leder for Chengdu Panda-basen, sa: 'Den bemerkelsesverdige mengden unger som ble født dette året er et bevis på effektiviteten i vårt avlprogram.' Tre vinnere av Pambassador-konkurransen vil få en femmåneders internasjonal konservasjonsreise, der de samarbeider med eksperter i 11 land som arbeider for pandakonservasjon.

article_content: Just days before Britain honors its war heroes on Remembrance Sunday, a metal plaque bearing the names of fallen soldiers from the Second World War was stolen from the Brentwood War Memorial in Essex. The shocking theft has deeply upset local residents and veterans. John Woolmore, 74, chairman of the Brentwood branch of the Royal British Legion, described the act as causing 'immeasurable sentimental damage' to families of the deceased. His own father, Francis Joseph Woolmore, who died in 1944 while serving in WWII, is honored on one of the seven remaining plaques. Woolmore expressed disbelief that anyone would steal a tribute to those who gave their lives — all for a few pounds in scrap metal. 'This is all our fallen heroes have to be remembered by,' he said. The incident comes less than eight months after vandals destroyed a memorial in neighboring Warley, Essex, honoring soldiers who died in Afghanistan. Brentwood Borough Council is racing to replace the stolen plaque before the Remembrance Day parade on November 11. Councillor Louise McKinlay condemned the theft as 'callous' and pledged to secure the remaining plaques. She urged the public to come forward with any information. Councillor Russell Quirk called the act 'absolutely disgusting,' questioning what could drive someone to desecrate a war memorial for just £30. Essex Police believe the plaque was removed between October 18 and 26, though the theft wasn't reported until October 30. The memorial contains 16 plaques commemorating service members from both World Wars. Authorities are appealing for witnesses or tips via Brentwood police on 101.

Den skremmende tyverien har dypt rammet lokale innbyggere og veteraner. John Woolmore, 74, nestleder i Brentwood-avdelingen av Det britiske krigsfellesskapet, beskrev handlingen som å forårsake 'uberegnelig følelsesmessig skade' for familiene til de døde. Hans egen far, Francis Joseph Woolmore, som døde i 1944 mens han tjenestegjorde i andre verdenskrig, er hedret på en av de syv gjenværende platene. Woolmore uttrykte forundring over at noen kunne stjele en hyllest til dem som ga livet sitt — bare for noen pund i skrapmetall. 'Dette er alt våre falede helter har for å bli husket,' sa han. Hendelsen skjedde mindre enn åtte måneder etter at vandalene ødela et minne i nabobyen Warley, Essex, som hedret ni soldater fra Royal Anglian Regiment som døde i Afghanistan for fem år siden. Brentwood Borough Council jakter på å erstatte den stjålne plata før Minnedagsparaden den 11. november. Essex Politi tror plata ble fjernet mellom 18. og 26. oktober, selv om tyveriet ikke ble rapportert før 30. oktober. Minnet inneholder 16 plater som hedrer tjenestemenn fra begge verdenskrigene. Myndighetene ber om vitner eller tipser via Brentwood politi på 101.

article_content:
Newcomers to the roads of Australia’s Northern Territory might be startled to find themselves overtaking a car with the plate BIGNOSE, tailgating YOLO, or feeling overshadowed by ADONIS. In the NT, vehicles don’t just transport people—they express personalities. One woman, Vivien Joseph, was so captivated by this phenomenon that she documented nearly 10,000 personalized license plates and published a book showcasing the most memorable ones. 

Number Plate Stories of the NT was launched in Darwin on Wednesday by Joseph, an Irish-born resident who moved to the Top End in 2011 after losing her job—and immediately began photographing plates. 

‘It was the first thing that caught my attention. It’s one of the most loveable things about the NT,’ Joseph says. 

Personalized plates in the Northern Territory cost just $178 AUD, a fraction of the $500 or more charged in other Australian states. Joseph believes affordability, combined with the region’s famously quirky and non-conformist spirit, fuels their popularity. 

Many plates are deeply personal: the Butt family, for instance, proudly displays HEDBUTT (dad), MYBUTT (mom), and simply BUTT (their son). Others nod to pop culture—like LIFE 42, a reference to The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy—or ASUWISH, inspired by The Princess Bride. 

Local businesses have embraced the trend too: SMILEDR (dentist), HITMAN (pest control), and POOGURU (plumber) turn plates into mobile ads. Even the NT Police have joined in with WATCHNU. 

Then there are the playful, the bold, and the absurd: REDBALL (a ute sporting red plastic testicles), TICKLED (a pink Hyundai), and PUNKROK (a red Suzuki Jeep adorned with a Team Edward Twilight sticker). Drivers are exhorted to COPTHAT, CRANKIT, or JAMIT—or charmed by FULISIK and BOGAN. 

One plate, BADNANA, was gifted by grandchildren to a woman who smuggled alcohol into an Elton John concert. Others reveal quiet resignation (YESDARL) or caffeine addiction (CAFIEND). 

For many, deciphering these plates has become a beloved pastime during long drives. ‘Is it that moving here makes you bolder? More creative? I don’t know,’ Joseph says, signing off with her own plate: PL8LADY.

article_content: Fernando Torres has returned home—to Atlético Madrid. On loan from AC Milan until the end of the season, the 30-year-old striker made a spirited second debut in the Copa del Rey last-16 first leg against bitter rivals Real Madrid. Atlético won 2-0 at the Vicente Calderón, and Torres, whose first spell at the club saw him score 91 goals in 244 appearances between 2001 and 2007, gave everything on the pitch. From the fifth minute, Torres was active—trying a delicate lob over Keylor Navas after being correctly flagged offside, then battling through tackles and pressing relentlessly. He committed several fouls, often due to overeagerness, and was repeatedly caught offside, including one instance where he jogged toward the ball as the linesman delayed raising his flag. Despite the frequent offside calls, Torres showed flashes of his old self: strong holds on defenders, smart positioning, and a powerful header to clear a James Rodríguez corner. He linked well with Antoine Griezmann, setting up a chance and earning praise for his physicality in the 56th minute, which led to a key attacking move. At the 59th minute, he was substituted to a standing ovation and a warm pat on the back from manager Diego Simeone. Though he didn’t score, his effort was undeniable. Fans waved scarves bearing his name and number 19, many showing him kissing the club badge. After the match, Torres said: 'There was plenty to celebrate. The atmosphere was electric, and so was our performance—but we know a 2-0 lead isn’t enough. We’ll need to be just as good at the Bernabéu to close it out.' It was his first-ever victory over Real Madrid while wearing an Atlético shirt—a moment rich with symbolism for a player who helped define the club’s golden era.

article_content: (CNN) — Desperation and a rapidly rising death toll underscore a new international effort by dozens of countries aiming to halt the brutal crackdown in Syria. On Friday, world leaders convened in Tunisia for a meeting of the 'Friends of Syria' group, seeking to increase pressure on Syrian President Bashar al-Assad. 'This is part of our ongoing collaboration with allies, partners, and the Syrian opposition to define next steps to stop the killing of Syrian civilians and advance a transition to democracy,' said U.S. State Department spokeswoman Victoria Nuland. More than 70 nations were invited. Russia, which recently vetoed a UN Security Council resolution targeting the violence, did not attend. Saudi King Abdullah urged Russian President Dmitry Medvedev in a phone call that dialogue with Assad would fail, according to the official Saudi Press Agency (SPA). Lebanon also declined to participate, as confirmed by its official news agency NNA. China, which also vetoed the UN resolution, has not yet confirmed its attendance. 'If China accepts the invitation, it would signal a positive step toward collective action to end the violence,' Nuland added. The choice of Tunisia as the meeting site is symbolic — it was there that the Arab Spring uprisings began a year earlier. 'The failure to pass a UN Security Council resolution lies with two countries,' said State Department spokesman Mark Toner. 'The international community remains largely united in supporting the Syrian people. The challenge now is determining our next actions.' Immediate priorities include delivering humanitarian aid, securing ceasefires, and compelling the Syrian regime to halt its assault on Homs. According to the opposition-linked Local Coordination Committees of Syria (LCC), the death toll has approached 9,000. On Thursday, two more deaths were reported: an army recruit shot for refusing to fire on protesters in Zabadany, and an 8-year-old boy from Aleppo. Wednesday saw 60 fatalities, including two journalists — one American, one French. Among them were 20 in Homs’ Baba Amr district, 13 in Hama, 22 in Idlib, one in Daraa, two in Aleppo, and two in Damascus suburbs. The deaths underscore the peril faced by journalists. Verified YouTube videos showed hundreds of students at Aleppo University marching to Clock Square, removing the Baath Party flag, and raising the pro-democracy 'independence flag' — originally used before Hafez al-Assad seized power in 1971. Shortly after, security forces and pro-regime militias opened fire, according to activists. Protests in Aleppo are particularly significant because the city, along with parts of Damascus, represents the upper-middle class — traditionally loyal to the Assad regime. In Damascus, security forces blocked access points and arrested over 800 civilians at the Hal Market. They later targeted shopkeepers and laborers from Daraa and Idlib provinces. Approximately 500 soldiers from the Syrian army’s 17th Regiment defected and formed a brigade within the Free Syrian Army in Idlib, according to opposition leader Mohamad al-Sayed. Much of the worst violence occurred in besieged Homs, where residents have been cut off from food, water, and medicine for weeks. UN officials say verifying the death toll is nearly impossible under current conditions. 'This level of brutality is something I’ve never witnessed in my life,' said activist Wissam Tarif, based in Beirut and in contact with Syrians inside the country. He emphasized the urgent need for ambulances to reach affected zones, especially Baba Amr, where the wounded are being denied medical care. The two Western journalists were killed in Homs during intense government shelling. The Sunday Times of London identified one as Marie Colvin, the only British newspaper journalist embedded in Baba Amr. French Foreign Minister Alain Juppe confirmed journalist Remi Ochlik died in a bombing. Syrian state television claimed the Ministry of Information had no record of the journalists’ presence and asked local authorities to locate them. The Syrian regime severely restricts foreign media access, making independent verification difficult. Yet some journalists have entered Syria covertly. The night before her death, Colvin spoke live with CNN: 'The Syrian army is shelling a city of cold, starving civilians.' A veteran war correspondent who also covered Libya, Colvin called the Syrian conflict the worst she’d ever reported, citing the sheer volume of artillery and sniper fire. 'You can spot snipers on rooftops, but you can’t predict where shells will land,' she said. Her death followed that of New York Times reporter Anthony Shadid, who died in eastern Syria last week from an asthma attack. Syria routinely attributes violence to 'armed terrorist groups.' State media SANA reported that 'competent authorities' killed three such individuals on Monday and arrested five in Idlib. Another report claimed an engineer was assassinated and his 16-year-old son wounded in Hama. Five military and police personnel were buried Wednesday, per SANA. However, the overwhelming majority of on-the-ground accounts indicate the Assad regime is systematically targeting civilians to crush dissent demanding his removal and democratic reform. Hours before her death, Colvin described the anguish of watching a young boy die from shrapnel wounds — one of many children killed. 'That little baby is one of two children who died today,' she said. 'His story, his image — they might make people ask: What is happening here? Why isn’t anyone stopping this daily massacre in Homs?' CNN contributors Hamdi Alkhshali, Arwa Damon, Holly Yan, Josh Levs, Joe Sterling, Yousuf Basil, and Tom Cohen contributed to this report.

article_content: In a harrowing incident in the remote Aboriginal community of Warburton, Western Australia, a 36-year-old man set himself ablaze after being tased by police — while drenched in gasoline. According to Inspector Bill Munnee of the West Australian Police, the man had been reported for glue-sniffing and emerged from his home holding a container of petrol and a cigarette lighter. When officers approached, he refused to comply with commands to halt. One officer deployed a Taser in an attempt to subdue him. Moments later, the man burst into flames. It remains unclear whether the ignition came from the lighter or the electrical spark emitted by the Taser device. As the officer rushed to extinguish the fire, a woman inside the residence began hurling rocks at him, causing lacerations alongside the burns he sustained. The man was urgently flown by air ambulance to a hospital in Perth, where he is receiving intensive care for life-threatening burns. He now faces charges of assaulting an officer with intent to evade arrest and possessing a dangerous substance. The woman was charged with assaulting a public official. Munnee described the man as having a long-standing history of violent confrontations with law enforcement, adding, 'He's not Mother Teresa or the Pope.' The event echoes a similar 2021 case in Texas, where a man also caught fire after being tased while soaked in gasoline — a tragic reminder of the deadly risks when volatile substances meet electrical deterrents.

Ifølge inspektør Bill Munnee hos Vest-Australisk politi hadde mannen blitt rapportert for limnosing og kom ut av hjemmet sitt med en beholder med bensin og en sigarettlås. article_content: On Monday afternoon, tragedy struck Pine Island, Minnesota, when two close friends and recent high school graduates — 18-year-old Kayla Jill Koranda and 19-year-old Nicholas Roecker — were found dead in a home on 100th Street North. Authorities believe the incident was a murder-suicide. Koranda was discovered dead inside a heated shed on the property, while Roecker, who was still alive but critically wounded, was rushed to Mayo Clinic Hospital, where he later passed away. Both young adults were freshmen at separate campuses of the University of Minnesota: Koranda studying liberal arts in Minneapolis, and Roecker pursuing science and engineering in Duluth. They had graduated together from Lourdes High School, a Catholic school in Rochester, where Roecker played varsity football and maintained a GPA above 3.5, earning him a spot on the honor roll. Koranda, too, was academically accomplished and had recently received a $1,000 award from the Olmsted Medical Center Auxiliary for her commitment to entering the healthcare field. According to Olmsted County Sheriff David Mueller, the two were close friends — not romantically involved — and had remained connected through social media. Police say Koranda visited Roecker on the day of the incident because he had been struggling with depression. A handgun found at the scene was determined to be the weapon used. Sheriff Mueller emphasized that while the exact nature of their bond remains unclear, there is no evidence suggesting anything beyond friendship. Roecker lived at Griggs Hall, and Koranda resided in Middlebrook Hall. Their deaths have left their families, classmates, and campus communities reeling. Officials continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the shooting, but early indications point to mental health struggles as a contributing factor.

article_content: NEW DELHI: Suryakumar Yadav was awarded the coveted 'Fielder of the Match' title for his outstanding fielding performance against the Netherlands, as India concluded the group stage of the World Cup with an unbeaten record. Known for his electrifying fielding, Suryakumar stood out among the nominees for the honor. India’s innovative fielding coach, T. Dilip, introduced a novel twist to the award ceremony by bringing the entire team and management onto the field. Instead of simply displaying nominees on a screen, Dilip revealed the finalists’ names live, building suspense and excitement. KL Rahul, Suryakumar Yadav, and Ravindra Jadeja were shortlisted for the award, with their images shown on the big screen. Ishan Kishan confidently predicted Suryakumar’s win before the announcement. When the results were revealed, Suryakumar was named the winner and received the gold medal from left-arm bowling specialist and fielding coach Nuwan Seneviratne. Expressing his gratitude, Dilip said, 'He has been tirelessly working behind the stumps, fulfilling dual roles. But especially in fielding, he has been my right shoulder — my everything.' After receiving the award, Suryakumar Yadav said, 'He has been behind me for a year — finally, I think this is the reward.' On the field, India successfully defended their total, winning by a commanding 160 runs. Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma each took a wicket with the ball, while star bowler Mohammed Siraj delivered a key performance. Looking ahead, Team India will face New Zealand in the semi-final at Mumbai’s Wankhede Stadium on Wednesday — a rematch of the 2019 World Cup clash. India aims to overturn their previous result and advance to the final. Their unbeaten group-stage run has heightened expectations for their World Cup campaign.

article_content: By Gordon Currie. PUBLISHED: 01:43 EST, 20 August 2013. | UPDATED: 07:09 EST, 20 August 2013. Audacious: Reece Scobie (pictured) deceived leading travel companies into funding a six-month global spree. It was a lavish con worthy of Leonardo DiCaprio’s character in the hit movie Catch Me If You Can. Teenager Reece Scobie repeatedly flew business class and stayed in luxury hotels after tricking his former employers at Thomson Travel. Like Frank Abagnale Jr.—DiCaprio’s character in the film—Scobie, 19, relied on charm and cunning to sustain his deception. Over six months, Scobie spent more than £70,000 by conning Thomson Travel, Cambridge Business Travel, and even Scottish court officials. He booked business-class flights to destinations including Singapore, Los Angeles, Dubai, Auckland, New York, and Vancouver. While under investigation, he convinced court staff to return his confiscated passport by presenting forged documents claiming a new job in the travel industry. Although he worked at Thomson Travel for only two months, Scobie continued using the company’s login credentials to make bookings after leaving his position. Perth Sheriff Court heard that Scobie has been diagnosed with Asperger’s syndrome. He used both his real name and multiple aliases to reserve hotel rooms. On one occasion, he accessed Cambridge Business Travel’s booking system after noticing a colleague had left a computer logged in at a British Airways lounge. From this access point, he arranged flights to Los Angeles, New York, Atlanta, Abu Dhabi, and Singapore. His scheme unraveled when he was in Los Angeles and his return flight was canceled due to suspicious activity, forcing him to borrow money to get home. Scobie admitted to two counts of fraud by obtaining services—flights and accommodation—while employed at Thomson Travel. He also confessed to using company passwords between July 2011 and January 2012 to book an unspecified number of flights and hotel rooms. He further admitted to accessing Cambridge Business Travel’s accounts in January 2013 and making multiple unauthorized bookings. Thomson Travel lost £11,256; Cambridge Business Travel lost £59,878. Some bookings were made from a public computer at Perth’s AK Bell Library. Scobie was arrested in early 2013, and his passport was seized as a bail condition. But on April 18, he returned to court, falsely claimed he had secured employment in the travel sector, and successfully retrieved his passport using fabricated documents. During sentencing proceedings, defense solicitor Jim Laverty acknowledged the gravity of the fraud and stated that, absent a credible alternative, detention would be necessary. Laverty informed the court that Scobie has been clinically diagnosed with Asperger’s syndrome. Sentencing was deferred pending psychiatric and restriction-of-liberty reports.

article_content: An eight-month-old Jack Russell terrier named Gypsy narrowly escaped death after clinging to a narrow ledge just feet from an active railway line for four hours. The ledge, formed by recent flooding, broke her fall ten feet above the busy Salisbury-to-London railway track in Andover, Hampshire. Gypsy had escaped from her home when someone improperly unlatched the garden door while her owner, Jane Alywiye, was at work. She tumbled down an embankment and became trapped, barking desperately for help. It took four hours before two passersby heard her cries and alerted authorities. Hampshire Fire and Rescue Service dispatched five firefighters, one of whom was lowered on a rope system to safely retrieve the frightened dog. Jane, 57, returned home to find the gate unlocked and Gypsy missing. When neighbors knocked on her door with the news, she rushed to the scene — relieved but furious. 'It was a miracle she didn’t land under a train,' she said. 'The person who left the door open nearly gave me a heart attack. It was reckless.' Miraculously, Gypsy emerged unharmed. Authorities emphasized the importance of securing pet access points to prevent such dangerous incidents.

article_content: CNN) — Palace Malice won the 2013 Belmont Stakes, the third leg of horse racing’s Triple Crown, on Saturday. The South Carolina-bred three-year-old outdueled Oxbow down the stretch to win the 1½-mile race. Oxbow, the Preakness Stakes winner, finished second. Orb — this year’s Kentucky Derby winner and the pre-race favorite at 2-to-1 odds — came in third. 'It was really a sneaky good race — he never took a breather once,' Palace Malice’s jockey, Mike Smith, told NBC, which broadcast the event. 'He was just enjoying the trip.' Palace Malice entered the 145th running of the Belmont Stakes as a longshot at 15-to-1 odds. His previous race was a 12th-place finish in the Kentucky Derby earlier that spring. Trained by Todd Pletcher, Palace Malice had only one prior win in seven starts, along with two second-place finishes and one third.

article_content: Robbie Keane modestly brushed aside personal accolades after becoming the highest goalscorer in European Championship qualifying history. The 34-year-old captain of the Republic of Ireland netted a hat-trick in a dominant 7-0 win over Gibraltar, taking his qualifying goal tally to 21 — one more than Turkey’s Hakan Şükür. That haul also pushed his overall international goal total for Ireland to 65, placing him just three behind West Germany’s Gerd Müller and six shy of retired German striker Miroslav Klose. Though widely celebrated, Keane, known for his lack of memory regarding past matches, insisted that milestones were far from his mind. 'I get messages — my brother texts me, my friends text me — but I honestly couldn’t tell you who’s close to me on the list,' he said. 'I know Klose. That’s about it. I don’t think about it. The past is the past. I’m focused on today.' Keane made his senior debut for Ireland in 1998 at age 17 and scored his first international goal later that year against Malta. His former strike partner, Niall Quinn — whose record of 21 goals Keane surpassed exactly ten years prior on October 12, 2004 — recognized his talent early. Now with 136 appearances, Keane is Ireland’s most-capped player. Despite occasional criticism over recent form, Keane remains indispensable. Defender John O’Shea defended him fiercely: 'People try to knock him because they’re desperate to find fault. But he’s an absolute legend — his finishing, his positioning, his consistency. He’s still doing it.' Ireland now turn their attention to a challenging Euro 2016 qualifier against world champions Germany in Gelsenkirchen. After Germany’s surprise 2-0 loss to Poland on October 10, 2015, Keane said: 'It’s a totally different challenge. But we’ve got six points in the bag heading into it. We believe we can get something from that game. No question.'

article_content: Editor's note: Junot Díaz’s novel, 'The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao,' won the Pulitzer Prize in 2008. (OPRAH.com) It wasn’t that I couldn’t write—I wrote every day. I showed up at my desk by 7 a.m., worked eight hours or more, scribbled at the dinner table, in bed, on the toilet, on the No. 6 train, even at Shea Stadium. I did everything I could. But nothing worked. My novel, which I’d begun with such hope after publishing my first short story collection, refused to progress beyond page 75. Everything after that felt meaningless. And yet—the first 75 pages? They were strong. Full of promise. It would’ve been easier if I could’ve moved on. But I couldn’t. Every other story I tried to write was worse. Worse still, I’d lost the ability to write short stories altogether. I felt trapped in a No-Writing Twilight Zone—with no exit. I was chained to those 75 pages like a man tied to a sinking ship, with no key, no patch for the hull. I wrote and wrote—but nothing I produced felt worthwhile. I persisted for five straight years. Five years of daily failure. Even I, a stubborn, hard-hearted soul, was worn down. Sixty months of rejection—by my own mind, by my own craft—nearly broke me. By year five, I was living with my fiancée (a relationship since ended), consumed by depression and self-loathing. I could barely function. I told her I might need to quit writing—for my sanity. She, desperate to see me happy and swayed by my despair, asked me to make a list of other careers. I’m not a list person. But I tried. It took a month to write three options. I stared at them for another month, praying for a miracle—a spark, a sign, a return of inspiration. Nothing came. So I boxed up the manuscript—hundreds of failed pages—and hid it away. I think I cried while doing it. Five years of my life, my identity, my dream—all gone because I couldn’t do what others seemed to do effortlessly: write a novel. I didn’t even want a Great American Novel anymore. I’d have settled for a forgettable New Jersey one. I became ‘normal.’ I avoided bookstores. I stopped reading the Sunday Book Review. I distanced myself from writer friends. The rage, the tears, the fights with my fiancée—gone. I slipped into a quiet, morose half-life. I prepared to return to school in September (I won’t say what I planned to study—it’s too embarrassing). While waiting, I’d lie on the floor of my writing room, the list on my chest, hoping its words would seep into me. Maybe I would’ve gone through with it. I’ll never know. But hearts, like the world, are what they are. One August night, sleepless and sick with regret—not just for quitting, but for fearing I’d have to return to writing—I dug out the manuscript. I told myself: if I can find just one good thing, I’ll go back. Just one. I read every page that night. It was worse than I remembered. Even more pathetic. That’s when I should’ve closed the box. Turned away. Walked into my new life. But I didn’t have the heart to let go. And somehow, I didn’t. While my fiancée slept, I sorted the 75 decent pages from the wreckage. Sat at my desk. Every fiber screamed 'no.' But I began again. No miracles. Just two more years of anguish, confusion, and doubt—then, slowly, the novel I’d dreamed of for over a decade began to emerge. Three more years passed before I could finally say the word I’d longed to speak for more than ten years: done. That’s my story—not how I wrote my novel, but how I became a writer. Because here’s the truth: you’re not a writer because you write well. Not because you’re gifted. Not because your words shine. You’re a writer because—even when there’s no hope, even when every page is trash—you keep writing anyway. It wasn’t until that night, staring at all those awful pages, that I truly understood who I was.
translated_content: Redaktørnotat: Junot Díaz' roman 'Den korte, wunderfulle livet til Oscar Wao' vant Pulitzerprisen i 2008. (OPRAH.com) Det var ikke at jeg ikke kunne skrive — jeg skrev hver dag. Jeg dukket opp ved skrivebordet klokken 7, jobbet åtte timer eller mer, kritterte på middagstabellen, i sengen, på toalettet, på linje 6, selv på Shea Stadium. Jeg gjorde alt jeg kunne. Men ingenting fungerte. Romanen min, som jeg hadde begynt med så stor håp etter å ha gitt ut min første samling noveller, ville ikke gå videre enn side 75. Alt etter det føltes meningsløst. Og likevel — de første 75 sidene? De var sterke. Full av potensial. Det hadde vært lettere hvis jeg kunne ha gått videre. Men jeg kunne ikke. Hver annen historie jeg prøvde å skrive var verre. Verre enn det — jeg hadde mistet evnen til å skrive noveller helt og holdent. Jeg følte meg fangt i en ingen-skrivning-Twilight-Zone — uten utgang. Jeg var festet til disse 75 sidene som en mann bundet til et synkende skip, uten nøkkel, uten pluss for hullene i skroget. Jeg skrev og skrev — men ingenting jeg produserte føltes verdiløst. Jeg holdt på i fem år i strøk. Fem år med daglig fiasko. Selv jeg, en stødig, hardhjertet sjel, ble slitt ned. Seksti måneder med avvisning — fra min egen hjerne, fra min egen kunst — nesten ødela meg. I år fem bodde jeg sammen med min forlovede (en relasjon som siden har sluttet), fordypet i depresjon og selvavsky. Jeg kunne knapt fungere. Jeg sa til henne at jeg kanskje måtte slutte å skrive — for min sjelssundhet. Hun, desperat for å se meg lykkelig og påvirket av min fortvilelse, ba meg lage en liste over andre yrker. Jeg er ikke en liste-type som hun var. Men jeg prøvde. Det tok en måned å skrive ned tre alternativer. Jeg stirret på dem i enda en måned, bad om et mirakel — et gnist, et tegn, en tilbakekomst av inspirasjon. Ingenting kom. Så jeg pakket inn manuskriptet — hundrevis av mislykkede sider — og skjulte det. Jeg tror jeg gråt mens jeg gjorde det. Fem år av mitt liv, min identitet, min drøm — borte fordi jeg ikke klarte å gjøre noe andre virket å gjøre med lettelse: skrive en roman. Jeg ville ikke engang ha en stor amerikansk roman lenger. Jeg hadde vært glad med en glemsel New Jersey-roman. Jeg ble 'normal.' Jeg unngikk bokbutikker. Jeg slo opp i søndagsbokseksjonen i Times ikke lenger. Jeg fjernet meg fra mine skribentvenner. Vrede, tårer, krangler med min forlovede — borte. Jeg glippe inn i et stille, mørkt halv-liv. Jeg forberedte meg på å gå tilbake til skolen i september (jeg vil ikke si hva jeg tenkte å studere — det er for pinlig). mens jeg ventet på at september skulle komme, lå jeg på gulvet i skriverommet mitt, listen på brystet, håpet ordene ville synke inn i meg. Kanskje jeg hadde gått gjennom med det. Jeg vet ikke. Men hjertene, som verden, er hva de er. En augustomkveld, våken og syk av sorg — ikke bare fordi jeg ga opp, men fordi jeg fryktet å måtte vende tilbake til skrivingen — jeg hentet fram manuskriptet. Jeg sa til meg selv: hvis jeg kan finne ett godt element, vil jeg gå tilbake. Bare ett. Jeg leste alle sidene den natten. Det var verre enn jeg husket. Enda mer meningsløst. Da burde jeg lagt alt i boksen. Vendt ryggen og gått inn i mitt nye liv. Men jeg hadde ikke hjertet til å la gå. Og på en måte, gjorde jeg det ikke. Mens min forlovede sov, skilte jeg de 75 gode sidene fra ruinene. Satte meg ved skrivebordet. Hver fiber skrek 'nei nei nei nei.' Men jeg begynte igjen. Ingen mirakler. Bare to år mer med sorg, forvirring og tvil — så, sakte, begynte romanen jeg hadde drømt om i over ti år å avsløre seg. Tre år til før jeg kunne si ordet jeg hadde lyst til å si i over ti år: ferdig. Det er min historie — ikke hvordan jeg skrev romanen min, men hvordan jeg ble en forfatter. Fordi her er sannheten: du er ikke en forfatter fordi du skriver bra. Ikke fordi du er begavet. Ikke fordi dine ord glimrer. Du er en forfatter fordi — selv når det ikke er håp, selv når hver side er søppel — du fortsetter å skrive likevel. Det var ikke før den natten, da jeg stirret på alle de onde sidene, at jeg virkelig forsto hvem jeg var.

article_content: By Stephen Wright. PUBLISHED: 16:14 EST, 3 April 2013. | UPDATED: 02:14 EST, 4 April 2013. A 20th anniversary memorial service for Stephen Lawrence will take place later this month. An independent poll commissioned by the think tank British Future has recognized the profound impact of the Daily Mail’s long-running campaign for justice following the 1993 racist murder of 18-year-old Stephen Lawrence. Sixty-seven percent of respondents said the media played a key role in keeping the case in the public eye, affirming that campaigning journalism can be a force for good in Britain. The poll results emerged shortly after Gary Dobson, 37—one of two men convicted of Stephen’s murder—dropped his appeal against conviction. His decision was welcomed by Stephen’s mother, Doreen Lawrence, who urged the other convicted man, David Norris, 36, to follow suit. For 16 years, the Daily Mail campaigned tirelessly for justice. In February 1997, it published photographs of the five main suspects—Dobson, Norris, Neil Acourt, Jamie Acourt, and Luke Knight—under the headline 'Murderers,' challenging them to sue if they believed the claims were false. None did. The newspaper repeated the front page in July 2006, again without legal repercussions. Its reporting exposed serious police failures and contributed to the establishment of the Macpherson Inquiry, which concluded the Metropolitan Police was 'institutionally racist.' This led to legal reforms allowing Dobson to be retried despite a prior acquittal. After both men were found guilty in January 2012, Dobson received a minimum sentence of 15 years and two months; Norris received 14 years and three months. As the Lawrence family prepares for a deeply emotional memorial on April 22, British Future released findings from a survey of 2,000 British adults. Seventy-four percent agreed that the Lawrence family’s determination demonstrated that ordinary citizens can achieve real change and secure justice. Only four percent disagreed. While most respondents believe racism in Britain has declined since Stephen’s death, they acknowledge that prejudice remains widespread. Sunder Katwala, director of British Future, said: 'This poll shows the public believes the campaign for justice made a vital difference. Hate crimes still occur—but honoring this anniversary means redoubling efforts to eliminate the prejudices that fuel them.' Labour MP David Lammy added: 'Those who killed Stephen did not represent Britain then, and racists today do not represent Britain now. The country is better—but we must not pretend the problem has vanished.'

article_content: Authorities are searching for a violent duo impersonating police officers to target motorists on the Gold Coast. The suspects use a smartphone app that simulates red and blue flashing police lights to trick drivers into pulling over — then assault them. Three attacks have occurred over a 12-day period. The most recent happened at 4:30 a.m. on Thursday on Enid Avenue in Southport. Previous incidents took place on Christine Avenue in Varsity Lakes on May 11 at approximately 4 p.m., and on Bundall Road on May 3 at around 10 p.m. In the latest attack, 24-year-old Terry Hicks was pulled over after seeing flashing lights on a vehicle behind him. Believing it to be a police officer conducting a random breath test, he rolled down his window. Before he could turn around, he was struck three times in the neck with a Taser-like device. His attacker also shouted obscenities. Hicks managed to fight back, kicking the assailant through the driver’s side window, repositioning himself in the driver’s seat, and speeding away. He immediately called emergency services. The suspect vehicle was described as a white 4WD dual-cab utility with a silver bull bar. In the earlier incident on Christine Avenue, an off-duty police officer was stopped by a blue Holden Commodore sedan fitted with a strobe light — the suspects fled before he could approach. On Bundall Road, a 54-year-old woman and her 64-year-old male passenger were pulled over. One attacker approached the window, yelling; the second punched the male passenger in the face, causing bruising and swelling. Queensland Police are seeking two men in connection with all three incidents. The suspects reportedly fled in a silver-blue vehicle. Hicks, though physically unharmed beyond minor neck bruising, expressed deep distrust toward roadside encounters. 'I don’t think I’d feel safe driving past that area again,' he said. 'I don’t understand how someone could do this for no reason.' Emergency responders and medical staff confirmed that Hicks’ quick actions likely saved his life.
