article_content: British celebrity chef Heston Blumenthal has teamed up with Michelin-starred chef Simon Hulstone to redesign British Airways’ in-flight menu for the summer Olympics. The new offerings—like mackerel rillette on pickled cucumber carpaccio with sourdough croutes—are part of a broader trend where airlines are turning to famous chefs to shake off their reputation for bland, unappetizing meals. Industry expert Peter Jones, formerly of the International Travel Catering Association and now a professor at the University of Surrey, explains that flying changes how we taste food: dry cabin air dulls our senses, making flavors less intense. That’s why top airlines aren’t just hiring chefs—they’re hiring scientists who understand physiology at altitude. Major carriers like Singapore Airlines, Air France, Qantas, and others have already partnered with stars like Gordon Ramsay and Joel Robuchon to craft elevated menus for business and first-class travelers. But for most people flying economy? Don’t expect much more than chicken or pasta—and on short flights, sometimes just a snack or sandwich. Marco 't Hart, who runs airlinemeals.net and has reviewed over 20,000 meals worldwide, notes that while premium dining has improved dramatically, economy remains stuck in the past. Some airlines, like airBaltic, have even incorporated regional Slow Food principles, and others, including Turkish Airlines and Etihad, bring chefs onboard to prepare meals mid-flight. Still, Jones doubts we’ll ever see celebrity chefs flipping pancakes in a moving jet. ‘The galley space is tiny, and safety rules are strict,’ he says. ‘It’s great marketing—but real cooking? That’s still done by trained cabin crew under tight constraints.’

De nye rettene — som f.eks. rillet av makrell på innlagt gurkekarpaccio med surdeigskroker — er en del av en bredere trend der flyselskaper vender seg mot kjente kokker for å skifte sin rykte om triste og utilgjengelige måltider. Derfor ansetter ikke bare toppflyselskaper kokker — de ansetter også vitenskapsmenn som forstår fysiologi i høyde. Store selskaper som Singapore Airlines, Air France, Qantas og andre har allerede samarbeidet med stjerner som Gordon Ramsay og Joel Robuchon for å lage forbedrede menyvalg for forretnings- og førsteklasses passasjerer. Men for de fleste som reiser i økonomiklasse? Ikke forvent mye mer enn kylling eller pasta — og på korte ruter, noen ganger bare en snack eller en sandwich. Marco 't Hart, som driver airlinemeals.net og har analysert over 20.000 måltider verden over, legger merke til at mens premium-måltider har blitt betydelig bedre, så er økonomiklassen fortsatt i fortiden. article_content: By Daily Mail Reporter. Stand clear — this is my personal space. An industrial designer frustrated by the constant pushing and shoving of subway travel has created a striking, non-lethal fashion accessory designed to keep fellow passengers at a distance: the 'Spike Away' vest. Made from flexible plastic spikes typically used in gardens to deter birds and cats, the vest is constructed entirely from common hardware store materials. According to its creator, Siew Ming Cheng, the spikes cause no physical harm — their effect is purely visual. Cheng developed the vest during a design workshop at the National University of Singapore, part of a course titled 'Chindogu' — the Japanese art of inventing impractical solutions to everyday problems. Led by German futurist designer Werner Aisslinger, the workshop challenged participants to prototype ideas using readily available materials within half a day. Cheng’s response? Wearable armor made from plastic spike strips secured with cable ties. Though the vest is not intended for commercial use, critics have jokingly labeled it a 'lawsuit waiting to happen.' However, its purpose isn’t functionality — it’s commentary. The design intentionally highlights the absurdity of overcrowded public transit and the lengths people might go to reclaim personal space.

Laget av fleksible plastspyd som vanligvis brukes i hagen for å skremme bort fugler og katter, er vesten laget helt av vanlige materialer fra en verkstedbutikk. Ifølge skaperen Siew Ming Cheng forårsaker spydene ingen fysisk skade — effekten er ren visuell. Cheng utviklet vesten under et designverksted ved Nasjonale universitet i Singapore, som var en del av et kurs med tittelen 'Chindogu' — den japanske kunsten å lage umulige løsninger på daglige problemer. Men formålet er ikke funksjonalitet — det er kommentar. Designet hevder bevisst absurditeten til overfylte kollektivtransportmidler og hvor langt mennesker kan gå for å gjenopprette personlig rom.

article_content: Changing 175 diapers and preparing 80 bottles of formula each week might sound impossible — but for Sarah Ward, it’s just Tuesday. Just nine months after welcoming her first child, Freddie, she gave birth to triplets: Stanley, Daisy, and Reggie. All four babies were conceived naturally, despite Sarah having spent over a year trying — and fearing — she’d never become a mother. When she discovered she was pregnant again, just eight weeks after Freddie’s birth, Sarah was in shock. She hadn’t even stopped wearing maternity clothes. Then came the ultrasound: three tiny heartbeats. 'We thought it was twins,' she recalls. 'When she said triplets, I nearly fell off the bed.' The pregnancy was high-risk, and doctors at Medway Hospital offered the option of reducing the number of babies to improve survival chances. Sarah and her partner, Benn, chose to carry all four to term. At 33 weeks, an emergency C-section was needed after one baby showed distress. Stanley, Reggie, and Daisy were born weighing under five pounds each. Now, with the triplets home and 19 weeks old, life is a whirlwind. Feeding, changing, laundry — it’s nonstop. A trip to the store can take hours because strangers constantly stop to ask if all four babies are hers. 'They can’t believe it when I say yes,' Sarah laughs. 'But I love the attention. I’m so proud.' Benn admits it’s exhausting. 'It’s crazy,' he says, 'but seeing them so close already? It’s worth it.' Sarah didn’t use birth control after Freddie’s birth, assuming conception would take another year. Instead, she became pregnant again — likely due to lactational amenorrhea, a natural, hormone-based method of contraception that can work if breastfeeding is frequent and exclusive. Though rare in Western countries, it’s medically documented and plausible under the right conditions. Though they’re overwhelmed, Sarah calls herself 'the luckiest mum in the world.' And for now, the idea of another baby? 'Not anytime soon,' Benn adds with a smile.

'Vi trodde det var tvillinger,' sier hun. 'Da hun sa trillinger, falt jeg nesten av sengen.' Graviditeten var høyrisikofylt, og leger ved Medway-sykehuset tilbød muligheten til å redusere antallet barn for å forbedre overlevelsesmulighetene. article_content: After 43 years of part-time study, 65-year-old Michael Poyzer has finally graduated with a BSc Honours degree from the Open University. He began his studies in 1971 at age 22, juggling coursework with running a bicycle business, raising three children, writing a novel, and later caring for four grandchildren. His determination paid off last summer when he received word he had passed with a 2:2 classification. He celebrated with a graduation ceremony at Birmingham’s Symphony Hall earlier this month, walking alongside students half his age. Now retired, Poyzer plans to pursue a Master’s in Creative Writing at Nottingham Trent University. 'I’ve got the thirst for academia again,' he said. 'I was never going to quit. Every time I picked up my books, it all came flooding back.' Poyzer left school at 16 to become an apprentice at the Raleigh bike factory in Nottingham. In 1977, he founded Super Cycles, which later became Rock 'n' Roll Bikes — a business he still operates today. He started his degree during the Open University’s inaugural year — the same year the UK adopted decimal currency. Back then, learning meant tuning into late-night TV lectures. 'There were no online platforms,' he recalled. 'You studied when you could — between shifts, after bedtime, during commercial breaks.' Over four decades, the total cost of his degree amounted to just £2,500. Had he started today, he estimates tuition alone would have reached £387,000. His wife, Susan, said: 'We’re so proud of him. Now he’ll have more time with the grandchildren.' The Open University praised his commitment: 'Mr Poyzer began studying when lecturers taught in tank tops on analog TV. He finishes in an era where students learn via smartphones and on-demand platforms.' Today, OU regulations cap degree completion at 16 years — a stark contrast to Poyzer’s lifelong journey.

article_content: The businessman who exposed Liam Fox’s unethical relationship with private adviser Adam Werritty—leading to Fox’s 2011 resignation from the Cabinet—is now secretly funding a campaign to unseat him as MP for North Somerset. In 2011, it was revealed that Fox, then Defence Secretary, took Werritty, a close friend, on 18 overseas trips funded by private donors and granted him frequent access to the Ministry of Defence (MoD). Dubai-based Harvey Boulter first brought this relationship to light. Now, The Mail on Sunday reports that Boulter has donated £30,000 to Ukip candidate Ian Kealey, Fox’s main opponent in North Somerset. Boulter is also paying for a billboard in the constituency featuring Fox and Werritty at Fox’s 2005 wedding, alongside the slogan: 'Vote Him, Get Him.' North Somerset is a key target for Ukip, having topped the vote in the 2014 European Parliament elections. Werritty, who had no security clearance, lived rent-free in Fox’s flat and carried a business card falsely claiming he was a government adviser. He even served as Fox’s best man. An inquiry led by Cabinet Secretary Sir Gus O’Donnell concluded Fox breached the Ministerial Code by allowing Werritty to create a misleading impression of official status. Fox resigned, apologizing for 'errors of judgment' and conflating personal and professional loyalties. Boulter, whose initial disclosures went unchallenged, was sued by Fox for libel over remarks made in an unbroadcast segment of a TV interview. That lawsuit was settled last year with damages paid by Fox. Kealey, a 56-year-old nuclear physicist turned farmer, said Boulter’s donation is helping Ukip reach voters through newsletters and campaign outreach. Boulter stated North Somerset 'deserves better' than Fox and believes Ukip is best positioned to defeat him. Fox, now 56, recently said he looks forward to campaigning on issues affecting his constituents.

I 2011 ble det avslørt at Fox, da forsvarsminister, tok Werritty, en nær venn, på 18 utenlandsreiser finansiert av private donatorer og gav ham hyppig tilgang til Forsvarsdepartementet (MoD). Dubai-basert Harvey Boulter var den første som la fram dette forholdet. Nå rapporterer The Mail on Sunday at Boulter har donert 30.000 britiske pund til Ukip-kandidat Ian Kealey, Foxs hovedmotstander i North Somerset. Boulter betaler også for en billboard i valgkretsen som viser Fox og Werritty ved Foxs bryllup i 2005, sammen med slogangen: 'Stem på ham, få ham.' North Somerset er et viktig mål for Ukip, som vant flest stemmer i europawvelgen i 2014. Werritty, som ikke hadde sikkerhetsklaring, bodde ubetalte i Foxs leilighet og bar en visittkort som falskt hevdet han var en offisiell rådgiver. Han var også Foxs brudgomsvenn. article_content: Incredible scenes unfolded on Dutch television tonight after a teenage gunman stormed the studios of the national broadcaster NOS, demanding to be put on air. The suspect, described as smartly dressed and carrying a suppressed pistol, seized control of the studio, forcing NOS off the air for approximately one hour. However, cameras continued recording as police rushed in to disarm him. According to an NOS reporter who spoke with the suspect—believed to be 19-year-old Tarik Zahzah—he claimed to be part of a hacker collective working for Dutch intelligence. After his arrest ended the standoff at the NOS headquarters in Hilversum, 12 miles east of Amsterdam, footage of the incident was broadcast nationwide. No one was injured, and no shots were fired during the event, which interrupted NOS’s prime-time evening news. Police stated the man threatened to detonate bombs at multiple locations across the Netherlands if his demand for live television access was not met. Witnesses reported that the suspect entered the studio after threatening a guard with his firearm. It remains unclear how he bypassed security, which had been strengthened following the Paris attacks earlier this month. Footage aired on Dutch TV showed the suspect pacing in the studio with a black pistol hidden behind his back. He had intended to address the nation during the most-watched news broadcast, but a quick-thinking security guard led him to an empty studio instead. As cameras rolled, the suspect told someone off-camera: 'The things that are going to be said—those are very large world affairs. We were hired by the security service.' He grew impatient, saying, 'This is taking too long.' Soon after, armed police stormed the studio shouting, 'Drop it! Drop it! And get on your knees!' The suspect immediately surrendered, obeying orders to turn around and lie down without resistance. He was handcuffed without incident. Police are investigating whether the suspect had accomplices and whether the threats—including a letter alleging eight radioactive bombs planted across the Netherlands—were genuine. The letter, reportedly shown on RTL, read: 'Realise that I am not on my own. Furthermore, eight high explosives have been planted that contain radioactive material. If you don't take me to Studio 8 to make my broadcast, we will be forced to step into action.' Its authenticity has not been confirmed. NOS confirmed the suspect had a suppressor attached to his weapon and forced a guard to escort him to the editorial offices. Reports suggest he was a student who had recently lost both parents and was not listed on any counterterrorism watchlists. NOS, which produces the Netherlands’ most-watched news program, is based in the Media Park in Hilversum—a facility heavily secured since the 2002 assassination of politician Pim Fortuyn. All staff were evacuated, and police conducted a full sweep of the building, finding no explosives. NOS resumed broadcasting from a studio in The Hague. Authorities continue to question the suspect, who may face charges including kidnapping, illegal firearm possession, and making credible threats.

Imidlertid fortsatte kameraene å filme mens politiet stormet inn for å våpenfri ham. Ifølge en NOS-rapportør som talte med den mistenkte—som antas å være 19-åringen Tarik Zahzah—påstod han at han var medlem av en hakergruppe som jobbet for den nederlandske etterretningstjenesten. Etter hans arrestasjon avsluttet dette gislerettet ved NOS-hovedkvarteret i Hilversum, 12 mil øst for Amsterdam, og opptaket av hendelsen ble sendt til hele landet. Ingen ble skadet, og ingen skudd ble avfyrt under hendelsen, som avbrøt NOS sine viktigste kveldsnyhetene. Politiet sa at mannen truet med å detonere bomber på flere steder i Nederland hvis han ikke fikk tilgang til direktesending. Vitner rapporterte at den mistenkte kom inn i studioet etter å ha truet en vakt med sin pistol. Det er fortsatt uklart hvordan han klarte å komme forbi sikkerheten, som hadde blitt forsterket etter angrepene i Paris tidligere denne måneden. Opptak som ble sendt på nederlandsk TV viste den mistenkte som gikk frem og tilbake i studioet med en svart pistol skjult bak ryggen. Han hadde hensikten å snakke til landet under de mest sett nyhetene, men en rasktanke vakt ledet ham til et tomt studio istedenfor. Mens kameraene gikk, sa den mistenkte til noen utenfor kameraet: 'Det som skal sies—det er veldig store verdenssaker. Vi ble ansatt av sikkerhetstjenesten.' Han ble utilfreds og sa: 'Dette tar for lang tid.' Snart etter stormet bevæpnede politifolk studioet og ropte: 'Slipp det! Slipp det! Og gå ned på kneene!' Den mistenkte kapitulerte umiddelbart, fulgte ordren om å snu seg og legge seg ned uten motstand. Han ble håndfeste uten problemer. Politiet undersøker om den mistenkte hadde medhjelpere og om truslene—inkludert et brev som påstår at åtte radioaktive bomber er plassert over hele Nederland—var sanne. Brevet, som ifølge RTL ble vist, sa: 'Forstå at jeg ikke er alene. Videre har åtte høye eksplosiver blitt plassert som inneholder radioaktivt materiale. Hvis dere ikke tar meg til Studio 8 for å gjøre sendingen min, vil vi bli tvunget til å gå til handling.' Ektegnet til brevet er ikke bekreftet. NOS bekreftet at den mistenkte hadde en suppressor på pistolen og tvang en vakt til å føre ham opp til redaksjonelle kontorer. Rapporter antyder at han var en student som nylig hadde mistet begge foreldrene og ikke sto på noen overvåkningsliste for islamistiske militanter. NOS, som produserer Nederlands mest sett nyhetsprogram, er basert i Media Park i Hilversum—et anlegg sterkt sikret siden politikeren Pim Fortuyn ble skutt i en parkeringsplass der i 2002. Alle ansatte ble evakuert, og politiet utførte en full gjennomgang av bygningen og fant ingen bomber. NOS gjenopptok sendingen fra et studio i Haag. Myndighetene fortsetter å forhøre den mistenkte, som kan bli tiltalt for kidnapning, ulovlig våpenbesittelse og trusler mot folk.

article_content: At Stamford High School in Connecticut, two top administrators—Principal Donna Valentine and Assistant Principal Roth Nordin—are being reassigned after failing to report a sexual relationship between teacher Danielle Watkins and an 18-year-old student. Despite being legally required to notify authorities within 12 hours of learning about the relationship, neither reported it. Valentine claims she learned of the affair near the end of the previous school year; Nordin allegedly knew as well. Their silence lasted until the student went to police in June, triggering an investigation that led to Watkins’ arrest. Watkins, a married mother of two, pleaded guilty in October to second-degree sexual assault and endangering a minor. She admitted to a nine-month relationship with the student, during which she allegedly threatened to fail him when he tried to end things. Police found marijuana in her car, along with explicit photos she’d sent to the teen. Evidence also showed she provided drugs to another 15-year-old student and let him drive her car without a license. Over 2,000 text messages and countless calls documented the inappropriate contact. Though they faced potential criminal charges, Valentine and Nordin entered Connecticut’s Accelerated Rehabilitation Program, which could erase their records if completed. Thanks to protections from their teachers’ union, they won’t lose their jobs—only their roles at Stamford High. Superintendent Winifred Hamilton confirmed they’ll be moved to other district positions, though she wouldn’t specify where. A third administrator, Angela Thomas-Graves, is also on leave amid suspicions she knew too. Meanwhile, Watkins is set to be sentenced on January 22, facing four years in prison and a decade on the state’s Sex Offender Registry. The school district is moving to revoke her teaching license. Parents are devastated. 'It’s going to take a long time to trust this school again,' said one parent. An independent review led by a retired judge is ongoing and due in February—but many feel no amount of investigation can undo the damage done.

article_content: New York (CNN) — The editor-in-chief of Essence Magazine has defended her decision to hire Elliana Placas, the publication’s first white fashion director — a move that has ignited intense debate within the Black community. For 40 years, Essence has celebrated and centered Black women, making the appointment especially provocative. The controversy began when former Essence staffer Michaela Angela Davis posted an emotional message on Facebook: 'It’s with a heavy heart I’ve learned Essence Magazine has engaged a white Fashion Director... It hurts, literally.' Davis, who deeply loves the magazine and its mission, argued that the role represented a rare opportunity for a Black woman to lead in an industry that has long excluded them. In response, Editor-in-Chief Angela Burt-Murray published an opinion piece on theGrio.com, explaining that Placas first joined Essence six months ago as a freelance fashion contributor. 'I saw firsthand her creativity, vision, and deep respect for our audience,' Burt-Murray wrote. 'She earned this role — and my confidence in her hasn’t wavered. This decision in no way diminishes my commitment to Black women.' Critics point to the stark lack of diversity in fashion: at recent Fashion Weeks, Essence had only one seat — and many feel it should have been occupied by someone who embodies the full spectrum of Black beauty, history, and identity. 'The fashion industry is an elite, closed world,' Davis told CNN. 'That seat should go to someone who can represent us authentically.' Burt-Murray acknowledged these concerns, stating she too wants to see more Black women on magazine mastheads, front rows, and design teams. 'I want us designing our own fashion lines and contributing our flyness to the world of style,' she wrote. Yet, she also reminded readers of Essence’s long record of covering urgent issues often ignored by mainstream media — from the disproportionate impact of HIV on young Black women, to child welfare failures and sex trafficking in urban communities. 'The things that really are the end of our world apparently aren’t,' she noted, suggesting the public’s focus on this hiring distracts from deeper advocacy. Davis, while critical, urged readers not to boycott the magazine: 'We need Essence today as we did 40 years ago.' But she added, 'I spoke out for all the Black girls who called me crying — what does this say to them?' Burt-Murray concluded: 'Our commitment to Black women remains unchanged. No matter who works with us, Essence will continue to celebrate, empower, and inspire.'
translated_content: New York (CNN) — Redaktøren i Essence Magazine har forsvart sitt valg av å ansette Elliana Placas, publikasjonens første hvite modedirektør — et valg som har utløst intens debatt innenfor svarte fellesskapet. I 40 år har Essence feiret og sentrert svarte kvinner, noe som gjør denne ansettelsen spesielt provokerende. Kontroversen startet da tidligere Essence-medarbeider Michaela Angela Davis postet en følelsesmessig melding på Facebook: 'Det er med tungt hjerte jeg har lært at Essence Magazine har ansatt en hvit modedirektør... Det gjør vondt, bokstavelig talt.' Davis, som elsker magasinet og dets misjon, argumenterte for at rollen var en sjelden mulighet for en svart kvinne til å lede i en bransje som lenge har ekskludert dem. Som svar publiserte redaktør i sjef Angela Burt-Murray en meningsartikkel på theGrio.com, der hun forklarte at Placas først kom til Essence for seks måneder siden som frilansmodebidragsyter. 'Jeg så med egne øyne hennes kreativitet, visjon og dypt respekt for vårt publikum,' skrev Burt-Murray. 'Hun har fortjent denne rollen — og min tillit til henne har ikke sviktet. Dette valget formindsker ikke min forpliktelse til svarte kvinner.' Kritikere peker på den store mangelen på mangfold i modebransjen: ved nylige Fashion Weeks hadde Essence bare én sete — og mange mener det burde ha blitt besatt av noen som representerer hele spekteret av svart skjønnhet, historie og identitet. 'Modebransjen er en elitær, lukket verden,' sa Davis til CNN. 'Denne seten burde ha gått til noen som kan representere oss autentisk.' Burt-Murray anerkjente disse bekymringene og sa at hun også ønsker å se flere svarte kvinner på magasinets redaksjonskomitéer, i forreste rad ved showene og som designere. 'Jeg vil se oss selv lage våre egne modekolleksjoner og bidra med vår unike stil og flyness til verden av mode,' skrev hun. Men hun minnet også leserne om Essences lange historie med å dekke presserende emner som ofte ignoreres av mainstream-media — fra den urettferdige påvirkningen av HIV på unge svarte kvinner, til barnepasningssvikt og menneskehandel i urbane samfunn. 'Sakene som virkelig er slutten på vår verden ser ut til ikke å være det,' bemerket hun, og antydde at offentlighetens fokus på denne ansettelsen avledet oppmerksomheten fra dypere engasjement. Davis, selv om hun er kritisk, oppfordret leserne til ikke å boykotte magasinet: 'Vi trenger Essence i dag akkurat som vi gjorde for 40 år siden.' Men hun la til: 'Jeg snakket ut for alle de svarte jentene som ringte meg og gråt — hva sier dette til dem?' Burt-Murray avsluttet: 'Vår forpliktelse til svarte kvinner forblir uendret. Uansett hvem som jobber med oss, vil Essence fortsette å feire, styrke og inspirere.'

article_content: A 44-year-old man was seriously injured in hospital last night after being bitten three times by an adder in Dalby Forest, North Yorkshire. He was airlifted to James Cook University Hospital in Middlesbrough by air ambulance after receiving initial treatment from paramedics at the scene. The victim, whose identity has not been disclosed, was attacked near the Go-Ape outdoor adventure site. Alan Eves of the Forestry Commission noted that Dalby Forest has a thriving population of adders. Although adder venom poses little threat to healthy adults, bites are extremely painful and require urgent medical attention. The last known fatality from an adder bite in Britain was a five-year-old child in Scotland in 1975. In the wild, adders use their venom to immobilize small prey — such as lizards, amphibians, nestlings, and small mammals — then return to consume them once the venom takes effect. Last month, an 11-year-old boy, Carl Jefferies, was bitten on the left leg by an adder while retrieving his football from a bramble bush near his home in Bolton, Lancashire. He was treated successfully in hospital.

Ofret, hvis identitet ikke er offentliggjort, ble angrepet nær Go-Ape-utendørs eventyrplassen. Alan Eves ved Skogvesenet bemerket at Dalby Forest har en rik populasjon av piggormer. Selv om piggormens gift utgjør liten trussel mot friske voksne, kan bittene være ekstremt smertefulle og kreve akutt medisinsk hjelp. Den siste kjente dødsfallet som følge av et piggormsbitt i Storbritannia var en fem år gammel gutt i Skottland i 1975. I viltet bruker piggormer sin gift for å lamme små byttedyr — som øgler, amfibier, unger og små pattedyr — og returnerer for å spise dem når giftet har tatt effekt. Forrige måned ble en 11-årig gutt, Carl Jefferies, biten i venstre ben av en piggorm mens han hentet fotballen sin fra en tornbusk nær hjemmet sitt i Bolton, Lancashire. Han ble behandlet vellykket på sykehus.

article_content: IIT Madras has rolled out a brand-new hub called the Career Pathway Centre — a one-stop destination designed to bring together every aspect of student career support. No more jumping between offices: now, placement advice, internship matching, soft skills workshops, and even startup incubation all happen under the same roof. At the heart of this initiative is the student-run Entrepreneurship Cell (E-Cell), which has been fully woven into the centre’s ecosystem. The goal? To give every student the tools, confidence, and real-world exposure they need to carve out their own unique career path — whether that means landing a corporate job, starting a business, or exploring freelance routes. The Placement and Internship Office connects students directly with employers, while the Career Development Cell runs practical sessions on communication, leadership, and professionalism. Meanwhile, the E-Cell acts as a live lab where aspiring founders test ideas, build teams, and pitch prototypes. Together, these components form a dynamic support network aimed at boosting not just employability, but entrepreneurial spirit and personal agency among students.

I hjertet av dette initiativet ligger elevdrevne Entrepreneurship Cell (E-Cell), som er fullstendig integrert i enhetens økosystem. Målet? Å gi hver student verktøy, selvtillit og reell eksponering for å skape sin egen unike karrierebane — enten det betyr å få et jobb hos et selskap, starte et firma eller utforske frilansmuligheter. Placement- og praktikantkontoret kobler studenter direkte med arbeidsgivere, mens Career Development Cell arrangerer praktiske kurs i kommunikasjon, ledelse og profesjonalitet. E-Cell fungerer som et livende laboratorium der fremtidige entreprenører tester idéer, bygger team og presenterer prototyper. article_content: In a vibrant Hindu wedding ceremony near Indore in Madhya Pradesh, India, a sacred cow named Ganga and a bull named Prakash were formally united in marriage. The event, attended by over 5,000 villagers, cost £10,000 and was organized by Gopal Patwari — Ganga’s guardian — along with 24 other community members. The wedding was conducted to invoke divine protection against natural disasters such as hailstorms and torrential rains, which had recently devastated neighboring farmlands. According to Patwari, local spiritual leaders advised the ceremony as a means to preserve the village’s agricultural livelihood. Ganga arrived adorned in a custom-made red bridal saree, jewelry, and floral garlands, while Prakash entered on a lavishly decorated bullock cart, draped in a colorful sherwani and orange turban. The ceremony followed all traditional Hindu rites, including Haldi, Ganesh Pooja, Mandap, and the sacred Fera — circling the holy fire seven times. A marching band led the procession, a professional chef prepared meals for guests, and a DJ entertained the crowd throughout the day-long celebration. Invitations were extended to 10,000 residents across three nearby villages, with donations encouraged to help cover the costs. Patwari expressed deep joy at the union, stating, 'I am happy. People around me are happy. Everyone is happy.' He hopes Ganga and Prakash will thrive together, produce offspring, and inspire future generations to honor their religious heritage. The organizers envision this as the first of many such ceremonies to come. The event, which took two months to plan, reflects the deep cultural and spiritual significance of cattle in Hinduism and underscores the community’s reliance on agriculture for survival.

Ifølge Patwari rådet lokale åndelige ledere til seremonien som et middel for å bevare landsbyens landbrukseksistens. Ganga ankom i en tilpasset rød brudekjole, smykker og blomsterkranser, mens Prakash ankom på en dekorert oksekjær, klædd i en farget sherwani og oransje turban. article_content: Eighteen-year-old fisherman Daniel Smith tragically lost his life after a shark attack off Rudder Reef, near Port Douglas in Far North Queensland, on Monday. He sustained severe bites to his upper thigh, groin, and upper arm while swimming. Friends aboard his private boat immediately administered emergency first aid, including CPR and use of an onboard defibrillator, as they raced toward shore—a journey taking approximately two hours. Daniel, a recent graduate of Mossman State High School and beloved member of the local community, was pronounced dead upon arrival at Sugar Wharf around 2 p.m. Despite efforts by Queensland Ambulance personnel and standby medical staff from Mossman Hospital, he could not be revived. Greg Thiedecke, Executive Manager of Operations at Queensland Ambulance Service, noted that the speed of cardiac arrest suggested massive blood loss, particularly given the location of the injuries near major blood vessels. Authorities have not yet identified the shark species involved. A coroner’s report is expected to follow. Veteran diver and marine tourism operator Col McKenzie remarked that Rudder Reef is a known spot for spearfishers, not tourists, and that thigh injuries are common among those who store bait in their weight belts—an observation that may be relevant to this case. He also recalled a similar fatality at nearby Opal Reef nearly a decade ago, when spearfisherman Mark Thompson, 38, suffered a shark bite on December 11, 2004, and later died of cardiac arrest. Tributes poured in on social media, with friends and locals describing Daniel as kind, vibrant, and tragically taken too soon. Douglas Shire Mayor Julia Leu called him a 'much-loved local high school graduate,' adding that the community is in shock. The incident has reignited discussions about safety in shark-prone waters frequented by recreational divers.

Vennene ombord på hans private båt utførte umiddelbar førstehjelp, inkludert hjertekomprimeringer og bruk av en defibrillator, mens de rasket mot kysten—en reise som tok cirka to timer. Daniel, en nylig eksamensstudent fra Mossman State High School og et mye elsket medlem av lokalsamfunnet, ble erklært død ved ankomst til Sugar Wharf rundt kl. 14:00. Tross anstrengelsene fra Queensland Ambulansetjenesten og det på vent stående medisinske teamet fra Mossman sykehus, kunne han ikke gjenopplives. Greg Thiedecke, administrerende direktør for operasjoner i Queensland Ambulansetjenesten, påpekte at hastigheten i hjertestans tydet på massivt blodtap, spesielt gitt skadenes plassering nær store blodkar. Han husket også et lignende dødsfall nær Opal Reef nesten ti år siden, da spydfiskeren Mark Thompson, 38, ble angrepet 11. desember 2004 og senere døde av hjertestans. Hyldester strømmet inn på sosiale medier, der venner og lokale beskrev Daniel som snill, levende og tragisk tatt for tidlig. article_content: Therese Serignese, now in her 60s, has shared her harrowing experience of being drugged and assaulted by Bill Cosby in 1976, when she was just 19. After meeting him following a Las Vegas stand-up performance, she says he handed her pills she didn’t question—out of fear and intimidation. When she regained consciousness, she says Cosby was sexually assaulting her. Though she stayed in his penthouse for weeks afterward, she eventually left, pursued nursing school, and fulfilled his promise: she earned good grades, and he sent her $10,000 through Western Union. But she says no amount of money could erase the trauma. Serignese is one of 13 women who came forward as ‘Jane Does’ in Andrea Constand’s 2006 civil lawsuit against Cosby, which ended in a settlement. She now demands an apology: 'You owe me an explanation. I want you to admit what you did was wrong.' In a separate account, Carla Ferrigno—wife of actor Lou Ferrigno—revealed that in 1967, when she was a teenager, Cosby forcibly kissed her at a party while his wife was home. She told reporters she considers herself 'lucky' because he didn’t physically harm her, though the incident left lasting emotional scars. She didn’t speak about it publicly until recently. Cosby has faced mounting pressure as more women come forward with similar stories spanning decades. Barbara Bowman, Joan Tarshis, Janice Dickinson, and Tamara Green have all described experiences of being drugged and assaulted by Cosby during the 1960s–1980s. None of these cases resulted in criminal convictions due to expired statutes of limitations. Yet the cultural fallout has been swift: Netflix postponed his comedy special, NBC scrapped a new series, TV Land halted reruns of The Cosby Show, and multiple talk show appearances were canceled. In a brief November 6 interview with the Associated Press, Cosby declined to comment, asking that the segment not be aired. His wife, Camille, stood silently beside him.

Men hun sier ingen mengde penger kunne slette traumet. Serignese er en av de 13 kvinnene som kom frem som 'Jane Does' i Andrea Constands sivile klage mot Cosby fra 2006, som endte i en avtale. Hun krever nå en unnskyldning: 'Du skylder meg en forklaring. Jeg vil at du skal innrømme at det du gjorde var galt.' Men den kulturelle konsekvensen har vært rask: Netflix skjøv opp komediespesialet hans, NBC kansellerte et nytt prosjekt, TV Land stoppet gjenopptak av The Cosby Show, og flere opptredener på talkshow ble kansellert. article_content: Almost a year after construction began on the redevelopment of Food Street in VV Puram, Bengaluru, the project remains incomplete. The road is partially paved, footpaths are cracked, and a constant cloud of dust lingers — turning the city’s beloved street food hub into a nearly deserted stretch. Even loyal patrons have stopped coming, and vendors report devastating losses. Originally slated for completion in September 2024, the project was expected to reopen on August 15. But with work still ongoing, officials withdrew that promise. Many stalls have closed voluntarily — traders estimate a 40% drop in business. Shine Varghese, 21, visited the street after a year away, hoping to relive past memories of masala papads and bustling crowds. Instead, he found an eerily quiet street at 7:30 p.m. — a far cry from the packed lanes he remembered. 'I don’t think I’ll come back until this is finished,' he told TOI. Jitendra Singhal, who has sold sweets here since 2007, described the dilemma: 'We can’t shut down — but we can’t really operate either.' Regulars are gone, and new visitors leave after seeing the mess. 'The biggest issue? No parking,' he said. Kiran Kumar, an ice cream vendor for four years, now opens only at 4 p.m. instead of 11 a.m. 'Dust settles on our food. I pay rent and wages for ten employees — but there’s barely any income,' he shared. The VV Puram Street Vendors’ Association, representing 42 shops along a 400-meter stretch, calls this crisis the 'third wave of coronavirus.' 'We were finally recovering — then this hit us again,' said president Mani Kanta Gupta. 'We just want the work done.' A BBMP official acknowledged the delay, blaming a contractor strike over unpaid dues. 'This time, we’ll finish the footpaths and everything else,' he assured TOI. Trade activist Sajjan Raj Mehta echoed vendor concerns, urging authorities to prioritize completion across similar congested areas.

Selv loyale kunder har sluttet å komme, og selgere rapporterer alvorlige tap. Opprinnelig planlagt ferdig i september 2024, skulle prosjektet gjenåpnes 15. august. Men med arbeidet fortsatt pågående, trakk myndighetene tilbake dette løftet. Mange stander har valgt å stenge ned frivillig — handlere estimerer et 40 prosent tilbakegang i inntekter. Shine Varghese, 21, besøkte gaten etter et år borte, håpet på å gjenoppleve gamle minner om masala papads og travle menneskemengder. Istedenfor fant han en tyst gate kl. 19:30 — langt unna de travle gatekjedene han husket. 'Jeg tror ikke jeg vil komme tilbake før dette er ferdig,' sa han til TOI. Jitendra Singhal, som har solgt søtsaker her siden 2007, beskrev dilemmaet: 'Vi kan ikke stenge ned — men vi kan heller ikke virkelig drive.' Vanlige kunder er borte, og nye besøkende går vekk etter å ha sett tilstanden. 'Det største problemet? Ingen parkering,' sa han. 'Vi var akkurat begynt å komme oss igjen — da traff oss dette igjen,' sa president Mani Kanta Gupta. 'Vi vil bare ha arbeidet ferdig.' En BBMP-funksjonær bekreftet forsinkelsen og la skylden på en kontraktørstreik på grunn av ubetalte regninger. 'Denne gangen vil vi ferdigstille fotgjengerveiene og alt annet,' sa han til TOI. article_content: NEW DELHI, India (CNN) — While many today understand the scientific explanation for a solar eclipse, the phenomenon remains steeped in tradition—and sometimes suspicion—in predominantly Hindu India. At the Gujarat Council of Science City, visitors test 'sky-watching telescopes' in preparation for the event. The exceptionally long solar eclipse set to cross half the planet on Wednesday will be visible to nearly the entire populations of China and India. For beggars in India, the eclipse means an extra day of receiving alms and food. Sandeep Jaggi, 34, says his neighborhood’s panhandler typically visits on Tuesdays, Saturdays, and during new and full moons. Because many observe the eclipse with alms-giving, prayers, and ritual bathing, Jaggi ensures he’s ready: 'It’s a family tradition—I follow it.' He fills the man’s steel pail with mustard oil and coins, and drapes lentils across his worn sash. For others, however, the eclipse carries a darker meaning. Pregnant women often avoid giving birth during the event. 'None of the expectant mothers under my care are willing to deliver on Wednesday,' said Dr. Shivani Sachdev Gour, a gynecologist at Fortis La Femme Hospital in New Delhi. Even critically ill patients have expressed reluctance to remain in hospitals on eclipse day. Indian astrologers advise expectant mothers to stay indoors. 'It may not physically harm the baby, but it could influence the child’s overall personality,' said R.K. Sharma, a remedial astrologer. He explains that during an eclipse, the sun god is temporarily weakened by an encounter with the celestial entity Rahu, disrupting cosmic balance. 'Bathing in holy rivers and ponds during this time helps protect health and fosters positivity and inner strength,' he added. About 1.5 million people are expected at Brahmsarovar, a sacred pond in northern India believed to be the pool of the god Brahma. 'They offer prayers to the sun god and take holy dips during an eclipse,' said Ashok Kumar Bansal, sub-divisional magistrate of Kurukshetra, an ancient Hindu city. But the century’s longest total solar eclipse isn’t just about myth—it’s also business. Indian travel companies are capitalizing on the event. Cox and Kings India has chartered a flight for eclipse enthusiasts bound for Bihar, one of the best viewing locations. The plane will hover over Gaya and return to New Delhi the same day, according to company spokesperson Thomas C. Thottathil. Passengers can choose between 'sunside' seats—facing the eclipse—for around $1,640, or 'earthside' seats for about $610. 'It’s completely sold out,' he said.
translated_content: NEW DELHI, India (CNN) — Mens de fleste i dag forstår den vitenskapelige forklaringen på en solformørkelse, forblir fenomenet dypt rotet i tradisjon—og noen ganger mistro—i hovedsakelig hinduistisk India. Ved Gujarat Council of Science City tester besøkende 'himmelskue-teleskoper' for å forberede seg på hendelsen. Den eksepsjonelt lange solformørkelsen som vil krysse halvparten av planeten onsdag vil være synlig for nesten hele befolkningen i Kina og India. For bedrere i India betyr formørkelsen en ekstra dag med å motta gavegaver og mat. Sandeep Jaggi, 34, sier at den lokale bedreren i hans nabolag vanligvis kommer tirsdager, lørdager og ved ny- og fullmåne. Fordi mange observerer formørkelsen med gavegivning, bønner og rituell badelse, er Jaggi forberedt: 'Det er en familietradisjon—jeg følger den.' Han fyller mannens stålspann med mosterolje og mynter, og legger lin til hans slappe skjorte. For andre har formørkelsen en mørkere betydning. Gravid kvinner unngår ofte å føde under denne tiden. 'Ingen av de gravide under min omsorg vil føde onsdag,' sa doktor Shivani Sachdev Gour, gynekolog ved Fortis La Femme-sykehus i New Delhi. Selv kritisk syke pasienter har uttrykt uvilje til å bli på sykehus på formørkelsesdagen. Indiske astrologer råder gravide kvinner til å holde seg inne. 'Det kan ikke skade barnet fysisk, men det kan påvirke barnets generelle personlighet,' sa R.K. Sharma, en terapeutisk astrolog. Han forklarer at under en solformørkelse svekkes solguden midlertidig av en konfrontasjon med det himmelske vesenet Rahu, og dette forstyrrer kosmisk balanse. 'Badelse i hellige elver og dammer under denne tiden hjelper til med å beskytte helsen og fremme positivitet og indre styrke,' sa han. Omtrent 1,5 millioner mennesker forventes på Brahmsarovar, et helligt vann i nord-India som anses å være Brahma-gudens basseng. 'De bønner til solguden og tar hellige bad under en solformørkelse,' sa Ashok Kumar Bansal, underavdelingsleder i Kurukshetra, en gammel hinduistisk by. Men den lengste totale solformørkelsen i århundret handler ikke bare om myter—det er også forretningsmuligheter. Indiske reisebyråer utnytter hendelsen. Cox and Kings India har charteret et fly for solformørkelsesentusiaster til Bihar, en av de beste stedene for å se hendelsen. Flyet vil sirkle over Gaya og returnere til New Delhi samme dag, ifølge selskapets talesperson Thomas C. Thottathil. Passasjerer kan velge mellom 'sol-side' seter—vendt mot formørkelsen—for rundt 1.640 dollar, eller 'jord-side' seter for rundt 610 dollar. 'Det er fullt booket,' sa han.

article_content: A London mother of two, Maria Malone-Guerbaa, has the extraordinary ability to transform her face into nearly any person or creature using only makeup. In support of England’s first match at the World Cup, she painted herself to resemble football legends Wayne Rooney and Daniel Sturridge — all without prosthetics. Using only face paints and tiny brushes, Maria creates astonishingly lifelike portraits of icons such as Nelson Mandela, Angelina Jolie as Maleficent, Morgan Freeman, and even Queen Elizabeth II. Her technique involves meticulous layering and shading, often taking up to four hours per design. After putting her artistic passion on hold following the birth of her children, Sophia (12) and Adam (10), Maria reignited her craft at age 33 by enrolling in Christine Blundell’s makeup academy in Camden. She began painting her own face to keep her kids engaged — a simple idea that soon went viral on Facebook. Her unique style — entirely prosthetic-free — caught the attention of the global makeup community. She was invited to speak at the International Make-Up Artist Trade Show (IMATS) and the Fabiac Face & Body Art International Event in Miami in 2015. Maria, originally from Limerick, moved to London after realizing there were no specialized training programs in Ireland for face and body art. She met her husband Billy shortly after arriving, and together they opened a series of cafés. While raising her children, she balanced business with art — eventually turning her hobby into a profession. Her work has appeared in major productions including The City of Angels at the Barbican, BBC’s Switch, and Channel 4’s Horrible Histories — where she famously created a decapitated look for Katherine Howard. Sponsored by Superstar Face Paints and Face Paint UK, Maria now shares her methods through YouTube tutorials and live demonstrations. She plans to teach workshops in the UK and the Netherlands, and is preparing for her appearance at Fabiac in Miami. Though she dreams of working behind the scenes in Hollywood, Maria has chosen to remain close to her children, avoiding long-term film shoots. 'I wouldn’t leave them for months,' she says. 'I’d rather teach and inspire locally.' Her goal? To be a respected educator in the makeup world — not just a performer. 'I want to do it the right way,' she says. 'And if I can show people that you don’t need prosthetics to create magic… then I’ve done something special.'

For å støtte Englands første kamp i VM, malte hun seg selv som fotballstjernene Wayne Rooney og Daniel Sturridge — uten noen prostetikk. Ved å bruke bare ansiktsfarger og små pensler skaper Maria utrolig livsnære portretter av ikoner som Nelson Mandela, Angelina Jolie som Maleficent, Morgan Freeman og selv Dronning Elizabeth II. Hennes teknikk innebærer nøyaktig lagvising og skyggelegging, og tar ofte opptil fire timer per design. Etter å ha lagt sin kunstneriske lidenskap på hylla etter fødselen av barna sine, Sophia (12) og Adam (10), gjenoppdaget Maria sin lidenskap ved 33 år da hun tok del i Christine Blundells make-up-akademi i Camden. Hun begynte å male sitt eget ansikt for å holde barna sine opptatt — en enkel idé som snart gikk vilt viral på Facebook. Hennes unike stil — helt uten prostetikk — tok oppmerksomheten til det globale make-up-fellesskapet. Hun ble invitert til å snakke på International Make-Up Artist Trade Show (IMATS) og Fabiac Face & Body Art International Event i Miami i 2015. Maria, opprinnelig fra Limerick, flyttet til London etter å ha oppdaget at det ikke fantes noen spesialiserte utdanningsprogrammer i Irland for ansikts- og kroppsmaling. Hun møtte sin mann Billy kort tid etter ankomsten, og sammen åpnet de en rekke kaféer. Mens hun oppdro barna sine, balanserte hun næringsvirksomhet med kunst — og endte opp med å gjøre sin hobby til et yrke. Hennes arbeid har dukket opp i store produksjoner som The City of Angels på Barbican, BBCs Switch og Channel 4s Horrible Histories — der hun berømt skapte et avhovet utseende for Katherine Howard. Sponsret av Superstar Face Paints og Face Paint UK, deler Maria nå sine metoder gjennom YouTube-tutorials og live-demonstrasjoner. Hun planlegger å undervise i workshopper i Storbritannia og Nederland, og forbereder seg på opptrådelsen sin ved Fabiac i Miami. Selv om hun drømmer om å jobbe bak kulisserne i Hollywood, har Maria valgt å forbli nær sine barn og unngå lengre filmprosjekter. 'Jeg vil ikke forlate dem i måneder,' sier hun. 'Jeg foretrekker å undervise og inspirere lokalt.' Hennes mål? Å bli en respektert lærer i make-up-verdenen — ikke bare en fremfører. 'Jeg vil gjøre det på riktig måte,' sier hun. 'Og hvis jeg kan vise folk at du ikke trenger prostetikk for å skape magi… så har jeg gjort noe spesielt.'

article_content: By Dan Bloom. PUBLISHED: 13:11 EST, 9 November 2013. | UPDATED: 02:48 EST, 11 November 2013. Ambrose Murray, 22, has been jailed for supplying Class A drugs and theft after his father’s fentanyl pain patches led to the fatal overdose of 20-year-old Josh Makin. Murray, a former top student, stole opioid skin patches from his father, John, who suffers from chronic back pain, and sold them at a house party in Altrincham, Greater Manchester. At the party, Josh Makin — who was drinking, using drugs, and playing video games — was given the patches and told they were strong painkillers meant for skin application. After Murray left, Josh swallowed one instead of applying it to his skin. The patch contained fentanyl — a powerful synthetic opioid 50 to 100 times stronger than morphine. Swallowing it delivered approximately 150 times the intended dose, causing respiratory failure and death overnight. His girlfriend discovered him dead beside her the following afternoon. Manchester’s Minshull Street Crown Court heard Murray had been stealing the patches for months, posting on Facebook: 'Does anyone there want to buy fents?' — slang for fentanyl. Although the court ruled Murray’s actions did not directly cause Josh’s death — due to the improper ingestion — he was sentenced to 18 months in prison for supplying controlled substances and theft. Defense lawyer Lisa Judge described Murray as a once-high-achieving student who struggled academically and descended into addiction. Judge Mushtaq Khokhar stated: 'Drugs are a plague on this society.' Josh’s mother, Louise, told the Manchester Evening News: 'No sentence could bring him back. We just want this to be a warning: when you experiment with drugs, you are stepping into the unknown.' Fentanyl patches are designed to release medication slowly over 72 hours. Misuse has led to multiple cases of addiction, including that of Bob Rees, 53, from Pontypridd, Wales, who described his dependency as comparable to heroin addiction.

article_content: By Lizzie Edmonds. In the run-up to India’s next general election, Zionnghaka Chana — a polygamist sect leader in Mizoram — has become a focal point for politicians seeking votes. With 39 wives and 127 children and grandchildren, his family represents a bloc of more than 160 eligible voters who cast ballots as one. Chana, who lives with his extended family in a 100-room, four-story home in Baktawng village, Aizawl, told reporters: 'In the final days before the election, we’ve seen a rush of politicians coming to meet us. Winning margins here are razor-thin — so even 100 votes matter.' One of his wives, Rinkmini, confirmed: 'When we vote, we all vote for the same candidate. That means over 160 votes come from our family alone.' Chana, whose grandfather founded the sect in the 1930s, said his priority is clean governance and state development — not personal gain. 'All we want is good leadership for the whole state, not favors for our family,' he said. The sect, which follows Christian teachings, has approximately 1,700 members across four generations. Many engage in woodworking and pottery. Though the sect permits polygamy, mainstream Presbyterian churches in Mizoram reject it. Family life is highly structured. The eldest wife, Zathiangi, 69, manages daily schedules for chores, including meal preparation — which can involve 30 chickens, 132 pounds of potatoes, and up to 220 pounds of rice per meal. The compound includes a school, playground, carpentry workshops, piggeries, poultry farms, and a large vegetable garden. Despite the size of the home, some wives still sleep in shared dormitories. Chana, 67, maintains a rotation system for marital visits, with younger wives living closer to his quarters. He is described by his wife Rinkmini, 35, as 'the most important person in the house — and the most handsome in the village.' Mizoram is voting in the fourth of nine stages in India’s 2024 general election. The Election Commission rescheduled polling after disputes over whether displaced tribal communities could vote from refugee camps. Mizoram accounts for less than 1% of India’s 814 million voters. Voting concludes May 12; results are expected May 16.

Det betyr over 160 stemmer fra vår familie alene.' Chana, hvis bestefar grunnla sekten i 1930-årene, sa at hans prioritet er ren styring og statlig utvikling — ikke personlig gevinst. 'Alt vi vil ha er god ledelse for hele staten, ikke favoriser for vår familie,' sa han. Sekten, som følger kristelige læren, har omtrent 1.700 medlemmer over fire generasjoner. Mange jobber med tresliperi og keramikk. Selv om sekten tillater polygami, forkaster de dominerende presbyterianske kirker i Mizoram det. Familieleven er høyst strukturert. Den eldste hustruen, Zathiangi, 69, leder daglige skjemaer for hjelp, inkludert matlaging — som kan involvere 30 høner, 60 kilo poteter og opp til 100 kilo ris per måltid. Stemmingen slutter 12. mai; resultatene forventes 16. mai.

article_content: In a case that has sparked widespread concern, two men who participated in the brutal sexual assault of a drunken woman in Preston have seen their sentences dramatically reduced. Rezgar Nouri, 27, and Mohammed Ibrahim, 24, were initially given indeterminate prison terms under a now-discontinued law meant to protect the public from those deemed 'dangerous'. But after an appeal hearing, three senior judges concluded there wasn’t enough proof to classify them as such. The woman, 24, had become separated from her friends late one night after a night out in Preston’s nightlife district. She was approached by Nouri, Ibrahim, and a third man, and taken to a nearby flat. There, she was repeatedly raped over several hours — one of the attackers reportedly laughed during the assault. When it ended, she fled the scene, only to return moments later when she realized she’d left her phone inside. That’s when Nouri attacked her again before throwing her out. She was found minutes later in severe emotional distress. Police were called immediately. Though both men admitted to rape in 2011, the Court of Appeal ruled that the original judge had misapplied the law by assuming they posed a continuing threat. Without sufficient evidence of future risk, the indeterminate sentence was unlawful. The men’s punishment has now been fixed at 12 years each — a term that allows for potential parole after serving half the sentence.

article_content: The biggest technology story of 2013 was also one of the biggest stories of the year—period. It had serious implications across the United States and around the world, and even six months later, its full impact was only beginning to unfold. In June, The Guardian published leaked documents from Edward Snowden, a contractor for the National Security Agency. These classified files revealed the existence of highly secretive government programs collecting vast amounts of data on Americans’ phone calls and internet activity. The scale of these programs triggered lawsuits, public protests, and a nationwide debate over the balance between privacy rights and national security.  Another major theme of the year was cybersecurity, marked by a series of high-profile hacking attacks targeting news outlets, major tech firms, and retail chains. Motivations varied: some breaches, like the one at Target, were financially driven, while others served as political statements or acts of espionage. Together, they underscored the fragility of digital security and personal privacy.  Established tech companies struggled to adapt. Microsoft pushed forward with its Windows 8 operating system and smartphones, even acquiring Nokia’s mobile division—the leading maker of Windows phones. Despite these efforts, sales remained weak, prompting the company to appoint a new CEO. A potential bright spot was the Xbox One, which competed with Sony’s PlayStation 4.  Apple, by contrast, maintained its momentum with modest but effective updates to the iPhone and iPad, introducing slimmer designs, faster performance, new color options, and a fingerprint scanner. Its most visible change came with iOS 7, which received a complete visual overhaul: flatter, simpler, and more modern.  Twitter went public and launched Vine, a short-form video app. Snapchat emerged from niche usage to mainstream popularity by making 'ephemeral' messaging a cultural phenomenon. Meanwhile, Bitcoin surged in value, fueling speculation about its future.  Wearable technology transitioned from hype to prototyping, with Google Glass and numerous smartwatches showing promise—but also revealing that design and social acceptance still lagged far behind technical capability. Many of 2013’s defining stories were merely previews of what was to come in 2014: Will face-mounted computers become socially acceptable? Will 3D-printed guns pose real threats? Can streaming platforms like Amazon and Netflix challenge traditional television?

Den hadde alvorlige konsekvenser i USA og rundt om i verden, og selv seks måneder senere var den fulle virkningen først begynnende å vise seg. I juni publiserte The Guardian lekkede dokumenter fra Edward Snowden, en kontraktør for Nasjonal Sikkerhetstjeneste. Disse klassifiserte filene avslørte eksistensen av svært hemmelige regjeringsprogrammer som samlet inn store mengder data om amerikaneres telefonoppringninger og internettaktivitet. Skalaen på disse programmene utløste rettsaker, offentlige protester og en nasjonal debatt om balansen mellom privatlivsrettigheter og nasjonal sikkerhet.  En annen viktig tema i året var cybersikkerhet, merket av en rekke høyt profilerte hackangrep som rettet seg mot nyhetsutgivelser, store teknologiselskaper og detailjister. Motivasjonene varierte: noen brudd, som det ved Target, var finansielt drevet, mens andre var politiske uttalelser eller spionasje. Sammen understreket de sårbarheten i digital sikkerhet og personlig privatliv.  Etaberte teknologiselskaper kjempet med å tilpasse seg. Microsoft satset videre på Windows 8-operativsystemet og smartphones, og kjøpte til og med Nokias mobilavdeling—ledende produsent av Windows-telefoner. Den mest synlige endringen kom med iOS 7, som fikk en komplett visuell omarbeidelse: flatere, enklere og mer moderne.  Twitter gikk offentlig og lanserte Vine, en kortform videos-app. Snapchat brøt ut fra nisjeforbruk til mainstream-popularitet ved å gjøre 'ephemeral' meldinger til et kulturelt fenomen. Mens Bitcoin steg i verdi og fremmet spekulasjoner om dens fremtid.  Bærbar teknologi gikk fra hype til prototyping, med Google Glass og mange smartur som viste potensial—men også avslørte at design og sosial aksept fortsatt var langt bak teknisk kapasitet. Mange av 2013s definierende historier var bare forsmak på hva som skulle komme i 2014: Vil datamaskiner som bæres på ansiktet bli sosialt akseptert? Vil 3D-printede våpen utgjøre reelle trusler? Kan streamingsplattformer som Amazon og Netflix utfordre tradisjonell TV?

article_content: Johnson & Johnson has voluntarily recalled one batch of Aveeno Baby Calming Comfort Lotion after the FDA detected bacterial levels slightly above permitted limits during testing. Although an independent laboratory’s subsequent analysis found no such exceedance, Johnson & Johnson chose to initiate the recall as a precautionary measure — not because any adverse reactions have been reported. The bacteria identified, coagulase-negative Staphylococci, is a common, naturally occurring microorganism found on human skin, in households, and in many personal care products at trace levels. The specific quantity detected was not disclosed. The affected lot, marked 0161LK, consists of approximately 2,200 tubes manufactured in Canada and distributed across nine U.S. states: Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Tennessee, and Texas. Consumers are not required to discard the product. According to company spokesperson Bonnie Jacobs, the recall targets retail inventory, and products already in homes pose no known health risk. Those seeking a refund may contact 877-298-2525.

De identifiserte bakteriene, coagulase-negative Staphylococci, er vanlige, naturlig forekommende mikroorganismer som finnes på menneskelig hud, i hjem og i mange personlige pleieprodukter i spor. article_content: A man who claimed he could not walk without excruciating pain was caught on camera racing a stock car, a court heard today. Peter Wilkes, 45, told authorities he was unable to get out of the bath due to a severe back injury — yet he was filmed competing in stock car races and pushing vehicles at Trent Raceway in Needwood, Staffordshire, between August 22 and October 17, 2010. Court proceedings revealed six separate video recordings of Wilkes driving his red stock car, numbered '39', with a banner reading 'Pete Wilkes' on the windshield. He participated in up to three races per day during fortnightly events. In the videos, Wilkes is seen climbing out of the car’s passenger window, walking freely around the track without a limp, laughing with friends, and purchasing food from vendors. He also uploaded these clips to YouTube, claiming they were filmed by his son. One clip shows him colliding with another car, spinning out, and then exiting the vehicle with apparent ease before walking normally. Wilkes had suffered spinal damage in a 1991 football accident, resulting in loss of sensation below his left knee. On his December 2008 DLA claim, he stated he could not walk on uneven ground without stumbling, could not bend over, and needed help dressing. During interviews with DWP officials in December 2010, Wilkes claimed he was 'permanently in severe discomfort' and that every step caused pain. He fraudulently received £4,439 in Disability Living Allowance between September 2009 and December 2010. At Burton Magistrates Court, Wilkes was found guilty of failing to notify the DWP of a change in circumstances affecting his eligibility. Magistrate Andrew Nelson acknowledged Wilkes’s original claim may have been legitimate but noted his condition had improved and he failed to update the DWP. Wilkes avoided jail after repaying the full amount using an inheritance. He was fined £300, ordered to pay a £15 victim surcharge, and £250 in court costs. Speaking outside court, Wilkes called the punishment 'completely unfair,' saying he had no income and would do it again to help his son, who now works as a mechanic thanks to the experience gained at the track.

Han fikk ulovlig utbetalt 4.439 britiske pund i Disability Living Allowance mellom september 2009 og desember 2010. Ved Burton Magistrates Court ble Wilkes funnet skyldig i ikke å varsle DWP om en endring i hans omstendigheter som påvirket retten til ytelser. Dommer Andrew Nelson anerkjente at Wilkes' opprinnelige søknaden kanskje var gyldig, men bemerket at hans tilstand hadde forbedret seg og at han ikke hadde varslet DWP. Wilkes unngikk fengsel etter å ha tilbakebetalt hele beløpet ved hjelp av en arv. Han ble dømt til en bot på 300 britiske pund, en tilleggsavgift på 15 britiske pund og 250 britiske pund i domstolskostnader. Utenfor domstolen sa Wilkes at straffen var 'fullstendig urettferdig', og at han ikke hadde noen inntekt og ville gjøre det igjen for å hjelpe sønnen, som nå jobber som mekaniker takket være erfaringen han fikk på banen.

article_content: Rostam Ahmadi, 23, was sentenced to indefinite detention under the Mental Health Act after pleading guilty to the manslaughter of Umesh Chaudhari, a 41-year-old father of two, in a brutal, unprovoked attack outside his home in Croydon, South London. Ahmadi, an illegal immigrant who initially claimed to be an Afghan refugee but later stated he was born in Iran in 1989, had been denied leave to remain in the UK in October 2010, and his asylum appeal was dismissed in February 2011. Despite being ordered to leave the country, he remained and committed a robbery on May 30, 2011, for which he was released on bail. On July 6, 2011, Ahmadi attacked Mr. Chaudhari with a brick just yards from his home on Dennett Road, striking him repeatedly on the head while his wife and children watched in horror. Neighbors intervened, restraining Ahmadi until police arrived. Mr. Chaudhari suffered multiple skull fractures and died the next day from traumatic brain injury. Mr. Chaudhari, who had immigrated to the UK from Nepal in 2003, worked 70 hours per week between a Tesco job in Addiscombe and a night shift at a restaurant in the City of London to support his family. His wife, Rekha Sah, described him as a devoted father, hardworking provider, and beloved member of the community. Ahmadi was diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia while in custody. Psychiatrists confirmed he was experiencing religiously motivated delusions, including statements such as, 'Do you know why I punched someone? Because of Allah and jihad.' Although he denied mental illness, evidence of self-harm and erratic behavior supported the diagnosis. Judge Richard Marks QC emphasized that Ahmadi’s actions were driven by severe mental illness, not malice, and stated: 'The particular tragedy of these events is compounded by the fact that you should not even have been in this country.' Ahmadi had prior convictions for battery, theft, and criminal damage. He pleaded guilty to manslaughter on grounds of diminished responsibility. The judge noted that Ahmadi was responding to psychiatric treatment but must be detained indefinitely to protect the public.

article_content: By Julian Gavaghan. PUBLISHED: 06:00 EST, 26 June 2012. | UPDATED: 06:05 EST, 26 June 2012. Call for action: Graham Aaronson QC warned that failing to stop aggressive tax avoidance could spark social unrest. There will be 'riots on the streets' if the government fails to tackle wealthy tax dodgers, said Graham Aaronson QC, the architect of new anti-avoidance rules. Aaronson, who recommended banning aggressive tax-reducing arrangements such as Jimmy Carr’s K2 scheme, said such practices are especially indefensible during times of austerity. The tax specialist barrister said learning about Carr’s K2 scheme — which allows participants to reduce their effective tax rate to around 1% — made his 'blood boil.' He argued that ensuring the wealthy cannot 'play fast and loose' with their duty to contribute to the nation is vital for public order. 'People on the street don't want these schemes to go ahead,' he told The Times. 'I feel very strongly that abusive tax schemes are antisocial and fuel the anger of ordinary people. The tents have been pitched at St Paul’s — and more riots are not far away if we don’t act.' Tax avoidance by individuals is estimated to cost the Treasury around £4.5 billion annually; corporations are believed to evade an additional £30.5 billion. To address this shortfall, Prime Minister David Cameron last year tasked Aaronson with determining whether Britain needed a General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR). In November, Aaronson — who says he pays roughly 50% tax — recommended such a rule, arguing it would strengthen HMRC’s enforcement powers without undermining the UK’s business competitiveness. In March, Chancellor George Osborne agreed a GAAR was necessary, and Treasury officials are now drafting legislation to enact it. However, Aaronson rejected a broad-spectrum law that would target all schemes, warning it could harm legitimate business activity. Instead, he proposed that only arrangements deemed 'unreasonable' on two levels should be caught by the new rules. Senior HMRC officials fear Aaronson’s proposal doesn’t go far enough. Pressure has mounted since it was revealed 10 days ago that comedian Jimmy Carr — along with 1,100 others — used a Jersey-based K2 scheme to shelter £3.5 million. Cameron called the scheme 'morally wrong.' Since then, it has emerged that Take That stars Gary Barlow, Howard Donald, and Mark Owen, along with their manager, invested £26 million in another avoidance arrangement. Olympic cyclist Chris Hoy denied allegations he avoided tax by taking loans through his own company. Additionally, 1,300 doctors are under investigation for suspected tax evasion. At the weekend, Chief Secretary to the Treasury Danny Alexander suggested cutting Britain’s £35 billion tax gap by a quarter could fund a 2p cut in the basic rate of income tax. However, officials warned that investigations into abusive avoidance have been hindered by a shortage of tax inspectors due to budget cuts. A backlog of 20,000 cases could take up to 38 years to resolve. Mounting frustration was amplified by a strike involving over 50,000 HMRC workers, protesting pay and pensions. The walkout will be followed by actions including an overtime ban. PCS General Secretary Mark Serwotka said: 'It is sickening to see millionaires in the Cabinet wringing their hands about the immorality of tax avoidance when it is their lack of political will that costs us tens of billions each year. The case for investing in public services — instead of austerity — has never been clearer. Yet the government plans to cut another 10,000 jobs from HMRC, letting wealthy tax dodgers off the hook and punishing the rest of us for a recession we didn’t cause.'

article_content: At 65, Roland Burton from Wisbech, Cambridgeshire, was living a life many would recognize: retired, inactive, and buried under junk food. His days revolved around the couch, chocolate bars, crisps, and endless sugary tea — until he realized he couldn’t chase his 14 grandchildren around without getting winded. That moment sparked a dramatic change. Inspired after watching a bodybuilding contest in Great Yarmouth, Roland decided to transform himself. He joined a gym, enlisted the help of his son Hal and trainer Paul, and committed to two-hour sessions five days a week. His diet? Steak, rice, and vegetables — no sweets, no carbs in the final stretch. It wasn’t glamorous, but it worked. Within six months, he’d lost 3 stone and 18 inches off his waist. By the time he stepped onto the stage at the Atlantis Arena for his first competition, he wasn’t just fit — he was shredded. Competing against younger, more experienced athletes, he took first place in the over-50 category. His wife, Margaret, was initially worried he’d hurt himself, but she soon became his biggest cheerleader — even helping him apply fake tan before the big night. When his chosen song, 'Rollin’' by Limp Bizkit, played, and he strutted across the stage, his entire family erupted in cheers. 'I never thought I’d win,' he says. 'But now? I’ve got a six-pack, and I feel like I’ve been given a second life.'

article_content: A young mother from West Yorkshire, Katherine Poxon, has been sentenced to over two years in prison for plotting with her lover to seriously injure her husband — a plan that collapsed due to its sheer clumsiness. Despite the gravity of the scheme, her husband, Steven Poxon, has chosen to forgive her and hopes to rebuild their life together once she is released. Katherine, 22, and her 44-year-old partner, Stephen Swallow, exchanged text messages urging violent action after Steven discovered their affair and threatened to seek custody of their young son. In one message, Katherine wrote: 'I hope you kill Stu, babe, then we can be happy.' Swallow, meanwhile, was spotted outside the family home, drinking from a can of lager, holding two knives and telling a neighbor he was 'off to stab Poxon.' Fortunately, the neighbor intervened and talked him down. Swallow had previously confided in his niece about his intention to kill Steven. The court heard that Katherine had no prior criminal record and was described by her lawyer as an immature, emotionally volatile young woman — not a cold-blooded planner. Swallow, who has a history of theft and violence linked to alcohol and depression, claimed he never intended to follow through, though he admitted carrying weapons multiple times. He later called Katherine 'twisted' and said she manipulated him with her anger over losing her child. Judge Geoffrey Marson QC noted the plot lacked any real planning or cunning. He sentenced Swallow to three years and Katherine to 27 months, acknowledging Steven’s forgiveness and Katherine’s youth. He also remarked that Swallow was lucky to have a family willing to take him in after prison. The case highlights how emotional turmoil, poor judgment, and toxic relationships can spiral into dangerous plots — even when those plots are far from well-executed. Yet, amid the chaos, one unexpected thread remains: a husband’s willingness to forgive.

Swallow, som har en historikk med tyveri og vold knyttet til alkohol og depresjon, påsto at han aldri hadde hensikt om å gjennomføre det, selv om han innrømmet å ha båret våpen flere ganger. article_content: Former TV-am presenter Mike Morris died after NHS staff failed to recognize warning signs of deterioration following bladder cancer surgery, an inquest has heard. Mr Morris, who rose to prominence alongside Lorraine Kelly and Anne Diamond on the breakfast show TV-am, was 66 when he died in October 2012. He had undergone surgery at East Surrey Hospital to address bleeding after bladder cancer treatment and was expected to recover fully. However, an inquest in Surrey heard that a series of failures by medical staff over several hours led to a cardiac arrest in the early hours of the morning. Medical witnesses testified that Mr Morris’s condition worsened without timely transfer to a high dependency unit. Coroner Karen Henderson stated: 'Mr Morris died from complications of necessary surgery when post-operative deterioration was not recognized and consequently went untreated.' His death was completely unexpected, and no family members were present when he passed away at 7:10 a.m. A week before his death, Mr Morris had been re-admitted after developing significant urinary bleeding and received five units of blood. An early warning system flagged critical declines in his vital signs—pulse, blood pressure, respiration, and heart rate—but staff failed to act. He suffered cardiac arrest at approximately 6:00 a.m. and died at 7:10 a.m. Gregory Armon-Jones, married to Mr Morris’s daughter Helen, said the family was shocked: 'He had various health problems, including heart issues, but his cancer was low-grade and considered under control.' 'He was a larger-than-life character,' Armon-Jones added. 'His whole life revolved around his family—especially his two daughters, Helen and Sarah, and his grandchildren.' Dr. Des Holden, medical director at Surrey & Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust, acknowledged that care after the emergency surgery fell below expected standards. The trust apologized to the family and implemented improvements: expanded ICU and HDU capacity, revised staffing models, and enhanced outreach team protocols. No staff were disciplined, as investigations concluded all involved were acting in good faith. Morris, known for his distinctive moustache, joined TV-am as a sports presenter and became host of Good Morning Britain in 1987, remaining until 1992. He also conducted a world-exclusive interview with Nelson Mandela upon his release from prison.

Han hadde gjennomgått en operasjon ved East Surrey Hospital for å stoppe blødning etter behandling for blærekreft og forventet å gjenopprette seg fullt ut. En rettssak i Surrey hørte at en rekke svik fra medisinsk personale over flere timer førte til hjertestop i de tidlige morgentimene. Medisinske vitner testifiserte at Herr Morris’ tilstand forverret seg uten rask overføring til en intensivavdeling. Dommer Karen Henderson sa: 'Mr Morris døde av komplikasjoner fra nødvendig kirurgi da postoperativ forverring ikke ble gjenkjent og dermed ikke ble behandlet.' Døden var helt uventet, og ingen familiemedlemmer var til stede da han døde klokken 7:10. En uke før sin død hadde Herr Morris blitt innlagt igjen etter å ha utviklet betydelig urinblødning og mottatt fem enheter blod. Et tidlig advarselssystem registrerte kritiske nedganger i hans viktige livstegn—puls, blodtrykk, pustefrekvens og hjertefrekvens—men personale tok ikke handling. Tjenesten beklaget seg hos familien og innførte forbedringer: økt kapasitet i ICU og HDU, endrede stillingsmodeller og forbedret arbeidsmønstre for utredningslagene. Ingen ansatte ble disiplinert, ettersom undersøkelser konkluderte med at alle involverte handlet i god tro. Morris, kjent for sitt tydelige skjegg, begynte på TV-am som sportskommentator og ble vert for Good Morning Britain i 1987, og ble ved tjenesten til 1992. Han gjennomførte også et verdenseksklusivt intervju med Nelson Mandela etter hans frigivelse fra fengsel.
