article_content: While the summer transfer window in England is officially closed, a number of high-caliber players remain available on free transfers — offering clubs smart, low-risk opportunities to strengthen their squads. With the Premier League season underway, several teams are quietly scouting talent beyond the usual market. Arsenal, for example, still have two slots open for non-homegrown players in their 25-man squad, and manager Arsène Wenger could consider veteran defender Mario Yepes. At 38, Yepes captained Colombia to the World Cup quarter-finals, playing every minute — proof he still performs at the highest level. Goalkeeper Victor Valdes, 32, is another compelling option. After 14 years at Barcelona — where he won six La Liga titles and three Champions Leagues — he’s currently recovering from a knee injury. Though a medical at Monaco failed and he won’t be match-fit until December, Liverpool are reportedly interested in a short-term deal. The legendary Ronaldinho, 34, remains unsigned since leaving Atlético Mineiro in July. Despite his age, his flair and charisma could make for a memorable final chapter in the Premier League. Links to Benfica and the Indian Super League persist, but football fans everywhere still hope to see his magic in England one last time. Other notable names include Hugo Almeida, a proven 30-year-old striker with 25 goals in three seasons at Besiktas, attracting interest from Leicester, West Ham, Sunderland, and Hull. Diego Lugano, 33, offers defensive grit after a brief stint at West Brom and World Cup appearances for Uruguay. Brazilian forwards Jonas and Nilmar bring proven scoring records — Jonas netted a rapid hat-trick last season, while Nilmar dazzled at Villarreal and earned 23 caps for Brazil. Right-back Anthony Reveillere, a five-time Ligue 1 champion with Lyon, and veteran French winger Florent Malouda, with over 150 Premier League appearances for Chelsea, are both ready to contribute immediately. Experienced campaigners like Joseph Yobo, George McCartney, and Matthew Etherington offer leadership and familiarity with English football, while Jermaine Pennant — seeking to rebuild his career after personal struggles — and goalkeeper Tomasz Kuszczak are also viable options. Even Park Chu-Young, who never started a league game for Arsenal during his three-year stint, remains eligible at 29 and could be a surprise hit for a newly promoted side given his international goal record. And that’s not all — names like Abdoulaye Faye, Robert Earnshaw, and Chris Eagles remain unsigned. For the complete list of free agents, visit the PFA’s official website.

article_content: On his 58th birthday, Bollywood legend Shah Rukh Khan was showered with love from fans, family, and fellow celebrities. Early Thursday morning, hundreds gathered outside his iconic Mumbai home, Mannat, hoping for a glimpse of the actor known not just as a star—but as a symbol of emotion for millions. His daughter, Suhana Khan, expressed her affection simply yet powerfully on Instagram Stories, posting two nostalgic photos of her father with the caption: 'Love you the most...'—a quiet moment that resonated more than any grand gesture. Farah Khan, who directed SRK in hits like 'Main Hoon Na' and 'Om Shanti Om', shared a video of cheering fans outside Mannat, writing: 'Can you feel the LOVVVVV tonight?! Happy birthday @iamsrk ♥️ #kingoftheworld.' Her post captured the electric energy surrounding his celebration. Even without sharing a film set, Ajay Devgn joined the tributes, reposting a clip from 'Jawan' with a playful nod: 'Here’s to another year of being Jawan—and fabulous! Happy birthday!' Their bond, forged through a decades-old Vimal pan masala ad, still shines. Director Kunal Kohli offered perhaps the most thoughtful tribute, responding to a tweet from SRK thanking fans. He wrote: 'It’s his humility, his quiet respect for women, his devotion to family—that’s why he keeps rising. After every fall, he comes back like a phoenix. @iamsrk isn’t just a star. He’s one of a kind.' Looking ahead, SRK will soon be seen in 'Dunki', a social comedy-drama directed by Rajkumar Hirani and co-starring Taapsee Pannu, set to release soon.

article_content: Before England faces Uruguay in a pivotal Group D showdown in São Paulo, they’d be wise to study the stunning upset from Saturday night. Ranked seventh in the world, Uruguay crumbled 3-1 against underdog Costa Rica — a result that sent shockwaves through the tournament. Coach Oscar Tabarez didn’t sugarcoat it: his team’s defense was sloppy, especially on set pieces, and they lost control of the midfield entirely after taking an early lead. 'We gave away space, and they punished us,' he admitted. 'As coach, I’m responsible.' To make matters worse, defender Maxi Pereira was sent off in stoppage time for a reckless ankle tackle on Joel Campbell, a young forward on loan from Arsenal. It wasn’t just a red card — it was a symbol of Uruguay’s unraveling composure. Meanwhile, Luis Suárez, their talismanic striker, looked far from 100% on the bench. Though not fully fit, he’s all but guaranteed to start against England — without him, Uruguay’s attack loses its edge. On the other side, Costa Rica is riding high. Their unity, energy, and belief are palpable. Campbell, just 21, delivered a standout performance and now has a personal mission: impress Arsenal enough to earn a permanent return. Assistant coach Paulo Wanchope made it clear: 'If he wants to go back to Arsenal, he needs to keep performing — next up, Italy, then England.' For England, the message is loud and clear: Uruguay’s set-piece vulnerabilities are a gift. Steven Gerrard will likely spend the entire week perfecting corners and free kicks. With discipline problems and a shaky defense, Uruguay may be more vulnerable than their reputation suggests. But don’t count them out — Suárez on his day can change everything.

article_content: Police in Clarksville, Tennessee, arrested 35-year-old Kristen Hines — also known as Kristen Rhonda Bible — for allegedly faking a cancer diagnosis to collect donations. According to court documents, Hines forged signatures from physicians at the Gateway-Vanderbilt Cancer Treatment Center and used these fake medical records on a Facebook page to portray herself as a cancer survivor. She shared images of herself with a shaved head and appealed for financial help, successfully raising more than $200 through online appeals and community events. One benefit event was held in mid-August at the Warehouse Bar and Grill, as reported by the Clarksville Leaf-Chronicle. A second fundraiser, the 'Chickin 'n' Pickin Cancer Benefit' organized by the Montgomery County Conservation Club, was scheduled for September 27 but canceled after her arrest. The scheme unraveled when staff at the cancer center received multiple calls from well-meaning donors trying to contribute to Hines’ nonexistent account. One doctor confirmed Hines had never been a patient there and reported the forged documents to authorities. Hines has a documented history of financial crimes, including 21 counts of forgery, two counts of identity theft, and one count of theft exceeding $10,000 — all from earlier in July. In a separate case, an elderly couple accused her of stealing $16,000 from their debit card while pretending to be their caregiver.

Ifølge domstoldokumenter falsifiserte Hines signaturer fra legene ved Gateway-Vanderbilt Cancer Treatment Center og brukte disse falske medisinske dokumentene på en Facebook-side for å fremstå som en kreftoverlevende. Hun delte bilder av seg selv med skallet hode og ba om finansiell hjelp, og samlet inn mer enn 200 dollar gjennom online-apeller og fellesskapsarrangementer. Et gavnarrangement ble holdt i midten av august på Warehouse Bar and Grill, ifølge Clarksville Leaf-Chronicle. Et annet arrangement, 'Chickin 'n' Pickin Cancer Benefit', arrangert av Montgomery County Conservation Club, var planlagt for 27. september, men ble kansellert etter hennes arrestasjon. Skjemaet ble avslørt da ansatte ved kreftsentret mottok flere oppringninger fra velmenende donatorer som forsøkte å donere til Hines' ikke-eksisterende konto. En lege bekreftet at hun aldri hadde vært pasient der og meldte de falsifiserte dokumentene til politiet. Hines har et dokumentert historikk med økonomiske forbrytelser, inkludert 21 anklager om falsifisering, to anklager om identitetsstyrt og én anklage om stjeling over 10.000 dollar — alle fra tidlig i juli. I et separat tilfelle ble hun beskyldt av et eldre par for å ha stjålt 16.000 dollar fra deres debetkort mens hun pretenderte å være deres omsorgsperson.

article_content: WASHINGTON (CNN) — When gunfire erupted at the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum last week, security officers Harry Weeks and Jason McCuiston were thrust into a nightmare. 'I would say it was surreal — neither of us could believe what was happening,' Weeks told CNN in his first national televised interview since the June 10 shooting. 'I just heard ‘pop, pop’ — and it felt unreal.' McCuiston added, 'It wasn’t normal. You knew something was terribly wrong.' White supremacist James von Brunn, 88, allegedly entered the museum and opened fire with a rifle, fatally shooting security officer Stephen Johns in the chest. Despite their shock, Weeks and McCuiston quickly regained composure, drew their weapons, and returned fire, likely preventing greater loss of life. Weeks, a former Washington, D.C., police officer who had fired his weapon in the line of duty 25 years prior, said nothing compared to this moment. 'This was terrible,' he whispered. 'This was worse. ... We lost Officer Johns.' Johns, a 6-foot-6-inch, 300-pound gentle giant, was known for his warm smile and unwavering friendliness. 'You’d never know he’d ever had a bad day,' McCuiston recalled. His teenage son told WUSA-TV, 'My dad was my hero.' Watching the clip, McCuiston broke down in tears. 'First thing I thought about? I have an 11-year-old.' In the moments before their CNN interview, both officers attended a joint grief counseling session. They acknowledge they’re still struggling emotionally. Though they believe von Brunn will survive and face trial, they’ve declined to discuss specifics of the shootout to avoid compromising the investigation. Instead, they chose to honor Johns — sharing stories of his character and urging the public to remember him. 'Let’s all remember Officer Johns and his family,' Weeks said. 'He did his job. He was where he was supposed to be. And his family paid the price.' When asked if they were heroes, both officers deflected. 'We chose this job,' McCuiston said. 'It’s the same as a firefighter running into a burning building — that’s their job. We didn’t do anything extraordinary.' Johns’ funeral has been moved to a larger church in the Washington area to accommodate mourners. The museum will remain closed for much of the day so colleagues can pay their respects. 'Death is one of the worst things,' McCuiston said. 'But time will heal. We’ll carry his memory — and never forget what a wonderful man he was.'
translated_content: WASHINGTON (CNN) — Da skuddene gikk av ved USAs Holocaustminnesenter i fjor, ble sikkerhetsvaktene Harry Weeks og Jason McCuiston kastet inn i en mareritt. 'Jeg vil si det var surrealt – ingen av oss kunne tro hva som skjedde,' sa Weeks til CNN i hans første nasjonale TV-intervju siden skytingen den 10. juni. 'Jeg hørte bare “pap, pap” – og det føltes urkelig.' McCuiston la til: 'Det var ikke normalt. Du visste at noe var veldig galt.' Hvit overlegenhetstilhenger James von Brunn, 88, skal ha trådt inn på museet og åpnet ild med et gevær og drept sikkerhetsvakt Stephen Johns i brystet. Trots deres sjokk fikk Weeks og McCuiston tak i seg selv, trakk våpnene sine og returnerte ild, sannsynligvis forhindret større tap. Weeks, en tidligere politibetjent fra Washington, D.C., som hadde skutt i tjeneste for 25 år siden, sa ingenting sammenlignet med dette øyeblikket. 'Dette var fryktelig,' hvisket han. 'Dette var verre. ... Vi mistet vakt Johns.' Johns, en 198 cm høy, 136 kg tung 'blid jævel', var kjent for sitt varme smil og uavbrutte vennlighet. 'Du ville aldri ha tenkt at han noen gang hadde hatt en dårlig dag,' sa McCuiston. Hans tenåringsunge sønn fortalte WUSA-TV: 'Min far var min helt.' Når han så klippet, brøt McCuiston i gråt. 'Det første jeg tenkte på? Jeg har en 11-åring.' I øyeblikkene før intervjuet med CNN besøkte begge offiserene en felles sorgterapi. De anerkjenner at de fremdeles kjemper med følelsene sine. Selv om de tror von Brunn vil overleve og stilles for retten, har de avslått å diskutere detaljer om skytingen for å unngå å forstyrre etterforskningen. I stedet valgte de å hedre Johns – dele historier om hans karakter og oppfordre offentligheten til å huske ham. 'La oss alle huske vakt Johns og familien hans,' sa Weeks. 'Han gjorde sin jobb. Han var der han skulle være. Og familien betalte prisen.' Da de ble spurt om de var helter, avviste begge offiserene det. 'Vi valgte denne jobben,' sa McCuiston. 'Det er det samme som en brannmann som løper inn i et brennende bygg – det er hans jobb. Vi gjorde ikke noe ekstraordinært.' Johns' begravelse er flyttet til en større kirke i området for å romme alle som ønsker å delta. Museet vil være stengt de fleste timene dagen for at kollegaene skal kunne delta. 'Død er en av de verste tingene,' sa McCuiston. 'Men tid vil helbrede. Vi vil bære minnet hans – og aldri glemme hvor fantastisk en mann han var.'

article_content: On Monday, the Indian rupee declined by 9 paise to settle at a record low of 83.35 against the US dollar, mirroring a negative trend in domestic equities and sustained foreign fund outflows, according to forex traders. At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 83.25 and closed at 83.35, marking a 9-paise drop from its previous close of 83.26 on Friday. This surpassed its earlier 2023 low of 83.33, recorded on November 13. Meanwhile, the US dollar index edged down 0.42% to 103.48, while Brent crude futures climbed 0.66% to $81.14 per barrel. Domestically, the Sensex fell 139.58 points (0.21%) to 65,655.15, and the Nifty dropped 37.80 points (0.19%) to 19,694.00. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) net sold shares worth ₹477.76 crore on Friday, exchange data showed. According to the Reserve Bank of India, India’s foreign exchange reserves decreased by $462 million to $590.321 billion for the week ended November 10, reversing last week’s gain of $4.672 billion. Despite a surge in IPO activity—with five new issues totaling ₹7,400 crore opening for subscription this week—finance companies that traditionally fund IPO bidders are showing muted interest. In a major leadership shift, OpenAI co-founder Sam Altman is joining Microsoft to lead a new AI research division, while former Twitch CEO Emmett Shear has been appointed interim CEO of OpenAI. Commercial vehicle sales in India are projected to reach an all-time high in FY24, driving record revenues for manufacturers including Tata Motors, Ashok Leyland, and VE Commercial Vehicles.

article_content: In early October 2012, 20-year-old University of Tennessee student Alexander P. Broughton was rushed to the hospital after a fraternity party left him unconscious with a blood alcohol level of 0.448%—nearly six times the legal driving limit—and serious rectal trauma. Police initially claimed he had been subjected to an alcohol enema, commonly referred to as 'butt-chugging,' based on statements from a fraternity member and physical evidence—including empty wine boxes—at the scene. But Broughton has strongly denied the allegation, calling it 'the most gross idea I have ever heard.' He insists that as a practicing Christian, he would never violate his body in such a way, stating it would contradict his faith. His attorney, Daniel McGehee, has announced plans to pursue legal action, alleging that university and hospital staff improperly disclosed private medical information and that the original witness has since retracted his statement. Meanwhile, the Pi Kappa Alpha chapter on campus was permanently closed, its charter surrendered after years of disciplinary issues, including a 2008 hazing incident where pledges were forced to do push-ups on broken glass, resulting in infections. Medical experts warn that alcohol enemas, while rare, are extremely dangerous: they bypass digestion, causing rapid and unpredictable intoxication. One documented fatality occurred in Texas in 2004, when a man died after receiving a sherry enema. Though some students reacted with disbelief—calling it a joke or too outrageous to be real—others expressed concern that such extreme cases distract from the far more common, equally deadly issue: binge drinking on college campuses. Health advocates stress that even without enemas, excessive alcohol consumption remains a leading cause of student death, and many young people falsely believe they’re safe because they wouldn’t do something 'so crazy.'

article_content: Westminster City Council has agreed to refund more than 5,000 parking fines issued to drivers who were confused by unclear signage in dual-use bays — spaces meant for general parking during the day but converted to taxi ranks at night. Each fine was originally set at £130, potentially totaling £665,000 if all were paid in full. However, the council now estimates the actual refund amount will be around £278,000, as many fines were paid at the discounted rate of £65 within two weeks. Drivers were often unaware they had broken any rules, as they were required to interpret two separate signs to understand the complex parking restrictions. This confusion has prompted the council to admit the signage failed to meet legal clarity standards. This move follows similar refunds by other UK councils. Last year, Hertfordshire repaid 35,000 fines totaling over £1 million after drivers were wrongly penalized for entering bus lanes. In Richmond, 20,000 fines from CCTV-equipped 'spy cars' were voided because the vehicles lacked proper certification. Earlier this year, over 300,000 fines for parking in construction-suspended bays were deemed invalid due to missing Department for Transport approval. The affected streets — Jermyn Street, Conduit Street in Mayfair, and Oxendon Street near Leicester Square — are among London’s most affluent, home to luxury retailers like Fortnum & Mason and designer Vivienne Westwood. Fines were issued between May 2011 and just days ago, when the council finally corrected the signage. While the council normally does not issue refunds after fines are paid, it has made a rare exception, acknowledging the exceptional ambiguity of the signs. To claim a refund, drivers must provide proof of payment, such as a reference number or receipt. Those who paid in cash may be unable to recover their money, as the council lacks digital records for such transactions. Council spokespersons say they will proactively contact those with registered contact details. Others are encouraged to submit any available information so their cases can be reviewed. Cllr Nickie Aiken, the council’s cabinet member for parking, stated: 'Dual-use bays aim to maximize limited kerbside space fairly. But we accept the signs were confusing — and correcting them and offering refunds is the right thing to do.' This is not the first time Westminster has faced scrutiny. In September, it was revealed its traffic wardens issued the highest number of parking fines in the UK — 1,269 per day — according to data from insurer LV=.

I september viste det seg at deres trafikkvakter utstedte flest parkeringsbøter i hele Storbritannia — 1.269 per dag — ifølge data fra forsikringsselskapet LV=.

article_content: As the U.S. men’s soccer team prepares for a pivotal friendly against Germany this weekend, midfielder Weston McKennie is sending a bold message: they’re no longer content just to compete with the world’s elite—they aim to defeat them. Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, the Juventus star reflected on the team’s journey since their surprising failure to qualify for the 2018 World Cup. Last year’s run to the Round of 16 in Qatar marked a turning point, and since then, the U.S. has gone 13 matches without a loss. With automatic qualification locked in as co-hosts of the 2026 World Cup, the team is using every match as a benchmark. On Saturday, they’ll face four-time champions Germany in East Hartford, Connecticut—a game McKennie calls essential for growth. 'We used to talk about competing with top teams,' he said. 'Now, we talk about beating them.' Another challenge awaits on Tuesday in Nashville, Tennessee, when they take on Ghana. For the Americans, these aren’t just friendlies—they’re stepping stones toward becoming a permanent force in international soccer. Germany, meanwhile, is seeking to rebuild its reputation after crashing out of the group stage in two straight World Cups. Both teams know: this isn’t just about one result. It’s about proving they belong among the best.

article_content: Want to look refreshed without stepping into a salon or operating room? Small, smart tweaks can make a surprising difference. Start with concealer—not just under your eyes, but also along the inner and outer corners of your lids, the sides of your nostrils, and the edges of your lips. This trick lifts your whole face subtly, making people wonder if you’ve had work done, says NYC makeup pro Mally Roncal. When it comes to hair color, go easy on the extremes. Over-lightening blonde strands can strip away their warm, youthful glow, warns colorist Louis Licari. On the flip side, going too dark looks artificial. Aim for balance that flatters your natural tone. Gravity doesn’t spare your backside. If your jeans feel loose after just one wear, they’re probably made of too much cotton. Look for at least 2% stretch—like Lycra—in every pair, advises Susie Crippen of J Brand. Support matters more than size. Heat styling and chemicals leave hair dull. Revive shine with a clear conditioning gloss—home kits like Fekkai’s work wonders. For daily radiance, try a shine serum such as Redken Color Extend Shine Enrich. Your bra might be the secret weapon you didn’t know you needed. Forget sizing charts. A well-fitted bra lifts your bust, which in turn creates the illusion of a longer, leaner torso—making you look years younger, according to stylist Annabel Tollman. Lips naturally thin over time. Dark, matte shades draw attention to that loss. Swap them for a bright pink gloss—it reflects light and gives the illusion of fullness, smoothing out fine lines instantly. Droopy eyelids? Try contouring. Use a light shadow right along your lashes to open up the eye, then add a slightly darker shade in an arch above the drooping area. The contrast tricks the eye into seeing a lifted lid, says Paula Dorf. Cheeks lose volume as we age. Plastic surgeon Gabriel Chiu points to Prevelle Silk—a hyaluronic acid filler that plumps skin immediately and lasts about three months (price: $250–$400 per syringe). Prefer something low-key? A pop of bright pink blush does the same magic: it highlights cheekbones and pulls focus upward. Powder foundation? Skip it. As skin gets drier with age, powder clings to fine lines and looks chalky. Instead, reach for dewy formulas like By Terry’s tinted moisturizer, cream blushes, and bronzers. A dab of highlighter on your cheekbones? That’s your personal spotlight. And finally, ditch the coordinated look. Matching everything is so last season. Add contrast—think tousled hair with a cocktail dress, or sneakers with tailored pants. That unexpected twist adds energy and modern flair, says Tollman. Ageless style isn’t about perfection—it’s about personality.

article_content: NEW YORK — U.S. life expectancy rose last year — by more than a year — but still hasn’t returned to pre-pandemic levels. According to researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the 2022 increase was primarily driven by declining COVID-19 deaths. Even with this significant gain, U.S. life expectancy is now just 77 years and 6 months — roughly where it stood two decades ago. Life expectancy is an estimate of the average number of years a baby born in a given year might live, assuming current death rates remain unchanged. It is widely regarded as one of the most critical indicators of a population’s overall health. The 2022 figures released Wednesday are provisional and may shift slightly as final data is processed. For decades, U.S. life expectancy rose gradually each year. But about a decade ago, that trend stalled — and in some years declined — largely due to rising overdose deaths and suicides. Then came the coronavirus pandemic, which has claimed over 1.1 million lives in the U.S. since early 2020. Life expectancy plummeted from 78 years and 10 months in 2019 to 77 years in 2020, then to 76 years and 5 months in 2021. 'We basically have lost 20 years of gains,' said Elizabeth Arias of the CDC. The drop in COVID-19 fatalities fueled the 2022 rebound. In 2021, COVID-19 was the nation’s third-leading cause of death, after heart disease and cancer. In 2022, it fell to fourth. With more than a month remaining in 2023, preliminary data suggests COVID-19 may rank as the ninth or tenth leading cause of death this year. Yet the U.S. continues to grapple with other deadly trends. Suicide rates reached an all-time high in 2022, the highest since 1941, according to a second CDC report released Wednesday. Drug overdose deaths rose slightly last year after surging early in the pandemic, and preliminary data for the first half of 2023 indicates this trend is continuing. U.S. life expectancy remains lower than that of dozens of other developed countries and has recovered more slowly than in nations such as France, Italy, Spain, and Sweden. 'What I’m trying to say is: That is not a great place to be,' said Steven Woolf, a mortality researcher at Virginia Commonwealth University. Highlights from the report: Life expectancy increased for both men and women and for every racial and ethnic group. Declines in COVID-19 deaths accounted for 84% of the 2022 gain; declines in heart disease deaths contributed about 4%. Experts note, however, that heart disease deaths rose during the pandemic and often co-occurred with COVID-19 fatalities. Gains varied significantly by group: Hispanic Americans and American Indian and Alaska Native populations saw life expectancy rise by more than two years. Black life expectancy increased by more than 1.5 years. Asian Americans gained about one year, while White Americans gained approximately 10 months. These gains are relative: Hispanic and Native American communities suffered the steepest losses early in the pandemic. Hispanic life expectancy dropped by more than four years between 2019 and 2021; Native American life expectancy fell by more than six. 'A lot of the large increases in life expectancy are coming from the groups that suffered the most from COVID,' said Mark Hayward, a sociologist at the University of Texas. 'They had more to rebound from.'
translated_content: NEW YORK — Livslengden i USA økte i fjor — med mer enn et år — men har fremdeles ikke kommet tilbake til nivået før pandemien. Ifølge forskere ved Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) var økningen i 2022 hovedsakelig på grunn av reduserte COVID-19-dødsfall. Selv med denne store økningen er livslengden i USA nå bare 77 år og 6 måneder — omtrent det samme som for to tiår siden. Livslengde er en estimert gjennomsnittlig levealder for en nyfødt i et gitt år, antatt at dødelighetsraten forblir uendret. Denne statistikken anses som en av de viktigste indikatorene for befolkningens helsetilstand. Tallene fra 2022 som ble publisert onsdag er midlertidige og kan endres litt når beregningene blir ferdigstilt. I flere tiår økte livslengden i USA litt hvert år. Men for cirka ti år siden stilnete trenden — og sank noen år — noe som hovedsakelig ble tilskrevet økte overdoser og selvmord. Deretter kom koronaviruset, som har drept over 1,1 millioner mennesker i USA siden begynnelsen av 2020. Livslengden sunk fra 78 år og 10 måneder i 2019 til 77 år i 2020, og deretter til 76 år og 5 måneder i 2021. 'Vi har tapet omtrent 20 års fremgang,' sa Elizabeth Arias fra CDC. Reduksjonen i COVID-19-dødsfall drev oppsvinget i 2022. I 2021 var COVID-19 det tredje største dødsårsaken i landet (etter hjertesykdom og kreft). I fjor falt den til fjerde plass. Med mer enn en måned igjen i dette året, tyder foreløpige data på at COVID-19 kan ende opp som niende eller tiende største dødsårsak i 2023. Men USA kjemper fortsatt mot andre problemer, inkludert overdosedødsfall og selvmord. Antallet selvmord i USA nådde et rekordhøy nivå i fjor, og selvmordsraten var høyest siden 1941, ifølge en annen CDC-rapport som ble publisert onsdag. Overdosedødsfall i USA økte litt i fjor etter to store stigninger i starten av pandemien. Og gjennom de første seks månedene i dette året har estimert overdosedødsfall fortsatt økt. Livslengden i USA er også lavere enn i dusinvis av andre land, og har ikke gjenopprettet seg like raskt som i land som Frankrike, Italia, Spania og Sverige. 'Hva jeg prøver å si, er: Det er ikke et bra sted å være,' sa Steven Woolf, en forsker i dødelighet ved Virginia Commonwealth University. Noen andre viktige punkter fra rapporten: — Livslengden økte for både menn og kvinner og for alle etniske og rasiale grupper. — Reduksjonen i COVID-19-dødsfall bidro med 84 % av økningen i livslengde. Den nest største bidragsyteren var reduksjon i hjertesykdomsdødsfall, som ble regnet med omtrent 4 %. Men eksperter påpeker at hjertesykdomsdødsfall økte under pandemien og ofte var involvert i mange dødsfall i pandemietiden. — Endringer i livslengde varierte mellom raser og etniske grupper. Hispanicamerikanere og urfolk i USA og Alaska så livslengden øke med mer enn to år i 2022. Livslengden for svarte økte med mer enn 1,5 år. Livslengden for asiatiske amerikanere økte ett år, mens livslengden for hvite økte med omtrent 10 måneder. Men endringene er relativt, fordi Hispanic- og urfolk ble hardest rammet i starten av COVID-19. Livslengden for Hispanic-amerikanere sunk med mer enn fire år mellom 2019 og 2021, og livslengden for urfolk sank med mer enn seks år. article_content: I’m knee-deep in the icy Atnarko River in central British Columbia, chest waders secured with a belt to keep me from being swept under if I slip. Cougar tracks press into the snow along the bank. Thankfully, the grizzlies—here each fall to feast on spawning salmon—are hibernating now. On this crisp morning, my guide Jai Condon demonstrates the finesse of fly-fishing: flick, whoosh, whoosh, whoosh—and release. 'How do you lay the line down so smoothly?' someone asks. 'Practice,' he laughs. I, meanwhile, am terrible. No nibbles. Even though trout can be caught year-round in the Bella Coola Valley, roughly 1,000 kilometers north of Vancouver, I didn’t come here to fish. But I’m hooked. Magical geography defines this place. Heavy fog grounded my first full day of heli-snowboarding—but Bella Coola Heli Sports thrives on backup plans. Conceived as an exclusive, year-round retreat for hardcore athletes chasing the kind of epic snowscapes seen in ski films, it also caters to restless adventurers who crave variety. Depending on the season, guests can cross-country ski, hike, bike, raft, ride horses, watch grizzlies, or even help with cattle calving—then ski in the afternoon. Yes, really. A helicopter or boat (depending on your budget) ferries you to remote fjords for a soak in natural hot springs, followed by a bracing dip in the Pacific. 'We didn’t come for the vertical,' says Kristina Enquist, visiting from Finland with her husband, Eric. 'We came for the whole experience.' That sentiment echoes why three filmmakers—Christian Begin, Peter 'Swede' Mattsson, and Beat Steiner—first came here 14 years ago. Glaciers dating to the last Ice Age crown the Coast Mountains, rising from sea level to Mount Waddington at 4,019 meters. This dramatic landscape doubled as the Himalayas in 'Seven Years in Tibet' and 'Kundun.' Sir Edmund Hillary trained here. And every year, over 30 meters of snow pile up. 'Wow, this place is on steroids,' Steiner recalls. 'Everything is big. The trees. The mountains. The glaciers. The biggest fjords in the Americas. It’s all big.' While heli-skiing boomed inland, no one touched this coast. The trio applied for—and surprisingly won—10,700 square kilometers of untouched terrain. 'Everyone was fighting over the interior,' Begin says. 'We grabbed the jewel. We grabbed the coast.' Since 2003, Bella Coola has whisked guests from Vancouver to this remote paradise. The one-hour flight in a Beechcraft 1900C is breathtaking—if not slightly nauseating. Jet-lagged travelers from the U.S., UK, Finland, Slovakia, and Thailand arrive for safety briefings on helicopters and avalanches. Skiing on arrival? Part of the 'rock star' treatment. But conditions are brutal: heavy snow, then a warm spell, then a freeze—creating dangerous crust layers. I cut through ice harder than week-old pizza. After a few shivering runs, we land at Tweedsmuir Park Lodge, where guests unwind in hot tubs, sweat lodges, and feasts of fresh salmon. Bella Coola operates three lodges, capping weekly guests at 34—ensuring pristine, uncrowded runs. Other operators cram dozens into smaller areas daily. 'That’s not private enough,' Mattsson says. For the ultra-wealthy, the Pantheon Heli Ranch offers eight guests exclusive access to 4,450 square kilometers—and first descents. Name your own run. Cost: $105,260 USD ($114,800 CAD) per week. Typical guests: executives, doctors, celebrities, ages 45–55. Almost all men. 'It’s always been a boy’s club,' Mattsson admits. 'Heli-skiing, overall, is.' Richard Lapointe, a former military pilot with experience flying stunt jets and rescue missions, is our pilot. He’s also what my guide calls a 'secret weapon.' In his AStar B2 helicopter—seating just four—he threads between razor-thin rock faces and lands on plateaus no bigger than picnic tables, hunting for untouched powder. The snow gods delivered: knee-deep, weightless flakes. In two days, I clocked 13,840 vertical meters of fresh lines. Glaciers glowed blue beneath me; forests sent me soaring on knolls and drifts. My board carved white smoke behind me. 'You know junkies chasing their next fix?' says Eric Enquist, the bolder half of the Finnish duo. 'Now I get it.' Danger is never far. We navigate avalanche debris and watch ice sheets collapse. Later, Jai Condon returns to the lodge holding a chunk of ancient glacier ice—chipped into glasses of scotch. I’m happy to let it melt slowly into my drink. On my final day—with the helicopter grounded again—Begin takes us to Bella Coola town, population 852, home of the Nuxalk First Nation. Their presence is everywhere: totem poles lining the streets, a hollowed-out cedar tree used for smoking fish near Big Cedars Trail (it smells like savory meat). Hard to find without a guide, Thorsen Creek petroglyphs reveal dozens of ancient carvings: human faces, animals, geometric shapes. Their origins remain debated, but their sacredness is undeniable. As I prepare to leave, I learn all flights are canceled—strong winds and heavy snow. I’m told this happens once a year. I’m happily stranded in Shangri-La.

Kullkattspor trykket inn i snøen ved bredden. Heldigvis sover bjørnene—som kommer hver høst for å spise spawnende laks—nå. På denne kolde morgenen viser veilederen min, Jai Condon, kunsten med flyfiske: sving, whoosh, whoosh, whoosh—og slipp. 'Hvordan får du linjen til å lande så fint?' spør noen. 'Øvelse,' ler han. Magisk geografi definerer stedet. Tung tåke hindret min første fulle dag med heli-snøbrett, men Bella Coola Heli Sports trives med backupplaner. Konseptet er en eksklusiv, år-rundt-ferie for hardcore-utadvendte som leter etter de episke snølandskapene de har sett i ski-filmer, men det tilfredsstiller også utadvendte som ønsker variasjon. Avhengig av sesongen kan gjester gå langrenn, gå tur, sykle, rafting, ride hest, se grizzlybjørner, eller selv hjelpe med kalving av kyr—og så snøbrette om ettermiddagen. Ja, virkelig. En helikopter eller båt (avhengig av hvor mye du vil utgi) frakter deg til fjordene for et bad i naturlige varmekilder, fulgt av en iskald dip i Stillehavet. 'Vi kom ikke for det vertikale,' sier Kristina Enquist, som besøker fra Finland sammen med ektemannen Eric. 'Vi kom for hele opplevelsen.' Denne følelsen reflekterer hvorfor tre filmmakere—Christian Begin, Peter 'Swede' Mattsson og Beat Steiner—kom hit for 14 år siden. Isbreer fra den siste istiden dekker Coast Mountains, som stiger fra havnivå til Mount Waddington på 4.019 meter. Dette dramatiske landskapet stod for Himalaya i filmene 'Seven Years in Tibet' og 'Kundun.' Sir Edmund Hillary trente her. Og hvert år samler det seg over 30 meter snø. 'Wow, dette stedet er på steroids,' husker Steiner. 'Alt er stort. Trærne. Fjellene. Isbreene. De største fjordene i Amerika. Alt er stort.' Mens heli-skiing ble populært innenfor kontinentet, var ingen her. Trioen søkte om—og til sin overraskelse, fikk—10.700 kvadratkilometer uutnyttet terreng. 'Alle kjempet i det indre,' sier Begin. 'Vi tok juvelen. Vi tok kysten.' Siden 2003 har Bella Coola transportert gjester fra Vancouver til denne avsides paradiset. Den ene timers flyvningen i en Beechcraft 1900C er spektakulær—om ikke litt magekvalmende. Jetlaggede turister fra USA, Storbritannia, Finland, Slovakia og Thailand ankommer for sikkerhetskurser i helikopter og snøskred. Å skire på ankomst? Del av 'rock star'-behandlingen. Men forholdene er brutale: tung snø, så varmt vær, så frysning—og dannelse av farlige islag. Jeg skar gjennom is som var hardere enn en ukes gammel pizza. Etter noen tannkramrende løp, lander vi på Tweedsmuir Park Lodge, der gjester slapper av i varme bader, svettebuer og fester med fersk laks. Bella Coola driver tre hytter, med maks 34 gjester i uken—sikrer perfekte, ubesatte spor. Andre operatører kjører dusinvis av mennesker hver dag over mye mindre områder. 'Det er ikke privat nok,' sier Mattsson. For de med ekstra dybde i lomma, tilbyr Pantheon Heli Ranch åtte gjester eksklusiv tilgang til 4.450 kvadratkilometer terreng—og første nedstigninger. Navngi din egen rute. Pris: 105.260 USD (114.800 CAD) per uke. Typiske gjester: bedriftsledere, leger, kjendiser, alder 45–55. Nesten alle menn. 'Det har alltid vært en gutteklynge,' gir Mattsson til. 'Heli-skiing i det hele tatt er.' Richard Lapointe, en tidligere militær pilot med erfaring fra stunt-flyging og redningsoperasjoner, er vår pilot. Han er også hva min veileder kaller en 'hemmelig våpen'. I hans AStar B2-helikopter—med plass til bare fire gjester—trår han mellom skarpe klipper og lander på plater så små som en piknikbord, på jakt etter uutsøkt snø. Snøgudene har gitt oss: knehøy, lett snø. I to dager registrerte jeg 13.840 meter vertikal høyde i ny snø. Isbreer blålyste under meg; skogene sendte meg i luften på knoller og snødrifter. Min snøbrett skar en dyp kanal—og hvit røyk—bak meg. 'Du kjenner junkies som leter etter neste dose?' sier Eric Enquist, den mer modige halvdelen av det finske paret. 'Nå skjønner jeg hva de mente.' Farlig er aldri langt unna. Vi navigerer gjennom nylige snøskredavfall og ser en isplate løsne fra fjellsiden. Senere returnerer Jai Condon til hytten med en blokk av urgamle is—hakket i glass med scotch og andre drikk. Jeg er glad for at den smelter langsomt inn i min drikk. På min siste dag—med helikopteret igjen på bakken—tar Begin oss til byen Bella Coola, befolkning 852, hjem til Nuxalk-førstehavn. Deres tilstedeværelse er overalt: totempolere langs gatene, en hul hule i en kjempestor ceder som brukes til å røyke fisk nær Big Cedars Trail (den lukter som kjøtt). Vanskelig å finne uten en guide, Thorsen Creek-petroglyphene avslører dusinvis av gamle ristninger: menneskeansikter, dyr, geometriske mønstre. Opprinnelsen er fortsatt diskutert, men deres hellighet er uhyggelig tydelig. Når jeg forbereder meg på å dra, får jeg vite at alle flyvninger er kansellert—sterke vind og tung snø. Jeg blir fortalt at dette skjer én gang per år. Jeg er heldigvis fastlåst i Shangri-La.

article_content: Mary Beard said she was left 'wanting to cry' after being bombarded with abuse for speaking out in favor of free speech. The celebrated academic joined other campaigners in urging universities not to ban speakers perceived as hostile to transgender people. But just hours after a letter — signed by Professor Beard and many others, including gay rights campaigner Peter Tatchell — was published, she faced a torrent of abuse on Twitter. Mary Beard and Peter Tatchell endured a barrage of abuse after signing a letter calling on universities to allow speakers labeled 'transphobic' to speak before students, in the name of free speech. The original letter argued it was 'illiberal and undemocratic' for universities to ban lecturers and academics deemed 'transphobic' — meaning prejudiced against transgender people. However, the letter triggered a fierce backlash from parts of the transgender community. Professor Beard was later branded an 'unrepentant bigot,' and Mr. Tatchell was called a 'parasite.' Professor Beard, 60, later wrote on her blog about how the relentless abuse disrupted her sleep. She stated: 'For two days, I’ve been bombarded by tweets (and a few emails). Some tweeters have been very polite in their disagreement — for which, thank you. Others less so (though I should be clear, there have been no threats of violence). I received 60 tweets in about an hour from one person alone.' Mr. Tatchell said the attacks were especially painful given his lifelong activism against prejudice. Professor Beard added: 'Last night, I went to bed wanting to weep... It wasn’t the force of any single remark — it was the relentless pummeling of attacks based on wildly distorted, sometimes entirely incorrect, interpretations of the letter. Cumulative harassment is what it felt like, though I’m sure it wasn’t intended that way.' Mr. Tatchell, 63, said he received more than 5,000 messages since the letter’s publication, some of them threatening. He told The Independent: 'On Saturday night, after the first attacks began, I couldn’t sleep. I was devastated by being misrepresented as an anti-trans bigot. I woke up exhausted, and on my way to an LGBT conference, I tripped on the pavement, hit my head, and suffered a concussion — which I’m still feeling today.'

Noen tweetere har vært veldig høflige i sin uenighet — takk for det. Andre mindre så (men jeg bør tydeliggjøre at det ikke har vært trusler om vold). Jeg fikk 60 tweets i løpet av omtrent én time fra én person alene.' Herr Tatchell sa at angrepene var spesielt smertefulle gitt hans livslange arbeid mot diskriminering. Det var ikke kraften i noen enkelt bemerkning — det var den vedvarende hammeringen av angrep basert på vilt fordreid, noen ganger helt feil, tolkninger av brevet. Kumulativ mobbing er hva det føltes som, selv om jeg er sikker på at det ikke var ment slik.' Herr Tatchell, 63, sa han mottok mer enn 5.000 meldinger siden brevet ble publisert, noen av dem truende. article_content: By Mail on Sunday Reporter. PUBLISHED: 17:55 EST, 6 July 2013. | UPDATED: 17:55 EST, 6 July 2013. Nobel Peace Prize laureate Mohamed El Baradei was reportedly named interim Prime Minister of Egypt last night. The 71-year-old former head of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is said to have been summoned to the presidential palace on Wednesday afternoon to be sworn in by interim President Adli Mansour. A long-time opposition leader, El Baradei had previously led resistance against both former President Hosni Mubarak, ousted in 2011, and Islamist President Mohamed Morsi, removed by the military last week. The appointment was condemned by the Freedom and Justice Party, the political wing of the Muslim Brotherhood. A spokesperson stated: 'We reject this coup and all that results from it, including ElBaradei.' The announcement comes as Egypt braces for further violence following a weekend of clashes that left at least 35 dead and more than 1,100 injured. Opponents of Morsi are expected to confront his supporters during a planned Muslim Brotherhood demonstration in Cairo’s Tahrir Square at 4 p.m. Fierce fighting erupted on Friday, as Islamists took to the streets to protest Morsi’s removal. The deadliest violence occurred in Alexandria, where 14 people were killed and 200 wounded. In central Cairo, pro- and anti-Morsi demonstrators engaged in prolonged street battles using stones, knives, petrol bombs, and clubs. A Coptic Christian priest was shot dead yesterday in the coastal city of El Arish — believed to be the first sectarian killing since Morsi’s ouster. The Muslim Brotherhood has criticized Coptic Pope Tawadros, spiritual leader of Egypt’s eight million Christians, for endorsing Morsi’s removal and attending the military’s announcement suspending the constitution. Last night, Hayat Mokhles, a 50-year-old mother of three, expressed concern over escalating violence but added: 'We will defend our revolution with our lives. These fundamentalists came close to ruining the country — that’s why Morsi had to go.'

article_content: Seven-year-old Brendon Mackey lost his life the day after being struck by a stray bullet while walking with his father to a Fourth of July fireworks show in Virginia. The boy, just steps behind his dad, suddenly collapsed in the parking lot of the Boathouse Restaurant around 9 p.m. Initially, his father thought Brendon had simply fallen and hit his head — but doctors later discovered a fatal gunshot wound to the top of his skull. Authorities believe the bullet came from celebratory gunfire fired into the air somewhere in the general vicinity of Brandermill. Such acts, often done to mark Independence Day, are tragically common and deadly: bullets fall back to earth at lethal speeds, sometimes striking people over a mile away. In fact, studies show that around one-third of those hit by falling bullets die — far higher than typical gun injury fatality rates. Brendon, who was set to start third grade at C.E. Curtis Elementary and adored golf and SpongeBob SquarePants, was nowhere near the source of the shot. His death is not an isolated case: on the same night, a 26-year-old woman in Florida was wounded in the leg by another stray round. Police stress this was not intentional, but the result of dangerous recklessness. Residents in the quiet community expressed shock, saying they’d never witnessed gun violence there. Officials are asking anyone who saw someone firing into the sky to speak up — urging the public to imagine the unimaginable grief the Mackey family now carries.

Myndighetene tror kulen kom fra festlig skyting som ble avfyrt opp i luften et sted i Brandermill-området. Studier viser at omtrent en tredjedel av de som blir truffet av fallende kuler dør — langt høyere enn typiske dødelighetsrater for skuddskader. Brendon, som skulle begynne på syvende klasse ved C.E. Curtis Elementary og elsket golf og SpongeBob SquarePants, var langt unna skytepunktet. Myndighetene ber alle som så noen skyte opp i luften om å kontakte politiet — og oppfordrer offentligheten til å tenke seg inn i den uforståelige sorgen som Mackey-familien nå må bære.

article_content: Ian Robert Turnbull, a 79-year-old wheat farmer from Moree in northern New South Wales, has been charged with the murder of Glen Turner, a 51-year-old environmental compliance officer for the NSW government. The fatal shooting occurred around 5:40 p.m. on July 29 on Talga Lane, near Moree, during what was reportedly a routine land inspection. Turnbull allegedly approached Turner and his colleague Robert Strange while they were conducting an official site visit related to illegal vegetation clearing on Turnbull’s property. He then armed himself with a rifle and opened fire. Turner was struck multiple times and died at the scene. Strange was assaulted and is in shock but otherwise unharmed. Turnbull was arrested five hours later at a nearby property. He has since been denied bail after two additional charges were laid at Moree Local Court. He is scheduled to return to court in September. Turnbull had previously been issued multiple legal notices by Turner for violating the Native Title Vegetation Act by clearing protected land, particularly in the Croppa Creek area. The Land and Environment Court had ordered him to rehabilitate the damaged land. Glen Turner is survived by his wife, Alison, and two young children, aged nine and ten. His death has drawn widespread condolences from government officials, including NSW Environment Minister Rob Stokes and Agriculture Minister Barnaby Joyce. Turnbull’s family and community members describe him as a well-respected local figure — active in community projects such as building homes for the elderly, collecting donations for school events, and delivering Meals on Wheels. They say he was under immense emotional strain due to years of regulatory pressure. The incident has reignited debate across regional NSW over the balance between environmental protection and farming livelihoods. Moree Plains Shire Mayor Katrina Humphries stated that rural residents feel ‘pushed and pushed and pushed,’ calling the tragedy a symptom of deeper systemic tensions. Ecologist Phil Spark noted that Turnbull had cleared approximately 100 hectares of land, much of which was critical koala habitat. Meanwhile, the NSW Public Service Association urged improved risk assessments for environmental officers working in high-conflict areas. While no one condones violence, many are now calling for policy reform to address the growing friction between landholders and regulators. Turnbull’s family has publicly offered their condolences to the Turner family, acknowledging the devastating loss of a father and husband.

article_content: Pop music superstar Beyoncé has postponed her scheduled concert in Antwerp, Belgium, due to dehydration and exhaustion, her representatives said. Following medical advice, she will not perform Tuesday night and is awaiting further guidance before deciding on her Wednesday show in Belgium. Other dates on her 'The Mrs. Carter Show' tour — named after her married name, as the wife of rapper Jay-Z (born Shawn Carter) — are not expected to be affected. Since launching the European leg of the tour on April 15 in Belgrade, Serbia, Beyoncé has performed across the continent. Her final European performance is set for London on June 1, followed by the North American leg beginning in late June and running through August. Shortly after announcing the Antwerp postponement — which will be rescheduled — Beyoncé’s official Facebook page posted: 'Thank you, Antwerp, for bringing your donations to the venue today! #beyGOOD.'

article_content: Since 2011, California has significantly reformed its criminal justice system, reducing its prison population with no increase in violent crime and only marginal effects on property crime statewide. The COVID-19 pandemic further accelerated decarceration as the state lowered prison and jail populations to curb the spread of the virus. Concerns emerged that releases tied to COVID-19 mitigation harmed public safety. A new study by researchers at the University of California (UC) Irvine and the University of Arizona investigated this claim and found no consistent relationship between COVID-19-related jail decarceration and violent or property crime at the county level. Published in the Journal of Contemporary Criminal Justice and promoted by the Crime and Justice Research Alliance—funded by the National Criminal Justice Association—the study highlights that California’s pandemic-driven reductions in correctional populations were more severe and abrupt than any prior reform. According to Charis E. Kubrin, professor of criminology, law, and society at UC Irvine and lead researcher, 'Concerns about the impact of these actions on crime rates were widespread. Although violent and property crime declined in large cities during the pandemic, homicide and car theft rose significantly.' However, since these increases mirrored national trends, it remained unclear whether California’s decarceration efforts were responsible. To isolate the effect of jail downsizing, researchers analyzed monthly average daily jail populations from January 2013 to December 2021, alongside county-level crime data. COVID-19 decarceration occurred from January through December 2020. The study found no consistent link between jail population reductions and crime increases across California’s 58 counties, suggesting that decarceration, on average, did not drive statewide crime rises. Among the study’s limitations, the authors note that their synthetic control method did not fully replicate ideal treated and untreated county crime trajectories. They also limited their analysis of COVID-19 mitigation to March through December 2020 to minimize confounding effects from summer 2020 protests following the murders of Breonna Taylor, George Floyd, and Jacob Blake. 'These limitations reveal how challenging it is to isolate decarceration’s potential effect from any single factor during one of the most dynamic and turbulent periods in recent state and national history,' notes Bradley J. Bartos, assistant professor of government and public policy at the University of Arizona and co-author. 'Nonetheless, our findings offer valuable insights to inform future criminal justice innovations.'

COVID-19-pandemien forsterket dekarserasjonen da staten reduserte fengsels- og fengselbefolkningen for å hemme spredningen av viruset. Det oppstod bekymringer om at frigivelser knyttet til COVID-19-mitigering skadet offentlig sikkerhet. En ny studie utført av forskere ved University of California (UC) Irvine og University of Arizona undersøkte denne påstanden og fant ingen konsistent sammenheng mellom dekarserasjon knyttet til COVID-19 og voldelige eller eiendomsforbrytelser på fylkesnivå. Publisert i Journal of Contemporary Criminal Justice og fremmet av Crime and Justice Research Alliance – finansiert av National Criminal Justice Association – understreker studien at Californias pandemibaserte reduksjoner i korrektive befolkningsmengder var mer alvorlige og bratte enn noen tidligere reformer. Ifølge Charis E. Kubrin, professor i kriminologi, lov og samfunn ved UC Irvine og leder av studien: 'Bekymringer om effekten av disse tiltakene på kriminalitetsnivåer var utbredt. Selv om voldelige og eiendomsforbrytelser sank i store byer under pandemien, steg drap og biltyverier betraktelig.' Men siden disse økningene speilte nasjonale trender, var det uklart om Californias dekarserasjonsinnsats var ansvarlig. For å isolere effekten av reduksjonen av fengselsbefolkningen, analyserte forskerne månedlige gjennomsnittlige fengselsbefolkninger fra januar 2013 til desember 2021, sammen med fylkesnivåets månedlige kriminalitetsdata. COVID-19-dekarserasjonen skjedde fra januar til desember 2020. Studien fant ingen konsistent sammenheng mellom reduksjoner i fengselsbefolkningen og økninger i kriminalitet i Californias 58 fylker, noe som antyder at dekarserasjon i gjennomsnitt ikke førte til økte kriminalitetsnivåer i staten. Blant studiens begrensninger, påpeker forfatterne at deres synthetic control-metode ikke fullt ut replikerte ideelle behandlet og ikke-behandlet kriminalitetsbaner i fylkene. De begrenset også analysen av COVID-19-mitigering til mars til desember 2020 for å minimere forvirrende effekter fra sommerens 2020-protester etter drapene på Breonna Taylor, George Floyd og Jacob Blake. 'Disse begrensningene avslører hvor utfordrende det er å isolere potensiell effekt av dekarserasjon fra en enkelt faktor under en av de mest dynamiske og kaotiske periodene i statens og landets historie,' sier Bradley J. Bartos, assistentprofessor i regjering og offentlig politikk ved University of Arizona og medforfatter. 'Likevel gir våre funn verdifulle innsikter som kan informere fremtidige innovasjoner innen strafferett.'

article_content: By Lee Moran. Last updated at 4:35 PM on September 5, 2011. Hurricane Katia could soon affect the U.S. East Coast—just days after Hurricane Irene caused extensive flooding and Tropical Storm Lee dumped torrential rain across the central Gulf. The Miami-based U.S. National Hurricane Center reported that Katia intensified over the open Atlantic and strengthened into a powerful Category 2 storm. While it remains too early to determine its exact landfall risk, most computer models predict Katia will turn northeast and recurve back out to sea later this week. Satellite images from the International Space Station show Katia churning in the Atlantic. The center warned that ocean swells linked to Katia are already reaching parts of the U.S. East Coast. Even if Katia does not make direct landfall, high surf and dangerous rip currents are expected to increase along eastern beaches over the next few days. At 5 p.m. yesterday (9 p.m. GMT), Katia had maximum sustained winds of 105 miles per hour and was located approximately 365 miles north-northeast of the Northern Leeward Islands. Forecasters said Katia could become a major hurricane by Monday, with winds reaching at least 111 mph (178 kph), depending on environmental conditions. The uncertainty in Katia’s path stems partly from Tropical Storm Lee’s presence over the Gulf of Mexico. Forecasters are unsure how Lee’s circulation might influence Katia later this week. Katia is the second hurricane of the Atlantic season, which runs from June through November and is entering its historically most active phase. Meanwhile, Tropical Storm Lee’s center moved ashore in Louisiana before dawn on Sunday, lingering over the central Gulf Coast and unleashing torrential rainfall. Some areas received 6 to 10 inches of rain, with forecasts predicting up to 15 inches along the central Gulf Coast—and as much as 20 inches in isolated locations. The National Weather Service warned of significant flash flooding, especially as rains moved north into the rugged Appalachian region. 'Up in the Appalachians, you get more threat of flash floods,' said NHC specialist Robbie Berg. 'That’s very similar to what we saw in Vermont.' Vermont is still recovering from Hurricane Irene, which triggered deadly river overflows last week. In Louisiana, flooding forced evacuations in towns like Jean Lafitte. Thousands lost power. Residents, including 31-year-old plumber Brad Zinet, remained in place, preparing what they could. 'We got nowhere to go. We’re just getting everything put up out of the way and hope for the best,' he said. 'This is a way of life around here.' In New Orleans, sporadic downpours caused localized street flooding, but levees held and pumps managed runoff. Mayor Mitch Landrieu urged residents: 'We’re not out of the woods. Don’t go to sleep on this storm.' Along the Gulf Coast, high winds pushed sand onto highways in Mississippi, reducing visibility. On U.S. Highway 90 and parts of Interstate 10, drivers struggled to distinguish roads from medians or curbs. Coastal Alabama saw rough seas that closed the Port of Mobile, though some casinos remained open. Beaches that would typically be crowded for Labor Day were nearly empty. Events were canceled, and residents secured property against wind and waves. 'The weekend is literally a wash,' said Dauphin Island Mayor Jeff Collier. 'It’s really a shame that it happened on a holiday weekend.' Katia, currently located about 365 miles (587 km) northeast of the Northern Leeward Islands, had sustained winds of 105 mph and was moving at 12 mph. No coastal watches or warnings were in effect due to its distance from land.

Det Miami-baserte U.S. National Hurricane Center rapporterte at Katia intensiverte seg over det åpne Atlanterhavet og styrket seg til en kraftig kategori 2-orkan. Selv om det fortsatt er for tidlig å fastslå dens nøyaktige trussel mot land, forutsier de fleste datamodellene at Katia vil snu nordøst og vende tilbake ut til havet senere denne uken. Selv om Katia ikke treffer land direkte, forventes høye bølger og farlige strømmer langs østkystens strander å øke de neste dagene. Kl. 17:00 i går (21:00 GMT) hadde Katia maksimale vedvarende vindhastigheter på 105 miles per time og var beliggende omtrent 587 kilometer nordøst for de nordlige Leewardøyene. Frognere sa at Katia kunne bli en stor orkan mandag, med vindhastigheter på minst 111 mph (178 km/t), avhengig av miljøforholdene. Usikkerheten i Katias bane skyldes delvis tilstedeværelsen av tropisk storm Lee over Golfen av Mexico. Frognere er usikre på hvordan Lees sirkulasjon kan påvirke Katia senere denne uken. Katia er den andre orkanen i Atlanterhavssesongen, som løper fra juni til november og nå er i sin historisk mest aktive fasen. Mens dette skjer, beveget tropisk storm Lees sentrum seg innover i Louisiana før daggry søndag, og ble liggende over det sentrale Golfområdet og frakta ekstremt mye regn. Noen områder fikk 150–250 mm regn, med forutsetninger for opptil 380 mm langs det sentrale Golfområdet – og opptil 500 mm i isolerte områder. Den nasjonale værtjenesten advarte om betydelig plutselig oversvømmelse, spesielt når regnet beveget seg nordover mot de bratte Appalacene. 'Opp i Appalacene får du større fare for plutselige oversvømmelser,' sa spesialist Robbie Berg fra NHC. 'Det er veldig likt det vi så i Vermont.' Vermont er fremdeles i ferd med å gjenopprette seg etter orkanen Irene, som utløste dødelige elveoversvømmelser forrige uke. I Louisiana forårsaket oversvømmelsen evakueringer i byer som Jean Lafitte. Tusenvis mistet strøm. Befolkningen, inkludert 31 år gamle rørleggeren Brad Zinet, sto igjen og forberedte seg så godt de kunne. 'Vi har ingen annen sted å gå. Vi bare setter alt opp og håper for det beste,' sa han. 'Dette er en livsstil her rundt.' I New Orleans forårsaket lokale nedbørsvann oversvømmelser på gater, men leveene holdt og pumper håndterte avløpet. Borgmester Mitch Landrieu advarte innbyggerne: 'Vi er ikke ute av skogene. Ikke sov på denne stormen.' Langs Golfkysten forårsaket sterke vindar vinddrift av sand på veier i Mississippi og reduserte synligheten. På U.S. Highway 90 og deler av Interstate 10 hadde kjørere vanskelig for å skille mellom vei, median og kant. Kysten i Alabama så brutale havbølger som lukket Havn i Mobile, selv om noen kasinoer fortsatte å drive. Strandene som normalt ville vært travle til Labor Day var nesten tomme. Arrangementer ble kansellert, og befolkningen sikret eiendeler mot vind og bølger. 'Helgen er bokstavelig tapt,' sa Dauphin Islands borgmester Jeff Collier. 'Det er virkelig synd at det skjedde på en helgedag.' Katia, som for tiden ligger omtrent 587 kilometer nordøst for de nordlige Leewardøyene, hadde vedvarende vindhastigheter på 105 mph og beveget seg med 19 km/t. Ingen kystvarsler eller advarsler var i kraft på grunn av dens avstand fra land.

article_content: Dominic Grieve, the UK’s Attorney General, has apologized after stating that minority communities in Britain bring with them 'endemic' corruption. His remarks, made in a Saturday interview with the Daily Telegraph, suggested that corruption is growing due to 'a favour culture' prevalent among some Pakistani communities. The comments were swiftly condemned as offensive and divisive. Within hours, Grieve issued a public apology, clarifying: 'If I gave the impression that there is a particular problem in the Pakistani community, I was wrong. I believe the Pakistani community has enriched this country a great deal. I’m sorry if I have caused any offence.' Tory MEP Sajjad Karim, a member of the British Pakistani community himself, called the remarks 'ill-advised' and 'populist,' accusing Grieve of painting an entire community with a broad brush. He stressed that while electoral fraud is real — as seen in the 2007 Slough case involving Eshaq Khan — it does not reflect the values of the wider community. Conservative Party chairman Grant Shapps echoed this view, emphasizing that corruption must be tackled everywhere, not targeted at specific ethnic groups. 'The Pakistani community has done an awful lot for this country,' he said. 'We must root out fraud wherever it occurs — but never by blaming a community.' The 2007 Slough electoral fraud scandal, in which Eshaq Khan and five others were jailed for using 'ghost voters' to rig a local council election, remains a key example cited in debates about electoral integrity. Experts warn that weak systems, not cultural norms, enable such fraud — a point reinforced by the Electoral Commission’s findings that the UK lacks effective safeguards against voter fraud.

Hans kommentarer, som ble gjort i et intervju med Daily Telegraph på lørdag, antydet at korruptjon øker på grunn av en 'favørkultur' som er vanlig blant noen pakistanske samfunn. Kommentarene ble raskt fordømt som fornærmende og delende. Innen få timer utstedte Grieve en offentlig unnskyldning og klargjorde: 'Hvis jeg ga inntrykket at det er et spesielt problem i det pakistanske samfunnet, var jeg feil. Jeg tror det pakistanske samfunnet har riket landet veldig mye. Beklager hvis jeg har forårsaket noen fornærmelse.' Tory-MEP Sajjad Karim, som selv er medlem av det britiske pakistanske samfunnet, kalte kommentarene 'uhensiktsmessige' og 'populisteriske', og beskyldte Grieve for å male hele et samfunn med en bred pensel. Han understreket at mens valgfusk er reelt — som sett i Slough-saken fra 2007 involvert Eshaq Khan — reflekterer det ikke verdier i det videre samfunnet. Torys partileder Grant Shapps tok opp denne synspunktet og understreket at korruptjon må bekjempes overalt, ikke rettet mot spesifikke etniske grupper. 'Det pakistanske samfunnet har gjort veldig mye for dette landet,' sa han. 'Vi må utrydde fusk hvor som helst — men aldri ved å skyldlegge et samfunn.' Valgfuskskandalen i Slough i 2007, der Eshaq Khan og fem andre ble dømt til fengsel for å bruke 'gjennomgående velgere' for å manipulere et lokalrådsvalg, er et nøkkelpunkt i debatten om valgintegritet. Ekspertene advarer mot at svake systemer, ikke kulturelle normer, muliggjør slike handlinger — et punkt styrket av Valgkommisjonens funn om at Storbritannia mangler effektive sikringssystemer mot valgfusk.

article_content: After nearly two decades in Congress, Ohio Republican David Hobson has announced he won’t seek re-election in 2008, concluding a nine-term career in the House. The 71-year-old lawmaker, who has represented parts of Dayton and Columbus since 1991, is a senior voice on the powerful appropriations panel that controls defense funding. Known for his sharp humor and steady leadership, Hobson was the only Republican invited on House Speaker Nancy Pelosi’s recent Middle East delegation — a sign of his bipartisan reputation. House Minority Leader John Boehner honored him as a dedicated public servant, praising his ‘dry wit’ and unwavering commitment to his district. As one of twelve Republican House members stepping aside ahead of the 2008 vote, Hobson’s departure opens a key seat in a traditionally GOP-leaning region. The National Republican Congressional Committee vowed to find a successor who’ll uphold core conservative priorities: lower taxes, economic growth, and national security. Meanwhile, fellow Republican Heather Wilson of New Mexico is running for the Senate seat vacated by retiring Senator Pete Domenici — highlighting how some GOP lawmakers are pivoting upward, not out.

Den 71 år gamle lovgiveren, som har representert deler av Dayton og Columbus siden 1991, er en fremtredende stemme på det kraftige utvalget for økonomiske midler som kontrollerer forsvarsfinansieringen. Kjent for sitt skarpe humor og stabile lederskap, var Hobson den eneste republikaneren som ble invitert til Høyesterådets Nancy Pelosis nylige Midtøsten-reise — et tegn på hans bipartisane rykte. article_content: New Delhi, India (CNN) — A U.S. federal air marshal may have violated Indian law by failing to properly secure his law enforcement equipment while in the country, U.S. officials said Friday. The equipment brought into India included two pistol magazines and ammunition — items the U.S. Transportation Security Administration (TSA) requires air marshals to secure upon entering a foreign nation. 'TSA is investigating this incident and working with Indian government officials to ensure the facts are thoroughly reviewed,' federal officials stated in a statement issued by the U.S. Embassy in New Delhi. Delhi police did not confirm whether a U.S. air marshal was involved in the investigation. However, P.N. Aggarwal, Joint Commissioner of Delhi Police, said that 'quite a few rounds of ammunition and two magazines' were discovered hidden inside an air-conditioning duct in a hotel room. The description matched the TSA’s account of equipment that had not been secured properly by an air marshal in India. The discovery led to an uncomfortable situation for three Italian tourists who had occupied the room prior to the find. By the time the items were discovered, the tourists had already traveled to Mumbai and were recalled to Delhi for questioning. 'They were allowed to go,' Aggarwal said, after investigators found no evidence implicating them. Neither Indian nor U.S. officials released the names of the tourists or the air marshal. While Indian authorities declined to confirm if the air marshal was a suspect, U.S. officials were more direct. 'On June 1, TSA was made aware of a situation involving the failure of a Federal Air Marshal to properly secure his law enforcement equipment upon entering India,' the TSA statement read. 'The equipment — two pistol magazines and ammunition — is consistent with duty gear issued to Federal Air Marshals.' 'The Federal Air Marshal Service takes such incidents seriously; agency policy requires compliance with international agreements to secure law enforcement equipment abroad. Violations are subject to full disciplinary action, up to and including termination.' CNN's Harmeet Shah Singh and Drew Griffin contributed to this report.

article_content: By Helen Lawson. A city worker has quit his job to star in a new Chinese-British sitcom—despite having no acting experience. Bilingual Richard Heathcote, 24, earned £26,000 a year as a translator for Foster and Partners, the renowned architecture firm led by Sir Norman Foster. Now, he’s betting on the success of 'Ciao Britain'. He plays Steve, a recent English graduate struggling to find purpose after university—a character he compares to Curly Watts, the hapless but lovable figure from 'Coronation Street'. Filmed in a warehouse in Greenwich, the sitcom follows four Chinese housemates and one Englishman living together in London. Heathcote says his character is the butt of everyone’s jokes—lacking direction and unable to settle into a job he cares about. 'I feel very at home with Chinese humor—it’s different from British or American comedy,' Heathcote said. 'My character is a Chinese-speaking British guy in his 20s whom the others tease relentlessly. He’s unlucky in life, much like Curly Watts.' Heathcote learned of the role through former lecturers at the University of Sheffield, who knew of his fluent Mandarin. He studied Chinese at university and lived in Nanjing, eastern China, for a year in 2007 as part of his degree. After graduating in 2010, he worked as a marketing coordinator for Chinese clients at Foster and Partners. Filming for the first series begins in April, with the pilot set to air on Chinese television in September. If successful, the show could produce at least 30 episodes per season. 'I had a great job, but this was too good an opportunity to pass up—it lets me truly embrace Chinese culture,' Heathcote said. Executive producer Xiaoyi Li explained: 'The idea came from our team’s shared experiences as international residents in London. We wanted to reflect the multicultural reality of modern cities—and bring it to Chinese audiences.' The series will be filmed partly in the UK and partly in China.

article_content: After months of tense negotiations, dockworkers on the U.S. West Coast and the shipping companies they work for have agreed in principle to a new five-year contract. The deal, brokered between the Pacific Maritime Association and the International Longshore and Warehouse Union, still needs approval from union members before it becomes binding. Talks began in May, but when no agreement was reached by July, operations at 29 major ports ground to a halt, creating massive delays across the nation’s supply chain. U.S. Labor Secretary Thomas Perez traveled to San Francisco to help push both sides toward a resolution. He noted that while workers have already returned to their posts, full operational recovery will take time. The Port of Oakland warned that clearing the backlog of idle ships, misplaced containers, and unbalanced chassis could take six to eight weeks. 'Everything’s out of place,' a port spokesperson said. 'Getting things back in order isn’t just about restarting work—it’s about rebuilding the entire logistics flow.'

Avtalen, som ble utforhandlet mellom Pacific Maritime Association og International Longshore and Warehouse Union, må godkjennes av fagforeningsmedlemmene før den blir bindende. Forhandlingene startet i mai, men da ingen enighet ble nådd i juli, stoppet operasjoner ved 29 store havner, noe som skapte massive forsinkelser i hele landets logistikk. Den amerikanske arbeidsministeren Thomas Perez reiste til San Francisco for å hjelpe begge parter mot en løsning. Han bemerket at arbeidere allerede har returnert til sine stillinger, men full gjenoppretting av operasjonene vil ta tid. Havn i Oakland advarte mot at det kan ta seks til åtte uker å rydde opp i bakloggen av stående skip, feilplasserte containere og ubalanserte chassier. 'Alt er ute av posisjon,' sa en havnespråkperson. 'Å få ting tilbake i orden handler ikke bare om å starte opp igjen — det handler om å gjenbygge hele logistikken.'

article_content: Distressed cries from a toddler were heard outside a house. The mother did not know the babysitter’s full name or address. By Helen Collis. Published: 11:01 EST, 21 April 2012 | Updated: 11:12 EST, 21 April 2012. Nicola Lewington, 24, of Mottingham, Bromley, South London, spent the night in custody while her two-year-old daughter, Tiana, was left alone at home. Tiana was discovered the next day by Lewington’s mother, who arrived to collect an Argos delivery. Thea Viney, prosecuting, said: 'She could hear her whimpering and crying inside and went to get her keys. She let herself in and found Tiana, then two years old, standing at the top of the stairs, distressed, with a soiled nappy, calling for her mother.' Lewington pleaded guilty to child neglect, claiming she had left Tiana in the care of a friend named Becky. On August 9, 2011, she put Tiana to bed and went out to buy a takeaway, leaving Becky to watch her. While away, she met friends and drove to Orpington, where she was arrested at 1 a.m. alongside four others after police found items suspected of being stolen during the riots in her vehicle. At Bromley Police Station, Lewington informed officers she had a child being cared for—but could not provide Becky’s full name, phone number, or address. Viney added: 'She left Tiana in the care of Becky and now accepts this was reckless, given how little she knew about the person entrusted with her child’s safety.' Defense lawyer James McCooey said: 'She was not a woman packing her bags and going on holiday. She would have been home if not for her arrest.' He emphasized that this behavior was out of character and that friends described her as a 'very loving mother.' Magistrate Geraldine Mushett sentenced Lewington to an 18-month community order with supervision and mandated participation in a women’s offender intervention program, along with £85 in court costs. Lewington was acquitted of the burglary charges related to her arrest on December 20, 2011.

article_content: Barcelona enter the second leg of their Champions League semifinal against Inter Milan with a daunting two-goal deficit, but possess a deep pool of attacking talent capable of turning the tie around. The biggest concern, however, is defensive: captain Carles Puyol is suspended after receiving a yellow card in last week’s 3-1 defeat at San Siro, forcing manager Pep Guardiola to reconfigure his central defense. With Eric Abidal still recovering from injury, Maxwell is set to start at left-back. Guardiola must now choose between Rafa Márquez and Gabi Milito to partner Gerard Piqué in the heart of the backline. The pair of Piqué and Milito — who previously played together at Real Zaragoza — delivered a commanding performance in Barcelona’s recent El Clásico victory, making them the most likely starting duo. Piqué himself is banking on the overwhelming support at Camp Nou to rattle Inter’s players. 'I hope the crowd makes them regret ever choosing football as a career,' he said on the club’s official website. 'The energy here is unlike anything I’ve experienced — fans are buzzing with belief.' In attack, Guardiola has an embarrassment of riches: Lionel Messi and Pedro Rodríguez have been devastating in recent matches, while Zlatan Ibrahimović, back to full fitness after scoring against Xerez, insists Barcelona must not abandon their attacking identity. 'We’re heading into a war,' he told AFP. 'They’ll try to exploit their strengths, but we lost in Milan not because they were better — we lost because we stopped playing like us.' Also available are veteran striker Thierry Henry, playmaker Bojan Krkić, and young winger Jeffren. On the other side, Inter’s chances are slightly hampered by the absence of midfield engine Wesley Sneijder, who sustained a hamstring strain during their 3-1 win over Atalanta — a result that kept their Serie A title hopes alive. As the stage is set for a dramatic showdown, Barcelona’s path forward depends on whether their offensive brilliance can offset defensive vulnerability — and whether the roar of 99,000 supporters can erase the memory of San Siro.
